# Casama: full text of casama.ai

> Casama is an open-source app for AI teammates that each have their own computer. They remember, work while you're away and ask before anything risky. Self-host it free, or use Casama Cloud.

Each section below is one page of https://casama.ai, in markdown. The index is https://casama.ai/llms.txt. Docs: https://docs.casama.ai/llms-full.txt. Facts about other products carry the date they were checked.

# About Casama

Casama is an open-source app for AI teammates that each have their own computer. They remember, work while you're away and ask before anything risky.

Updated 2026-11-19. Page: https://casama.ai/about

## What Casama is

Casama gives you AI teammates, called bots. Each bot has its own instructions, memory, skills and
a sandboxed Linux computer. It can research, write, code, browse and run tasks on a schedule, and it
asks before doing anything risky. You reach your bots from apps on iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac,
Windows, Linux and the web.

You can run Casama on your own server for free, with any AI model, or use Casama Cloud, which has a
free plan and paid plans from $15 a month.

This Casama is the AI app at casama.ai. It is not related to other companies or products with the
same name.

## Facts at a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| What it is | An open-source app for AI teammates with their own computers |
| Made by | Stackwares |
| Website | casama.ai |
| Licence | AGPL-3.0; SDKs, CLI and plugin kit Apache-2.0 (a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence) |
| Source code | github.com/stackwares/casama |
| Platforms | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web |
| Hosted version | Casama Cloud: Free, Plus $15, Pro $49, Max $99 a month |
| Self-hosted | Free, with no limit on users or bots |
| Models | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted |
| First public release | November 2026 |

## Who makes it

Casama is made by Stackwares, a small software company. This is the founding team.

## Press kit

Writing about Casama? Use these.

**One sentence.** Casama is an open-source app for AI teammates that each have their own computer,
remember how you work and ask before anything risky.

**One paragraph.** Casama gives people AI teammates, called bots, that do real work on computers of
their own: they browse, fill in forms, write files and run code on a sandboxed Linux machine you
can watch and take over. Bots remember what matters, start on schedules and triggers, and stop for
your approval before risky steps such as sending, paying or deleting. Casama is open source under
AGPL-3.0 and free to self-host with any AI model, and it is also offered as Casama Cloud. It has
native apps for iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux and the web.

**Name.** Casama, with a capital C. Not "Casama AI" in running text, and not "Kasama", its name
before November 2026.

**Logo and screenshots.** The mark and screenshots are in the
[repository](https://github.com/stackwares/casama/tree/main/site/assets). The
[trademark page](https://github.com/stackwares/casama/blob/main/TRADEMARKS.md) says how the name and
logo may be used.

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# Agent Zero alternative: how Casama compares

Agent Zero is a free, MIT-licensed agent that works inside a Docker container with its own Linux desktop, terminal and browser. You host it yourself, and every tool is allowed until you block it. Casama is the alternative for people who want the same kind of computer per bot with approvals on from the start, apps in the stores, team workspaces and a hosted option.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/agent-zero

## Casama and Agent Zero at a glance

| | Casama | Agent Zero |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | MIT |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your computer or your own server, in Docker; no hosted version |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | A Docker container with its own Linux desktop, terminal and browser; can also be given access to your computer |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | None by default: every tool is allowed until you block it in an agent profile |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Your own keys, a ChatGPT sign-in, or local models through Ollama or LM Studio |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | A0 Launcher for Windows, Mac and Linux, a web app and a CLI; no phone app |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | Telegram, WhatsApp and email; more through plugins |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Long-term memory you can search and edit, per project |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Scheduled tasks: cron, one-time or by hand |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Not described: one login per instance |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Free; you pay your model provider |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Yes, all of it |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | Not stated; it runs on your machine and sends prompts to the model you choose |

Facts about Agent Zero come from its own README, documentation and website, and were checked on
November 18, 2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

The two are closer than most pairs on this site. Both give the agent a Linux computer of its own
instead of your laptop, both accept local models, and both are open source.

The differences are in the defaults and around the edges. Agent Zero allows every tool unless an
agent profile blocks it, and nothing pauses to ask. Casama sorts every tool by risk and stops before
risky steps until you approve, with payments always asking. Agent Zero is one login per instance;
Casama has workspaces with roles. Agent Zero has a desktop launcher and a web app; Casama also has
iPhone, iPad and Android apps, and a hosted plan if you don't want to run a server.

## Choose Agent Zero if

- You want an agent with a full Linux desktop you can watch, including apps like LibreOffice and Blender.
- You want free software you can read and change, with plugins, MCP and A2A.
- You want to choose any model, including local ones.

## Choose Casama if

- You want risky steps to wait for you from day one, without writing tool rules first.
- You want phone apps from the App Store and Google Play, with notifications when a bot needs you.
- More than one person will use it, with roles and separate workspaces.
- You want a hosted version, or to start hosted and move to your own server later.
- You want spending limits per bot, per run and per day.

## Worth knowing about Agent Zero

- There is no hosted version: you run Docker and bring your own model keys or model server.
- Tools are allowed by default and nothing asks before acting; limits are set in agent profiles.
- No phone apps and no team accounts.

## Moving from Agent Zero to Casama

Recreate each agent profile as a Casama bot with the same instructions, and each scheduled task as a
routine. Self-hosted Casama takes the same kinds of models: provider keys, a ChatGPT plan, or a local
model through Ollama or LM Studio. Files from the agent's workspace can go into the bot's computer or
its Library.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is Agent Zero free?

Yes. The software is free under the MIT licence, and you pay only your model provider.

### Does Agent Zero have a computer of its own like Casama?

Yes. Each instance runs in a Docker container with its own Linux desktop. Casama gives every bot its
own sandboxed computer too, which you can watch live and take over.

### Can Agent Zero ask before risky actions?

Not out of the box. You can block whole tools or single actions in an agent profile, and pause or
stop a run, but its documentation describes no prompt that asks first.

### Does either work on my phone?

Agent Zero is reached from a phone through its web app over a tunnel, or through Telegram, WhatsApp
or email. Casama has native apps in the App Store and Google Play.

## Sources

- Agent Zero (checked 2026-11-18): https://github.com/agent0ai/agent-zero/blob/main/LICENSE, https://github.com/agent0ai/agent-zero/blob/main/README.md, https://github.com/agent0ai/agent-zero/blob/main/plugins/_tool_access/default_config.yaml, https://github.com/agent0ai/agent-zero/blob/main/docs/setup/installation.md, https://github.com/agent0ai/agent-zero/tree/main/plugins, https://github.com/agent0ai/agent-zero/blob/main/docs/guides/memory.md, https://github.com/agent0ai/agent-zero/blob/main/docs/guides/task-scheduler.md, https://www.agent-zero.ai/p/docs/installation/, https://www.agent-zero.ai/p/cookies/

See how Casama compares with [other AI agents](https://casama.ai/alternatives/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# ChatGPT Dots alternative: how Casama compares

Dots are OpenAI's always-on agents inside ChatGPT, each with its own cloud computer. One dot comes with ChatGPT Pro or Business Premium, and Pro subscribers in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK don't get them. Casama is the open-source alternative, with a free plan, no region limits, and as many bots as your plan or server allows.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/chatgpt-agent

## Casama and ChatGPT Dots at a glance

| | Casama | ChatGPT Dots |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Closed |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | OpenAI's cloud |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Each dot has its own cloud computer that you can open |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Built-in rules plus your own; some confirmations can't be removed |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | OpenAI's model; no choice |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | ChatGPT on desktop, web and phone |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | ChatGPT, Slack, Microsoft Teams |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes; a review reports you can't view or delete single memories |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Looks for ways to help when idle; schedules aren't described |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | One dot per Business Premium seat |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | One dot is included with ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | No |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Not for Pro subscribers in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | Not confirmed |

Facts about ChatGPT Dots come from its own public pages and from press, and were checked on November 18,
2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

A dot is one agent tied to your ChatGPT account on OpenAI's most expensive plans. Casama gives you several bots, each with a job and its own computer, on a free plan or your own server. We could not read OpenAI's own pages for this comparison, so its column rests on press coverage; check the sources.

## Choose ChatGPT Dots if

- You already pay for ChatGPT Pro and want an always-on agent inside it.
- You want a very large set of app connections.
- You want cautious background behaviour: unprompted work is read-only.

## Choose Casama if

- You want more than one agent, each with its own role and computer.
- You are in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK.
- You don't want to pay for the top ChatGPT plan to get an agent.
- You want to self-host, or to choose the model.
- You want to read and edit what a bot remembers.

## Worth knowing about ChatGPT Dots

- It is only on the most expensive plans, and not for Pro subscribers in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK.
- Users reported dots stopping for hours at a limit with no meter or reset time.
- Early users described repeated confirmation prompts.

## Moving from ChatGPT Dots to Casama

Recreate your dot as a Casama bot: paste its role into the bot's instructions, reconnect apps, and add routines. If you self-host and have a ChatGPT plan, a Casama bot can sign in with it and use it for chat and tools.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### What happened to ChatGPT agent?

Reports say the older ChatGPT agent mode was replaced by ChatGPT Work for long tasks, with dots as the always-on agent. We could not confirm this on OpenAI's own pages.

### Are ChatGPT dots free?

No. Reports say a dot is included only with Pro and Business Premium.

### Can I use my ChatGPT plan with Casama?

Yes, when you self-host: sign in with your ChatGPT plan instead of a key.

### Is Casama available in Europe?

Yes. Casama has no region limits.

## Sources

- ChatGPT Dots (checked 2026-11-18): https://siliconangle.com/2026/09/29/openai-launches-dots-always-on-ai-agents-in-chatgpt-with-their-own-cloud-computers/, https://thenextweb.com/news/openai-dots-always-on-ai-agents-cloud-computers-devday, https://chatgpt.com/pricing, https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/

See how Casama compares with [other AI agents](https://casama.ai/alternatives/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# Claude Cowork and Duet alternative: how Casama compares

Claude Cowork is Anthropic's agent mode for files and multi-step work, and Duet is its always-on assistant in preview. Both are part of paid Claude plans, use Claude models only, and count against your plan's limits. Casama is the open-source alternative: any model, a computer per bot that you can watch, and free to self-host.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/claude-cowork

## Casama and Claude Cowork and Duet at a glance

| | Casama | Claude Cowork and Duet |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Closed |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Anthropic's cloud; it reaches your computer through the desktop app |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Cowork: cloud sessions you can watch. Duet: its own cloud computer that you can't watch |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Cowork: depends on the mode you pick. Duet: asks before sending, paying, signing or deleting |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Claude models only |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Mac, Windows, Linux (beta), web, iPhone, Android |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | The Claude apps only |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes for Duet |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Scheduled tasks; Duet sends a morning brief |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Cowork on Team and Enterprise plans; Duet not yet |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Included in paid Claude plans and counted against their limits |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | No |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Cowork: paid plans. Duet: United States only, by waitlist |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | On for consumer plans unless you switch it off |

Facts about Claude Cowork and Duet come from its own public pages and from press, and were checked on November 18,
2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

Cowork and Duet are the right choice if you live in Claude already. Casama is a separate, open product: a team of bots with their own computers, memory and routines, reachable from native apps and chat apps, on Casama Cloud or your own server.

## Choose Claude Cowork and Duet if

- You want finished documents made from your own files: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF.
- You already pay for Claude and want agents inside it.
- You want firm approval rules: Duet has a short list of actions it won't do even if you approve.

## Choose Casama if

- You want to choose the model, or mix several.
- You want to watch and take over a bot's computer. Duet's browser can't be watched.
- You are outside the United States, where Duet isn't offered.
- You want a free plan, or to self-host for nothing.
- You want bots reachable in Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp or iMessage.

## Worth knowing about Claude Cowork and Duet

- Duet is US-only and waitlisted, and you can't watch or take over its browser.
- Anthropic advises against scheduling tasks that send, buy or do things that are hard to undo.
- Both draw on your Claude plan's usage limits, and Cowork uses them faster than chat.

## Moving from Claude Cowork and Duet to Casama

Recreate recurring Cowork tasks as Casama routines and move your instructions into a bot. Connect the same apps. If you have an Anthropic API key, a self-hosted Casama bot can run on Claude models.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is Claude Cowork free?

No. Anthropic's pages list it on paid plans only, and Duet isn't on the Free plan.

### Can Casama use Claude models?

Yes. When you self-host, add an Anthropic key and pick a Claude model per bot.

### What is the difference between Cowork and Duet?

Cowork is an agent mode for tasks you start. Duet is an always-on assistant with its own cloud computer, in a US-only preview.

### Does my Claude plan limit apply to Casama?

No. Casama Cloud uses credits, and self-hosted Casama uses your own model key.

## Sources

- Claude Cowork and Duet (checked 2026-11-18): https://claude.com/product/cowork, https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile, https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17631495-get-started-with-claude-duet.md, https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely, https://claude.com/pricing, https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10023580-is-my-data-used-for-model-training

See how Casama compares with [other AI agents](https://casama.ai/alternatives/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# Grok Bot alternative: how Casama compares

Grok Bot is xAI's always-on agent: polished apps on every platform and team Bots in Slack, on paid plans from $30 a month. All of a person's Bots share one cloud computer, and you can't choose the model or host it yourself. Casama is the open-source alternative: a computer per bot, any model when self-hosted, and a free plan.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/grok-bot

## Casama and Grok Bot at a glance

| | Casama | Grok Bot |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Closed |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | xAI's cloud only |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | One cloud computer per person, shared by all of that person's Bots |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | An automatic check decides; you can add up to 20 "ask first" rules |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | No choice, and you aren't shown which model ran |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, Android |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | X, Slack, Microsoft Teams |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Schedules and some events |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Team Bots in Slack; admin controls on Enterprise |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Paid plans at $30, $100 or $200 a month; a weekly usage pool, then billed at token cost |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | No free plan; some accounts get a 7-day trial credit |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open; its computers run in the United States |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | A training opt-out exists |

Facts about Grok Bot come from its own public pages and from press, and were checked on November 18,
2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

Grok Bot is a closed, hosted product from a large lab, sold as part of a subscription with a weekly usage pool. Casama is open source. You can run it on your own server for free with any model, or use Casama Cloud, where credits are dollars and each bot has budgets you set.

*Diagram: Two diagrams side by side. On the left, three bots all feed into one shared computer that holds one set of files and a shared setup, so what one bot does can affect the others. On the right, three bots each have their own computer with their own files and sign-ins, so each bot is walled off from the others, as in Casama.*

Bots on one shared computer share its files and setup. In Casama, each bot works on its own computer.

## Choose Grok Bot if

- You want native apps on every desktop and phone platform from a large vendor.
- You want shared team Bots in Slack and Teams with ready-made roles.
- You want to teach a workflow by recording it once.

## Choose Casama if

- You want to host it yourself, or keep that option open.
- You want each bot on its own computer, not one machine shared by all of them.
- You want to choose the model, or use local models.
- You want a free plan, and spending limits per bot.
- You want to read the code that decides what a bot may do.

## Worth knowing about Grok Bot

- Subscribers reported weekly limits being cut in late October 2026 without warning.
- All of a person's Bots share one computer, files and sign-ins.
- You can't choose or see the model, and you can't host it yourself.

## Moving from Grok Bot to Casama

Grok Bot has no export, so Casama asks your Bot instead: in Casama, choose **Paste a Bot's Setup**, send your Bot the prompt and paste its reply. Its instructions, schedules, skills and "ask first" rules come over as a bot and routines, and you review each one first. Then reconnect its apps. If your team uses Bots in Slack, connect Casama's Slack app and add the bot to the same channels.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is Grok Bot free?

No. Its docs say it is included in paid plans only, with a 7-day trial credit for some accounts. Casama has a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free.

### How much does Grok Bot cost?

Plans are $30, $100 and $200 a month, with usage from a weekly pool and pay-per-use beyond it. The size of the pool isn't published.

### Can I self-host Grok Bot?

No. Its security docs say self-hosting isn't supported. Casama is free to self-host.

### Does Casama work in Slack and Teams?

Yes, along with Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage, Discord and others.

## Sources

- Grok Bot (checked 2026-11-19): https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/security, https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq, https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/approvals-security-and-privacy, https://x.ai/bot

More on Grok Bot: [pricing](https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-pricing), [is it free?](https://casama.ai/compare/is-grok-bot-free), [templates](https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-templates) and [moving to Casama](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/moving-from-grok-bot).

See eight [Grok Bot alternatives](https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-alternatives) side by side, or how Casama compares with [other AI agents](https://casama.ai/alternatives/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# Hark Pro alternative: how Casama compares

Hark Pro is a consumer assistant with a free plan that includes every feature and a clear promise not to train on your data. It runs in Hark's cloud only, with no desktop apps, team plan or choice of model, and its usage caps aren't published. Casama is the open-source alternative for people who want those things.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/hark

## Casama and Hark Pro at a glance

| | Casama | Hark Pro |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Closed |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Hark's cloud only |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Its own cloud browser per person; you can watch it |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | It checks in before actions that need approval; there is no published list |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Hark chooses; no choice |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Web, iPhone, iPad, Android |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | Its own app only |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes; not in the EEA, the UK or Switzerland |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Scheduled tasks |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | None found |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Free; $20 or $100 a month for more usage |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Yes, with every feature; the cap isn't published |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open sign-up |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | Says it doesn't train on your data |

Facts about Hark Pro come from its own public pages and from press, and were checked on November 18,
2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

Hark is a polished phone-first assistant for everyday errands. Casama is a team of bots for work and life, with a full Linux computer for each, desktop apps, group chats with other people, and published limits.

## Choose Hark Pro if

- You want a free plan that includes every feature.
- You want everyday errands on websites done from a cloud browser you can watch.
- You want a clear default of no training on your content.

## Choose Casama if

- You want published limits: credits in dollars and a budget per bot.
- You want desktop apps for Mac, Windows and Linux.
- You want to share bots with a team.
- You want a full computer for each bot (shell, files, browser), not only a browser.
- You want to self-host, or to choose the model.

## Worth knowing about Hark Pro

- Usage caps aren't published, and reviewers call them hard to predict.
- There are no desktop apps, no team plan, and no calls or texts.
- Memory is unavailable in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland.

## Moving from Hark Pro to Casama

In Casama, choose **Paste a Bot's Setup** and pick Hark Pro. Send Hark the prompt and paste its reply: what it does for you, its scheduled tasks and what it remembers come over as a bot, routines and memories, and you review each one first. Then connect the same accounts (mail, calendar, Slack).

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is Hark free?

Yes. Its pricing page lists a free plan with every feature; paid plans at $20 and $100 a month raise usage.

### Does Hark train on my data?

Its pages say it doesn't train AI models on your account data. Casama doesn't either.

### Does Hark have a desktop app?

None is listed. Casama has apps for Mac, Windows and Linux.

### Is memory available in Europe?

Hark's pages say memory is off in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland. Casama's memory works everywhere.

## Sources

- Hark Pro (checked 2026-11-18): https://hark.com, https://hark.com/using-hark, https://hark.com/security, https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hark-pro/id6772362941, https://hark.com/privacy-policy, https://hark.com/pricing

See how Casama compares with [other AI agents](https://casama.ai/alternatives/).

# Hermes Agent alternative: how Casama compares

Hermes Agent, from Nous Research, is an open-source agent that improves itself: it writes its own skills and keeps searchable memory. It runs from a terminal or desktop app on your machine and has no phone app yet. Casama is the alternative for people who want a team of bots with their own computers, real phone apps and approvals beyond shell commands.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/hermes-agent

## Casama and Hermes Agent at a glance

| | Casama | Hermes Agent |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | MIT |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your own computer or server; a hosted agent comes with paid Nous Portal plans |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Your machine by default; Docker, SSH or cloud sandboxes are optional |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | For shell commands that match risky patterns |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Your own keys, Nous Portal, some subscriptions, or local models |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Mac and Windows desktop apps and a terminal app; no phone app yet |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | More than 20, including Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Teams and iMessage |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes, and it writes and improves its own skills |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Schedules set up in plain language |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Limited; separate user accounts aren't described |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Free; optional Nous Portal at $0, $20, $100 or $200 a month |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Yes |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | With your own keys only your provider sees your data; Nous Portal may train on prompts unless Privacy Mode is on |

Facts about Hermes Agent come from its own public pages and from press, and were checked on November 18,
2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

Hermes Agent is built around one agent that gets better the longer you use it, with a wide choice of models and of places for its commands to run. Casama is built around several bots that each hold a job, each on its own sandboxed computer, with apps on phone and desktop and rules for what every kind of action must ask before doing.

## Choose Hermes Agent if

- You want one agent that teaches itself: it writes and refines its own skills and keeps searchable memory.
- You want wide model choice, including local models and several subscription sign-ins.
- You want to choose where commands run: locally, in Docker, over SSH or in a cloud sandbox.

## Choose Casama if

- You want native iPhone and Android apps with push notifications today.
- You want approvals for every kind of risky action (sending, paying, publishing), not only shell commands.
- You want each bot on its own managed computer you can watch and take over.
- Several people will share it, with accounts and roles.
- You want a hosted plan where your data isn't used for training.

## Worth knowing about Hermes Agent

- Commands run on your own machine by default, and its docs say the deny rules are pattern matching that scripts can get around.
- There is no phone app yet.
- It is still before version 1.0, with a very large backlog of open issues.

## Moving from Hermes Agent to Casama

Recreate each Hermes setup as a Casama bot: paste its instructions, add the same model key, and turn its scheduled jobs into routines. Skills are plain instructions in both, so the useful ones can be copied across as Casama skills.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is Hermes Agent free?

The agent is free and MIT-licensed. The optional Nous Portal has plans at $0, $20, $100 and $200 a month. Self-hosted Casama is free too.

### Hermes Agent or OpenClaw?

See our [OpenClaw vs Hermes Agent comparison](https://casama.ai/compare/openclaw-vs-hermes-agent).

### Does Hermes Agent have a mobile app?

Not yet; its pages describe one as coming. Casama has apps for iPhone, iPad and Android.

### Can both use local models?

Yes, through Ollama and similar servers.

## Sources

- Hermes Agent (checked 2026-11-18): https://api.github.com/repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent, https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com, https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent, https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/security, https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers, https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/compare, https://portal.nousresearch.com/privacy

See how Casama compares with [other AI agents](https://casama.ai/alternatives/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# Instinct alternative: how Casama compares

Instinct is an invite-only personal assistant you text or call. It publishes no prices, and its terms say it may train on your content unless you opt out. Casama is the alternative you can sign up for today: open source, with documented approvals, no training on your data, and a server of your own if you want one.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/instinct

## Casama and Instinct at a glance

| | Casama | Instinct |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Closed |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Instinct's cloud; you text or call it |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Reviews describe its own cloud computer; the vendor's pages don't say |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Not documented; its terms don't promise any |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Not stated |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | None needed; there is a web workspace for settings |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | Text message and phone call |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Implied, with no controls described |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Reviews say it texts or calls you first |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | None published |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Not published; reported free during the beta |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Reported free while invite-only |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Invite or waitlist only |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | On by default; you can opt out |

Facts about Instinct come from its own public pages and from press, and were checked on November 18,
2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

Instinct's appeal is that there is nothing to learn: you message it like a person. Its maker publishes very little about how it works, so much of its column comes from reviews. Casama publishes everything, down to the code that decides when a bot must ask.

## Choose Instinct if

- You want nothing to install: you text or call it like a person.
- You want everyday errands done for one person, such as groceries and tickets.
- You want an assistant that follows up without being asked.

## Choose Casama if

- You don't have an invite.
- You want written rules for what the assistant must ask before doing.
- You don't want your content used for training by default.
- You want to know the price.
- You want it on your own server.

## Worth knowing about Instinct

- Its terms bind you to agreements it makes for you and cap its liability at $100 or six months of fees.
- Training on your data is on by default.
- Early testers reported an email sent without permission and a successful phishing test.

## Moving from Instinct to Casama

Instinct has no export that we could find, so Casama asks Instinct instead: in Casama, choose **Paste a Bot's Setup**, text Instinct the prompt, and paste its reply. Its instructions, regular check-ins and what it knows about you come over, and you review each one first. Then connect your mail and calendar.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### How do I get access to Instinct?

Its site offers a waitlist and invites from existing users. Casama is open to everyone.

### How much does Instinct cost?

No prices are published. Press reports it has been free during the invite-only beta.

### Can I text a Casama bot?

Yes: SMS, iMessage, WhatsApp, Telegram and other chat apps can be connected to a bot, and bots can take live calls in the app.

### Is Instinct open source?

No.

- Instinct (checked 2026-11-18): https://www.instinct.com/terms, https://builtin.com/articles/instinct-ai, https://instinct.com, https://www.eesel.ai/blog/instinct-ai-review, https://instinct.com/privacy-policy

# Lindy alternative: how Casama compares

Lindy is a hosted AI assistant that your team shares in Slack, by text and in Gmail, with routines that start on emails, messages and meetings. It is paid per seat after a seven-day credit trial. Casama is the open-source alternative: a free plan that doesn't run out after a week, a computer of its own for every bot, apps on every platform, and the option to run it all on your own server.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/lindy

## Casama and Lindy at a glance

| | Casama | Lindy |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Hosted service; no source code offered |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Lindy's cloud only |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Can drive a browser for tools without an integration, on higher plans |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Actions with outside impact wait for your OK |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Lindy picks per task; you can choose per task |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Web app and a Chrome extension for Gmail |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | Slack, iMessage and SMS, email; Teams coming |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Files you can view, edit and restore, personal and team |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Schedules, plus email, Slack, calendar and meeting events |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Per-seat plans with shared credits and team memory; SSO on Enterprise |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | From $29.99 a month per seat for 3,000 credits; Enterprise custom |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | $50 of credits for 7 days |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | No, says Lindy |

Facts about Lindy come from its own website, pricing page, documentation and security page, and were
checked on November 18, 2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

Lindy is built around work chat. You @mention it in Slack channels, text it, or use it in Gmail, and
it acts across your connected tools, waiting for your OK before anything with outside impact. It is
a hosted service only.

Casama is built around bots with their own computers. Each bot has a sandboxed Linux machine with a
shell, files and a browser, so it can install software, write code, build files and browse, not only
call integrations. Approvals work in a similar spirit. The big differences are ownership and price:
Casama is open source, can run on your own server with any model, and has a free hosted plan with no
end date.

## Choose Lindy if

- You want one assistant your whole team shares in Slack, called with an @mention.
- You want routines that start on emails, Slack messages, calendar events or meetings ending.
- You want to see and edit what the assistant remembers, with version history.

## Choose Casama if

- You want to self-host, keep your data on your own server, or use your own model keys or local models.
- You want a free plan that doesn't expire after seven days.
- You want each bot to have a real computer for code, files and browsing.
- You want native apps on iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows and Linux.
- You use Microsoft Teams, which Casama supports today.

## Worth knowing about Lindy

- The free plan is $50 of credits that expire after 7 days; after that you pay per seat.
- Microsoft Teams isn't supported yet.
- Hosted only, and the privacy notice doesn't say which region holds your data.

## Moving from Lindy to Casama

Recreate each routine as a Casama routine with the same schedule or trigger, and give a bot the
instructions your Lindy follows. Connect the same apps (Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack and others) in
Connections. Paste anything important from Lindy's memory files into the bot's memories.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is Lindy open source?

No. Lindy is a hosted service and offers no source code or self-hosting. Casama is open source under
AGPL-3.0.

### Is Lindy free?

Its free plan is $50 of credits that last seven days. After that, plans start at $29.99 a month per
seat.

### Does Lindy train on my data?

Lindy says neither it nor its providers use your data to train AI models.

### Can Casama work in Slack like Lindy?

Yes. Casama bots can join Slack, as well as Teams, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp and iMessage.

## Sources

- Lindy (checked 2026-11-18): https://www.lindy.ai/pricing, https://www.lindy.ai/privacy, https://www.lindy.ai/, https://docs.lindy.ai/pricing.md, https://docs.lindy.ai/features/imessage-sms.md, https://docs.lindy.ai/teammate/memory.md, https://docs.lindy.ai/teammate/routines.md, https://docs.lindy.ai/start-here/quickstart.md, https://www.lindy.ai/security

See how Casama compares with [other AI agents](https://casama.ai/alternatives/).

# Manus alternative: how Casama compares

Manus is a hosted agent with its own cloud computer that produces finished work such as slide decks, websites and research. It is closed, cloud-only and priced in credits that depend on how complex each task turns out to be. Casama is the open-source alternative: self-host it free with any model, or use a hosted plan where credits are dollars.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/manus

## Casama and Manus at a glance

| | Casama | Manus |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Closed |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Manus's cloud; a desktop app can run commands on your computer |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | A cloud sandbox with a browser, per person |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | None described in the cloud; three modes on your own computer |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Manus picks; no choice on standard plans |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Web, iPhone, iPad, Mac (Apple silicon), Windows |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | Slack and email |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Projects keep instructions and files; no separate memory is described |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Schedules and events: 2 on Free, 20 on Pro |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Yes: shared credits, single sign-on, audit logs |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Credits: Free; Pro from $20 a month for 4,000 credits, up to $200; Team from $20 a seat |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Yes: 300 credits a day |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open; sales were paused in some regions in August 2026 |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | Team plans say no; individual plans are unclear |

Facts about Manus come from its own public pages and from press, and were checked on November 18,
2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

Manus is strongest when you hand it one big task and want a finished deliverable back. Casama is built for bots that stay: each has a role, a memory, routines and its own computer, and stops for your approval before sending, paying or deleting.

## Choose Manus if

- You want nothing to set up: a hosted agent with its own cloud computer on web, phone and desktop.
- You want finished deliverables such as slide decks, websites and wide research.
- You want team administration on a hosted product.

## Choose Casama if

- You want to run it on your own server, with your own model keys or local models.
- You want risky steps to wait for approval in the cloud too.
- You want costs in dollars with a budget per bot, per run and per day.
- You want standing teammates with memory and check-ins, not only one-off tasks.
- You want a native Linux app alongside the rest.

## Worth knowing about Manus

- It is closed and cloud-only, and you don't choose the model on standard plans.
- Credit use depends on how complex a task turns out to be, and Trustpilot reviewers complain about credits lost to errors.
- In August 2026 it deleted data and paused sales for users in regions it didn't name.

## Moving from Manus to Casama

There is no import. Recreate your recurring Manus automations as Casama routines, and move project instructions into a bot's instructions or a skill. Files a bot makes land in Casama's Library.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is there an open-source Manus alternative?

Yes. Casama is open source under AGPL-3.0 and free to self-host. OpenClaw and Hermes Agent are open source too, and run on your own machine.

### How much does Manus cost?

Its help pages list a free plan with 300 credits a day and Pro from $20 a month for 4,000 credits, up to $200. Tasks spend credits according to their complexity.

### Does Manus ask before acting?

In the cloud, no approval step is described; it asks you to take over for sign-ins. Its desktop app has approval modes for actions on your own computer.

### Can Casama make slide decks and documents?

Bots have office tools on their computers and can produce documents and PDFs. Manus's built-in deliverable tools are more polished.

# MausBot alternative: how Casama compares

MausBot, also called OpenMausBot, is a free desktop app that runs a team of bots on your own computer using the AI tools you're already signed in to. Its own site says approvals aren't guaranteed to pause every action. Casama is the alternative with a sandboxed computer for every bot, approvals built into every tool, and phone apps in the stores.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/mausbot

## Casama and MausBot at a glance

| | Casama | MausBot |
|---|---|---|

| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your desktop, your own server, or MausBot Cloud |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Your machine by default; a cloud computer per bot on paid Cloud plans |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Allow and Deny cards; the vendor says not every action is guaranteed to pause |

Facts about MausBot come from its own public pages and from press, and were checked on November 18,
2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

MausBot is a local-first app that drives other agent tools such as Claude Code and Codex with your existing subscriptions. Casama runs its own agent on an isolated computer per bot, on your server or in the cloud, so bots keep working when your laptop is closed.

## Choose MausBot if

- You already pay for Claude Code, Codex or Grok and want to reuse those sign-ins with no markup.
- You want a free desktop app that runs bots on your own computer.
- You want many cloud computer hours for the price.

## Choose Casama if

- You want bots that keep working when your computer is off, on a free plan or your own server.
- You want approvals that apply to every tool, with payments always asking.
- You want phone apps from the App Store and Google Play.
- You want chat apps beyond Slack: Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage, Teams, Discord.
- You want each bot on its own computer by default.

## Worth knowing about MausBot

- The vendor itself says approvals aren't guaranteed to pause every action.
- Slack is the only chat app, and only on paid plans.
- Free bots stop when your computer is off, and the phone apps aren't in the stores.

## Moving from MausBot to Casama

Recreate each bot in Casama with the same instructions, and its schedules as routines. If you rely on a Claude or Codex subscription, note that self-hosted Casama can sign in with a ChatGPT plan; other models need a key.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is MausBot the same as OpenMausBot?

Yes. MausBot is the product and OpenMausBot is the repository's name.

### Is MausBot free?

The desktop app is free. MausBot Cloud costs $15, $49 or $99 a month, and model usage is never included.

### Can Casama reuse my Claude Code subscription?

No. Self-hosted Casama accepts API keys, local models and a ChatGPT plan.

### Which has more cloud computer hours?

MausBot's paid Cloud plans list more hours. Casama's plans include model credits and a free tier.

## Choose Meta Muse if

- You want a generous free plan for a full cloud-computer agent.
- You want to message your agent inside WhatsApp.
- You want a documented safety design with a separate guard that approves outbound actions.

- You are outside the United States.
- You don't want your interactions used for training by default.

Not at launch. Casama has no region limits.

### Does Meta Muse train on my data?

Meta's pages say interactions can be used for training by default, and that you can turn it off in settings. Casama doesn't use your data to train models.

### Can I message a Casama bot on WhatsApp?

Yes.

# n8n alternative: how Casama compares

n8n and Casama solve different problems. In n8n you design a workflow yourself, step by step, and it runs the same way every time. In Casama you describe the job in plain words and a bot works out the steps on a computer of its own. Pick n8n when you need an exact, repeatable process. Pick Casama when the work is too varied to draw as a diagram.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/n8n

## Casama and n8n at a glance

| | Casama | n8n |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Sustainable Use License: source-available, not open source; for internal, personal or non-commercial use |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your own server, or n8n Cloud |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | No computer per agent; agents share one code sandbox, and shell commands are self-hosted only |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Approve or reject on an agent's tool calls |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Many providers with your own keys, or local models through Ollama |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | A web editor; no desktop app |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | Slack, Telegram, Teams and Linear for agents; hundreds of apps as workflow steps |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes, across sessions for agents |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Schedules and app triggers |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Users and roles; single sign-on on Enterprise or self-hosted Business |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Self-hosted Community: free. Cloud: €20 or €50 a month by executions; Business €667 |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | A self-hosted free edition; Cloud has a trial only |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | Says assistant data isn't used to train AI providers' models |

Facts about n8n come from its own public pages and were checked on November 18, 2026. The sources
are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

**n8n is a workflow builder.** You connect steps on a canvas: when this happens, do that, then
that. It has hundreds of ready-made app connections, and each run follows the path you drew. It
has added agents you can chat with, still marked as a preview.

**Casama is a team of bots.** You don't draw anything. You tell a bot what you want, and it uses
its own sandboxed Linux computer (a browser, files, a shell) and your connected apps to get there.
It remembers how you like things done, runs on schedules and triggers, and stops for your approval
before risky steps.

A simple way to choose: if you can write the task as a flowchart, n8n will run it reliably and
cheaply. If the task needs judgement, a web browser, or changes each time, a bot fits better.

## Choose n8n if

- You want to build exact, repeatable workflows step by step in a visual editor.
- You need hundreds of ready-made app connections.
- You have someone technical who wants full control of each step.

## Choose Casama if

- You'd rather describe the outcome than build the steps.
- The task needs a real computer: browsing sites with no API, filling in forms, handling files.
- You want software under an open-source licence. Casama is AGPL-3.0, an OSI-approved open-source licence.
- You want native apps on phone and desktop, with approvals as push notifications.
- You want a free hosted plan.

## Use both

They work well together. Casama bots can call any HTTP API or webhook, so a bot can start an n8n
workflow when a task reaches a step that should always run the same way. And an n8n workflow can
hand a messy step to a Casama bot by posting to a routine's webhook, or through Casama's API.

## Worth knowing about n8n

- Its licence isn't open source: it limits use to internal, personal or non-commercial purposes.
- Agents don't get a computer of their own with a browser and files.
- Cloud plans are priced by executions, and there is no free Cloud plan.

## Moving from n8n to Casama

Don't move the workflows that work. Move the ones you keep patching because the inputs vary:
describe each as a routine for a bot ("every weekday at 8, read the support inbox and draft
replies from the help docs"), connect the same apps, and keep approvals on while you compare the
results.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is n8n open source?

Not in the usual sense. Its code is public under the Sustainable Use License, which limits use to
internal, personal or non-commercial purposes. Casama is open source under AGPL-3.0.

### Is n8n free?

The self-hosted Community edition is free. n8n Cloud has a trial and paid plans from €20 a month,
priced by executions. Casama has a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free.

### Can n8n agents use a computer?

n8n's pages describe a shared code sandbox for agents and shell commands on self-hosted servers
only. A Casama bot has its own computer with a browser, files and a shell.

### Which is better for AI agents?

For a fixed process with an AI step in it, n8n. For an assistant you talk to that carries out
varied tasks by itself, Casama.

## Sources

- n8n (checked 2026-11-18): https://docs.n8n.io/n8n-community-license/community-license.md, https://docs.n8n.io/choose-n8n/, https://docs.n8n.io/build/build-and-manage-agents.md, https://docs.n8n.io/build/integrate-ai/ai-examples/human-in-the-loop-for-tools.md, https://docs.n8n.io/llms.txt, https://community.n8n.io/t/sunsetting-self-hosted-team-plan-desktop-version/25830, https://docs.n8n.io/build/integrate-ai/understand-ai-components/how-memory-works.md, https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.scheduletrigger.md, https://n8n.io/pricing/, https://docs.n8n.io/privacy-and-security/privacy.md

See how Casama compares with [other AI agents](https://casama.ai/alternatives/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# nanobot alternative: how Casama compares

nanobot, from the University of Hong Kong's Data Intelligence Lab, is a lightweight, MIT-licensed personal agent in Python. It began as a much smaller take on OpenClaw, runs on the machine you install it on, and reaches more chat apps than almost anything else, including WeChat and Feishu. Casama is the alternative for people who want each bot on its own sandboxed computer, approvals on from the start, native apps and a hosted option.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/nanobot

## Casama and nanobot at a glance

| | Casama | nanobot |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | MIT |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your own machine or server, as a Python app or in Docker |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | The machine it's installed on; an optional shell sandbox |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | No ask-before-acting step; workspace limits and the sandbox are off by default in the config |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Your own keys, Codex, Copilot or Grok sign-in, or local models; fallbacks supported |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | A web app (works on phones), a terminal UI and a CLI |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, WeChat, Feishu, Signal, Matrix, email and more |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Layered files, tidied on a schedule and tracked in git |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Time, interval or cron schedules, command triggers and long-running goals |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | No team accounts; separate people need separate instances |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Free; you pay your model provider |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Yes, all of it |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | Not stated |

Facts about nanobot come from its README, documentation and website, and were checked on November 18,
2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

nanobot is a small program you run on your own machine. Its file and shell tools work in a folder you
choose, with an optional sandbox, and in its config both the workspace limit and the sandbox start
off. Casama puts each bot on its own isolated Linux computer, so a mistake stays on that machine, and
risky tools wait for your approval.

nanobot is strongest on reach and simplicity: sixteen chat apps, any model with fallbacks, and code
small enough to read. Casama is broader around the agent: apps on every platform, team workspaces
with roles, budgets, a Library for everything bots make, and Casama Cloud if you don't want to run
anything.

## Choose nanobot if

- You want an agent in many chat apps, including WeChat, Feishu, QQ and DingTalk.
- You want any model, including local ones, with fallbacks.
- You want a small Python codebase you can read, extend or embed.

## Choose Casama if

- You want each bot on its own computer instead of the machine you installed it on.
- You want risky steps to wait for you without configuring a sandbox first.
- You want native apps on phones and desktops, with notifications.
- More than one person will use it, each with their own workspace and memory.
- You want a hosted version as well as self-hosting.

## Worth knowing about nanobot

- There is no hosted version: you install it, bring a model and keep it running for chat apps and schedules.
- The workspace limit and shell sandbox are off by default, and plugins run with full permissions.
- One instance has one memory and one admin, so keeping people apart takes separate instances.

## Moving from nanobot to Casama

Recreate your agent as a Casama bot and copy what matters from its memory files into the bot's
instructions and memories. Scheduled automations become routines. Self-hosted Casama accepts the
same model choices: provider keys, a ChatGPT plan or a local model. Casama connects to Feishu but
not to WeChat, QQ or DingTalk, so keep nanobot for those.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is nanobot related to OpenClaw?

It started as an assistant inspired by Clawdbot, OpenClaw's earlier name, written to be far smaller,
and its bundled skills still follow OpenClaw's skill format.

### Is nanobot free?

Yes. It is free under the MIT licence; you pay your model provider or run a local model.

### Who makes nanobot?

HKUDS, the Data Intelligence Lab at the University of Hong Kong, with outside contributors.

### Can several people share one nanobot?

They can chat with it through allowed chat apps, but they share one memory and one admin. Its docs
suggest separate instances for separate people.

## Sources

# NanoClaw alternative: how Casama compares

NanoClaw is a small, MIT-licensed personal agent built as a lighter alternative to OpenClaw. Every session runs in its own Docker container, and you reach it through chat apps such as WhatsApp, Telegram and Signal. There are no settings screens; you change it by changing its code. Casama is the alternative for people who want a sandboxed computer per bot plus native apps, approvals on every risky tool and a hosted option.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/nanoclaw

## Casama and NanoClaw at a glance

| | Casama | NanoClaw |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | MIT |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your own machine with Docker (macOS, Linux, Windows via WSL2); a hosted version is invite-only |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Each session in its own Docker container that sees only the folders you mount |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Asks an admin before installing packages, adding MCP servers or admitting new senders; shell commands in the container don't ask |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Claude by default (key or subscription); Codex, Cursor and OpenCode as options |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | None: chat apps and a terminal |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Teams, iMessage, Signal, Matrix and more, each added with a skill |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Markdown files per agent group |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | One-time or cron tasks |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Owner and admin roles and agent teams; built for one person |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Free; you pay your model provider |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Yes, all of it |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone; needs a terminal, git and Docker |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | Not stated; self-hosted data stays on your machine |

Facts about NanoClaw come from its own website, README and documentation, and were checked on
November 18, 2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

Both take isolation seriously. NanoClaw runs each session in an unprivileged container that only sees
the folders you mount, and keeps API keys out of it. Casama gives each bot its own sandboxed Linux
computer with a shell, files and a browser you can watch live.

They part ways on how you use and shape them. NanoClaw is built for one person who is comfortable in
a terminal: you install it with git and Docker, add chat apps with Claude Code skills, and customize
it by editing code. Casama has apps on every platform and settings for bots, routines, approvals and
budgets, so nobody has to touch code. NanoClaw asks an admin before installing packages or adding MCP
servers; Casama asks before any risky tool and always before a payment.

## Choose NanoClaw if

- You want each agent sandboxed in its own container, with API keys kept out of it.
- You want to message your agent from many chat apps, including WhatsApp, Signal and iMessage.
- You want a small codebase you can read in an afternoon and change with a coding agent.

## Choose Casama if

- You want apps for iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows and Linux, not only chat apps.
- You'd rather change bots in settings than in code.
- You want approvals on every risky tool, not only on installs and new tools.
- You want models other than Claude without extra setup, including local models.
- You want a hosted plan you can use today, or a team with roles.

## Worth knowing about NanoClaw

- It needs Docker and comfort with a terminal; there is no desktop or phone app.
- There are no settings screens: you customize it by changing code, and adding chat apps needs Claude Code.
- Containers have open internet access by default, and asking before each credential use is opt-in.

## Moving from NanoClaw to Casama

Recreate each agent group as a Casama bot and paste in the contents of its memory files as
instructions or memories. Scheduled tasks become routines. Casama connects to WhatsApp, Telegram,
Slack, Discord, Teams and iMessage too, so the chats you use can stay the same.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is NanoClaw a fork of OpenClaw?

No. Its creator wrote it as a smaller alternative to OpenClaw, using operating-system containers
for isolation instead of permission checks inside the app.

### Is NanoClaw free?

Yes. It is free and open source under the MIT licence. You pay for the model, usually Claude.

### Does NanoClaw need Claude?

Claude is the default. Codex, Cursor and OpenCode are optional providers, and its docs call the
local Ollama route a legacy workflow.

### Which is easier to set up?

NanoClaw needs git, Docker and a terminal. Casama needs Docker for a server, and its Mac and Linux
app can set that up for you, or you can skip the server and use Casama Cloud.

# OpenClaw alternative: how Casama compares

OpenClaw is the most popular open-source personal agent: free, MIT-licensed, and on about 29 chat apps. It runs on your own machine with its sandbox and approval prompts off until you turn them on. Casama is the alternative for people who want each bot on its own locked-down computer, approvals on from the start, and a hosted option.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/alternatives/openclaw

## Casama and OpenClaw at a glance

| | Casama | OpenClaw |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | MIT |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your own computer or server only; there is no hosted version |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Runs on your machine; a sandbox is optional and off by default |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Optional, and off by default |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Your own keys, a ChatGPT or Claude plan, or local models |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, Android; no hosted web app |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | About 29, including WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, iMessage and Teams |

| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Yes, entirely |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | There is no OpenClaw cloud; your model provider's policy applies |

Facts about OpenClaw come from its own public pages and from press, and were checked on November 18,
2026. The sources are at the end of this page.

## How they differ

The two projects start from opposite ends. OpenClaw is one powerful agent on your own computer that you reach from the chat apps you already use, and it trusts you to switch on the safety features you want. Casama is a team of bots, each on its own isolated Linux machine, with approvals on by default, native apps, workspaces for more than one person, and Casama Cloud if you'd rather not run a server.

## Choose OpenClaw if

- You want the most chat apps: about 29 channels, plus apps on every desktop and phone platform.
- You want software with no paid tier at all, run by a nonprofit.
- You want the largest community: about 395,000 GitHub stars.

## Choose Casama if

- You want each bot kept apart from your own files, on its own sandboxed computer, without setting that up.
- You want risky steps to wait for you from day one, with a checkpoint saved before destructive commands.
- More than one person will use it, with roles and separate workspaces.
- You'd like a hosted version, or to start hosted and move to your own server later.
- You want to watch a bot's screen live and take over.

## Worth knowing about OpenClaw

- Tools run on your own machine, and both the sandbox and approval prompts are off until you turn them on.
- The Register reported three high-impact security advisories in three days in February 2026, and malicious skills on its skill registry.
- It isn't designed for people who don't trust each other to share one agent.

## Moving from OpenClaw to Casama

Casama imports an OpenClaw folder directly: its persona, memories, skills and scheduled jobs come over, and you review each one first. Chat apps reconnect per bot. Casama's gallery has ready-made skills and starter bots to fill gaps.

Start on [Casama Cloud's free plan](https://app.casama.ai), or
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

## Questions

### Is OpenClaw free?

Yes. OpenClaw's site says there is no subscription or paid edition. You pay your own model provider. Self-hosted Casama is also free.

### Is OpenClaw safe?

It can be set up safely, but its own docs say tools run on the host by default, with sandboxing and command approvals off until you turn them on. Casama starts with both on. See [is OpenClaw safe and free](https://casama.ai/learn/is-openclaw-safe) for how to set it up more safely.

### Does Casama have as many chat apps?

No. OpenClaw lists about 29. Casama has ten, including Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, iMessage, Teams and Discord.

### Can I use local models with both?

Yes. Both accept your own keys and local models. On Casama Cloud, Casama picks the model.
