# Casama vs Rakazo: which should you choose?

These two are close. Both are open source, both give every bot its own computer, and both can be self-hosted or hosted at $15, $49 or $99 a month. Pick Rakazo if you want hosted model usage at the provider's price or a wide choice of sandbox providers. Pick Casama if you want a free hosted plan, more chat apps, or workspace roles.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/compare/casama-vs-rakazo

## The short answer

- **Rakazo** runs on your own server, as a desktop app, or on its cloud. Its hosted plans let you
  bring your own keys or a ChatGPT plan, or buy credits at the provider's price.
- **Casama** runs on your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or on Casama Cloud. Its hosted plans
  include dollar credits, and there is a free one that doesn't end.
- The choice is about details, so the table matters more than this summary. We make Casama, so
  weigh our view accordingly.

## Side by side

| | Casama | Rakazo |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Apache-2.0 |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your own server, a desktop app, or Rakazo's cloud |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Each bot has its own container or cloud computer |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Yes: an Ask mode, or an Auto mode where a model decides when to ask |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Your own keys, a ChatGPT plan, local models, or Rakazo credits at the provider's price |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, Android |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | Slack and Teams; iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram only when self-hosted |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes, per bot, and bots can share what they learn |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Schedules, email, webhooks, GitHub events, watched changes |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Organizations, spaces and group chats; roles for people aren't described |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: $15, $49 or $99 a month, or credits from $20 |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Self-hosting is free; hosted plans have a 7-day trial |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | Not stated either way |

Facts about Rakazo were checked on November 18, 2026. Both projects are young and change often.

## Where Rakazo wins

- You want hosted model usage at the provider's price with no markup.
- You want a wide choice of sandbox providers for bot computers when self-hosting.
- You want every way to run it (self-hosted, desktop, hosted) from one project.

Model choice on the hosted version is the clearest difference. On Rakazo's cloud you can use your
own keys or a ChatGPT plan. On Casama Cloud, Casama picks the model.

## Where Casama wins

- **A free hosted plan.** Casama Cloud's Free plan has $1 of credits a month, 3 bots and one cloud
  computer with 5 hours. Rakazo's hosted plans have a 7-day trial.
- **Chat apps.** Casama lists ten: Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu,
  iMessage, Microsoft Teams and Discord. Rakazo lists Slack and Teams, with iMessage, WhatsApp and
  Telegram only when self-hosted.
- **Roles for people.** Casama workspaces have owner, admin and member roles, and extra seats on
  paid plans. Rakazo has organizations, spaces and group chats, and its pages don't describe roles.
- **Approval rules you write.** Casama lets you set rules per kind of action, such as "send email
  to my own company without asking". Payments always ask. A checkpoint is saved before a command
  that deletes data.
- **A stated position on training.** Casama says your data is not used to train models. Rakazo's
  privacy page doesn't say either way.

## Where Casama is weaker

- It is newer still: first released in November 2026. Rakazo's repository dates from August 2026
  and has about 9,000 GitHub stars.
- No model choice on the hosted version, as above.
- Hosted model usage comes out of the credits in your plan. Rakazo sells credits at the provider's
  price with no markup.
- A wide choice of sandbox providers for self-hosting is something Rakazo leads with. Casama's
  default is Docker.

## Three questions to decide

1. **Do you want to choose the model on a hosted plan?** If yes, Rakazo. If you would rather not
   think about models, Casama Cloud picks for you, and self-hosted Casama takes any provider.
2. **Do you want to start hosted for free?** Casama has a free plan. Rakazo has a trial.
3. **Which chat apps do you need without running a server?** If Slack or Teams is enough, either
   works. If you want Telegram or WhatsApp, compare what each offers on the version you plan to
   use.

## What moving costs

Less than between most products, because the ideas map one to one: bots, instructions, memory,
routines and a computer per bot.

**From Rakazo to Casama.** Recreate each bot, paste its instructions, and re-add its routines and
app connections. On a self-hosted server, add your model key again. Files on a bot's computer need
copying across.

**From Casama to Rakazo.** The same steps in reverse. Your Casama workspace exports in full. If you
used workspace roles or action rules, check what Rakazo offers in their place before you move a
team.

Self-hosting either one is free, so you can run both for a week on the same job.

## Questions

### Are both open source?

Yes. Rakazo is Apache-2.0 and Casama is AGPL-3.0, with its SDKs under Apache-2.0. Casama keeps enterprise features in a separate `ee/` folder with its own
licence.

### Which is cheaper?

Self-hosted, both are free. Hosted, the plan prices match at $15, $49 and $99 a month. Casama adds
a free plan and includes credits. Rakazo adds credits from $20 at the provider's price.

### Which has more computer time?

Rakazo's entry hosted plan has 25 computer hours a month. Casama's Plus plan has 30, and its Free
plan has 5.

### Do both have phone apps?

Yes. Both list iPhone, iPad and Android apps, along with desktop and web.

# The best Grok Bot alternatives in 2026

People look past Grok Bot because it has no free plan, because they want to choose or see the model, or because they want to run it on their own server. Rakazo, MausBot and OpenBot are open-source takes on the same idea. Agent Zero is free software with a desktop of its own. Manus, ChatGPT Dots and Claude Cowork are the hosted options. Casama is open source with a free hosted plan.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-alternatives

## The short list

| | Pick it if you want | Open source | Free to start |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rakazo** | A computer per bot, self-hosted or hosted, with no markup on models | Yes | Self-hosting is free |
| **MausBot** | To reuse AI subscriptions you already pay for, on your desktop | Yes | The desktop app |
| **OpenBot** | To roll AI coworkers out across a company with admin controls | The app is; it needs a separately licensed part | For one person on a laptop |
| **Agent Zero** | A full Linux desktop for the agent, free and hackable | Yes | Yes, all of it |
| **Manus** | Finished decks, websites and research with nothing to set up | No | 300 credits a day |
| **ChatGPT Dots** | An always-on agent inside a ChatGPT plan you already have | No | No |
| **Claude Cowork and Duet** | Agents inside a Claude plan, with finished documents from your files | No | No |
| **Casama** | A computer per bot, approvals on by default, native apps, self-hosted or hosted | Yes | A free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free |

We make Casama, so weigh its place here accordingly. Every fact about the others comes from the
sources at the end of the page, checked on November 18, 2026.

## Why people switch from Grok Bot

Grok Bot has native apps on every desktop and phone platform and team Bots in Slack and Teams. Its
sources also show the reasons people look elsewhere:

- **No free plan.** Paid plans are $30, $100 or $200 a month, with a weekly usage pool and then
  pay per use. Subscribers reported weekly limits being cut in late October 2026 without warning.
- **One computer per person.** All of a person's Bots share one computer, its files and its
  sign-ins.
- **No choice of model.** You can't choose the model, and you aren't shown which one ran.
- **No self-hosting.** It runs in xAI's cloud only, on computers in the United States.

## Side by side: the open-source options

| | Casama | Grok Bot | Rakazo | MausBot | OpenBot | Agent Zero |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Closed | Apache-2.0 | Apache-2.0, with a source-available `enterprise/` folder | MIT app; it needs CopilotKit Intelligence, which is licensed separately | MIT |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | xAI's cloud only | Your own server, a desktop app, or Rakazo's cloud | Your desktop, your own server, or MausBot Cloud | Your Mac or Windows desktop, or your own server or Kubernetes; hosted is early access | Your computer or your own server, in Docker; no hosted version |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | One cloud computer per person, shared by all of that person's Bots | Each bot has its own container or cloud computer | Your machine by default; a cloud computer per bot on paid Cloud plans | A container per person; a bot can be given its own | A Docker container with its own Linux desktop, terminal and browser; can also be given access to your computer |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | An automatic check decides; you can add up to 20 "ask first" rules | Yes: an Ask mode, or an Auto mode where a model decides when to ask | Allow and Deny cards; the vendor says not every action is guaranteed to pause | Yes: admin policies block, allow or require approval | None by default: every tool is allowed until you block it in an agent profile |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | No choice, and you aren't shown which model ran | Your own keys, a ChatGPT plan, local models, or Rakazo credits at the provider's price | None included: it drives AI tools you're already signed in to, or API keys | Your own keys or subscriptions, or any OpenAI-style endpoint | Your own keys, a ChatGPT sign-in, or local models through Ollama or LM Studio |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, Android | Web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, Android | Mac, Windows, Linux (beta); phone apps are handed out through Discord | Mac and Windows; phone, web, Slack and Teams are early access | A0 Launcher for Windows, Mac and Linux, a web app and a CLI; no phone app |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Paid plans at $30, $100 or $200 a month; a weekly usage pool, then billed at token cost | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: $15, $49 or $99 a month, or credits from $20 | Desktop app: free. Cloud: $15, $49 or $99 a month; Team $40 for two people | Free for personal use; Business up to $29 per active user a month | Free; you pay your model provider |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | No free plan; some accounts get a 7-day trial credit | Self-hosting is free; hosted plans have a 7-day trial | Yes, the desktop app | Yes, for one person on their own laptop | Yes, all of it |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | A training opt-out exists | Not stated either way | Not stated | Not stated for OpenBot | Not stated; it runs on your machine and sends prompts to the model you choose |

## Side by side: the hosted options

| | Casama | Grok Bot | Manus | ChatGPT Dots | Claude Cowork and Duet |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | xAI's cloud only | Manus's cloud; a desktop app can run commands on your computer | OpenAI's cloud | Anthropic's cloud; it reaches your computer through the desktop app |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | One cloud computer per person, shared by all of that person's Bots | A cloud sandbox with a browser, per person | Each dot has its own cloud computer that you can open | Cowork: cloud sessions you can watch. Duet: its own cloud computer that you can't watch |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | An automatic check decides; you can add up to 20 "ask first" rules | None described in the cloud; three modes on your own computer | Built-in rules plus your own; some confirmations can't be removed | Cowork: depends on the mode you pick. Duet: asks before sending, paying, signing or deleting |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | No choice, and you aren't shown which model ran | Manus picks; no choice on standard plans | OpenAI's model; no choice | Claude models only |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, Android | Web, iPhone, iPad, Mac (Apple silicon), Windows | ChatGPT on desktop, web and phone | Mac, Windows, Linux (beta), web, iPhone, Android |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Paid plans at $30, $100 or $200 a month; a weekly usage pool, then billed at token cost | Credits: Free; Pro from $20 a month for 4,000 credits, up to $200; Team from $20 a seat | One dot is included with ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium | Included in paid Claude plans and counted against their limits |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | No free plan; some accounts get a 7-day trial credit | Yes: 300 credits a day | No | No |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open; its computers run in the United States | Open; sales were paused in some regions in August 2026 | Not for Pro subscribers in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK | Cowork: paid plans. Duet: United States only, by waitlist |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | A training opt-out exists | Team plans say no; individual plans are unclear | Not confirmed | On for consumer plans unless you switch it off |

## Each alternative

### Rakazo

- You want hosted model usage at the provider's price with no markup.
- You want a wide choice of sandbox providers for bot computers when self-hosting.
- You want every way to run it (self-hosted, desktop, hosted) from one project.

Worth knowing:

- It is young: the repository was created in August 2026 and it is before version 1.0.
- iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram work only when self-hosted.
- The entry hosted plan has 25 computer hours a month.

### MausBot

- You already pay for Claude Code, Codex or Grok and want to reuse those sign-ins with no markup.
- You want a free desktop app that runs bots on your own computer.
- You want many cloud computer hours for the price.

Worth knowing:

- The vendor itself says approvals aren't guaranteed to pause every action.
- Slack is the only chat app, and only on paid plans.
- Free bots stop when your computer is off, and the phone apps aren't in the stores.

### OpenBot

- You are rolling AI coworkers out across a company and need roles, single sign-on, audit export and spend limits.
- You want to deploy inside your own cloud with Kubernetes.
- You want to plug in agents you built yourself.

Worth knowing:

- The MIT app can't run without CopilotKit Intelligence, which needs a paid licence for production.
- Only the Mac and Windows desktop apps are generally available.
- An independent review of version 1.0.2 found the default policy allows every action.

### Agent Zero

- You want an agent with a full Linux desktop you can watch, including apps like LibreOffice and Blender.
- You want free software you can read and change, with plugins, MCP and A2A.
- You want to choose any model, including local ones.

Worth knowing:

- There is no hosted version: you run Docker and bring your own model keys or model server.
- Tools are allowed by default and nothing asks before acting; limits are set in agent profiles.
- No phone apps and no team accounts.

### Manus

- You want nothing to set up: a hosted agent with its own cloud computer on web, phone and desktop.
- You want finished deliverables such as slide decks, websites and wide research.
- You want team administration on a hosted product.

Worth knowing:

- It is closed and cloud-only, and you don't choose the model on standard plans.
- Credit use depends on how complex a task turns out to be, and Trustpilot reviewers complain about credits lost to errors.
- In August 2026 it deleted data and paused sales for users in regions it didn't name.

### ChatGPT Dots

- You already pay for ChatGPT Pro and want an always-on agent inside it.
- You want a very large set of app connections.
- You want cautious background behaviour: unprompted work is read-only.

Worth knowing:

- It is only on the most expensive plans, and not for Pro subscribers in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK.
- Users reported dots stopping for hours at a limit with no meter or reset time.
- Early users described repeated confirmation prompts.

### Claude Cowork and Duet

- You want finished documents made from your own files: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF.
- You already pay for Claude and want agents inside it.
- You want firm approval rules: Duet has a short list of actions it won't do even if you approve.

Worth knowing:

- Duet is US-only and waitlisted, and you can't watch or take over its browser.
- Anthropic advises against scheduling tasks that send, buy or do things that are hard to undo.
- Both draw on your Claude plan's usage limits, and Cowork uses them faster than chat.

### Casama

- You want each bot on its own sandboxed Linux computer, not one shared by all of them, and you
  want to watch it and take over.
- You want risky steps to wait for you from the start, with payments always asking and a checkpoint
  saved before destructive commands.
- You want native apps on iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows and Linux, like Grok Bot.
- You want a free hosted plan, or to self-host for free with any model.

Worth knowing:

- It is new, first released in November 2026, with a small community.
- Grok Bot can learn a workflow from one recording, and comes from a much larger vendor.
- Choosing your own model is for self-hosted servers. On Casama Cloud, Casama picks.

## Moving over from Grok Bot

Each Grok Bot becomes a Casama bot. Grok Bot has no export, so Casama asks your Bot instead: choose
**Paste a Bot's Setup**, send your Bot the prompt and paste its reply. Its instructions, schedules,
skills and "ask first" rules come over after you review them. Then sign in to the apps it used. Each bot gets its own computer, so sign-ins no longer leak from one
bot to another. Team Bots in Slack or Teams reconnect per bot.

## Questions

### What is the best open-source alternative to Grok Bot?

Rakazo is the closest in shape: a computer per bot, hosted or self-hosted. MausBot suits people who
want to reuse subscriptions they already pay for. Casama adds approvals on by default and native
phone apps. Agent Zero is the most hackable, but you run it yourself.

### Is there a free alternative to Grok Bot?

Yes. Agent Zero is free software. Rakazo and Casama are free to self-host, and MausBot's desktop app
is free. Manus gives 300 credits a day, and Casama Cloud's Free plan has $1 of credits and 5
computer hours a month.

### Which Grok Bot alternative lets me choose the model?

Rakazo, MausBot, OpenBot and Agent Zero all take your own keys or subscriptions, and so does Casama
when self-hosted. Manus, ChatGPT Dots and Claude Cowork pick the model for you.

### Can I self-host a Grok Bot alternative?

Yes: Rakazo, MausBot, OpenBot, Agent Zero and Casama can all run on your own server. See
[how to self-host an AI agent](https://casama.ai/learn/how-to-self-host-an-ai-agent).

### Which has apps on every platform?

Grok Bot, Rakazo and Casama list apps for Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone and Android. See
[which AI agents have iPhone and Android apps](https://casama.ai/learn/which-ai-agents-have-iphone-and-android-apps).

# Grok Bot pricing in 2026: plans, weekly limits and what you really pay

Grok Bot costs $30, $100 or $200 a month on the Premium, Super and Ultra plans. Each plan includes a weekly pool of usage, and anything beyond the pool is billed by token cost. xAI doesn't publish the size of the pool or the per-token rate, so the monthly bill for heavy use can't be worked out in advance. Here is what is published, what isn't, and cheaper ways to get the same thing.

Updated 2026-11-19. Page: https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-pricing

Casama is not affiliated with xAI or Grok Bot. Grok Bot is a trademark of its owner. We make Casama,
so weigh our view accordingly. Facts about Grok Bot were checked on November 19, 2026, and the sources
are listed at the end.

## Grok Bot plans and prices

| Plan | Price | What the usage is |
|---|---|---|
| **Premium** | $30 a month | "Weekly Grok Bot usage included". The amount isn't stated. |
| **Super** | $100 a month | Everything in Premium, plus 3.5 times Premium's usage and priority model access at peak times. |
| **Ultra** | $200 a month | Everything in Super, plus 12 times Premium's usage and earliest access to all products and models. |

The [Grok Bot page](https://x.ai/bot) shows monthly prices only. It doesn't show a yearly price.
Premium, Super and Ultra are X subscriptions, and Grok Bot is included on each of them. Plus and
Free X accounts don't include it, according to the
[Grok Bot FAQ](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq).

| | Casama | Grok Bot |
|---|---|---|
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Paid plans at $30, $100 or $200 a month; a weekly usage pool, then billed at token cost |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | No free plan; some accounts get a 7-day trial credit |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | xAI's cloud only |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | One cloud computer per person, shared by all of that person's Bots |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | No choice, and you aren't shown which model ran |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Team Bots in Slack; admin controls on Enterprise |

## How the weekly pool works

- **One shared pool.** Grok Bot draws on one weekly pool of usage that it shares with Cursor and the
  Grok apps, says the [FAQ](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq). Super and Ultra have larger pools than
  Premium.
- **No published size.** Neither the pricing page nor the FAQ gives the pool as a number of messages,
  tokens or dollars. You can see your own use under Usage in the Grok dashboard.
- **It resets weekly.** If you use it up, it comes back at the weekly reset.

## What happens when the pool runs out

The Grok Bot page says that subscriptions "come with weekly usage included, with additional usage
billed based on token cost". The FAQ adds that prepaid credit covers use beyond the weekly pool, and
that you can leave Auto Top-up off or set a monthly limit under Additional usage credits.

What the sources don't say is the rate. There is no per-token price on either page.

On older accounts billed through Cursor, a user thread on the Cursor forum describes the order in
which usage is taken: the weekly allowance first, then referral or usage credits, then paid
on-demand usage. A Cursor staff member said in the
[thread](https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-gives-no-warning-before-weekly-usage-spills-into-paid-on-demand/169679)
that this was working as intended. Users there asked for a warning before paid use starts. The
workaround they describe is to watch the weekly meter and pause the bot near 100%.

The FAQ also warns that a spending cap doesn't stop a run that is already going, so a task can go
somewhat over it.

## Weekly limits were cut in October

Crypto Briefing reported on November 2, 2026 that many subscribers used up their weekly allowance
four or more days early in late October. xAI put some of it down to a billing dashboard glitch and
some to "necessary adjustments to how usage gets allocated". The same report says Elon Musk wrote on
November 1 that serving Grok Bot had become "unsustainably high relative to revenue"
([source](https://cryptobriefing.com/musk-grok-bot-usage-limits-high-costs/)). That is no promise of
a price change, but it is a reason not to plan around today's limits staying the same.

## What you really pay

Only the fixed part is known:

| Use | Grok Bot | What the sources let us say |
|---|---|---|
| Light | Premium, $30 a month, $360 over twelve months | Fixed fee, as long as you stay inside the pool |
| Steady | Super, $100 a month, $1,200 over twelve months | 3.5 times Premium's usage |
| Heavy | Ultra, $200 a month, $2,400 over twelve months | 12 times Premium's usage, then billed by token cost |

We can't give a dollar figure for what happens after the pool, because no rate is published. If you
go over, your bill is the plan price plus whatever your usage costs at token rates you can only see
on your own dashboard. Set a monthly limit first.

## Teams and Enterprise

The Grok Bot page has a Teams tab but lists no Teams prices. It says Grok Bot is available to teams
on the Teams plan and to Enterprise, and sends Enterprise buyers to "Contact sales". Per the FAQ,
every paid X subscription seat includes Grok Bot, and Enterprise admins turn it on. So team pricing
isn't published; you have to ask.

## Is there a free trial?

Some accounts see a Start Trial button. The FAQ says the trial is a usage credit with a 7-day
window, that it never turns into a paid plan, and that used credit isn't restored. Whether you see
it isn't something you can count on. See [Is Grok Bot free?](https://casama.ai/compare/is-grok-bot-free).

## A cheaper way to get the same thing

[Casama](https://casama.ai/pricing) is an open-source AI teammate app. Each bot has its own computer, and you can
watch it and take over. Its prices are all published:

| Option | Price | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| **Casama Cloud Free** | $0 | $1 of credits a month, 3 bots, 1 computer with 5 hours |
| **Casama Cloud Plus** | $15 a month, or $150 a year | $5 of credits, 10 bots, 2 computers with 30 hours |
| **Casama Cloud Pro** | $49 a month, or $490 a year | $15 of credits, unlimited bots, 5 computers with 100 hours, 3 seats |
| **Casama Cloud Max** | $99 a month, or $899 a year | $30 of credits, unlimited bots, 10 computers with 300 hours, 10 seats |
| **Self-hosted** | $0 for the software | Any model, no limit on users, bots or computers |

On Casama Cloud a credit is a dollar. Credits pay for models, extra computer time and other paid
work, and every bot has a budget per run ($1 by default) and per day ($10 by default). When a run
reaches its budget it stops and tells you, and a bot that is waiting for your approval costs nothing.
Casama is also open about its limit: when credits run out, bots stop starting paid work, and nothing
is charged unless you buy a pack or change plan.

Self-hosting costs you a server and your model provider. With your own keys that is usually a few
dollars a month for light use, and local models cost nothing but run slower. See
[run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

Two honest caveats. Casama is new, first released in November 2026, and Grok Bot comes from a far
larger company. And choosing your own model is for self-hosted servers: on Casama Cloud, Casama
picks the model.

## When Grok Bot is worth it

- You want native apps on every desktop and phone platform from a large vendor.
- You want shared team Bots in Slack and Microsoft Teams with ready-made roles.
- You want to teach a workflow by recording it once.
- You already pay for an X Premium plan, so Grok Bot is included.

If one of those is the deciding point, Grok Bot is a good pick. See the
[full comparison](https://casama.ai/compare/casama-vs-grok-bot).

## Questions

### How much does Grok Bot cost?

Grok Bot costs $30 a month on Premium, $100 on Super and $200 on Ultra. Each plan includes weekly
usage, and extra use is billed by token cost. Teams and Enterprise prices aren't published.

### What is the Grok Bot weekly limit?

xAI doesn't publish it as a number. Super has 3.5 times the usage of Premium and Ultra has 12 times.
You can see your own use on the Usage page of the Grok dashboard.

### What happens if I go over the Grok Bot limit?

Use beyond the weekly pool is billed by token cost, drawn from prepaid credit. You can leave Auto
Top-up off or set a monthly limit, though a limit doesn't stop a run in progress.

### Is there a yearly Grok Bot price?

The Grok Bot page shows monthly prices only. Casama Cloud does have yearly prices: $150, $490 and
$899.

### What is the cheapest Grok Bot alternative?

Self-hosted Casama costs nothing for the software, and Casama Cloud's Free plan costs $0. See
[Grok Bot alternatives](https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-alternatives), and [Grok Bot templates](https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-templates)
for what you can start from.

# Grok Bot templates, and the Casama equivalents

Grok Bot templates are ready-made Bots for a job, such as Sales Outbound or Chief of Staff, that you add as your own copy. Its page shows eight, and x.ai's sitemap listed 91 template pages in November 2026. Casama's gallery has 49 starter bots, 43 routines, 42 skills and 61 apps, all free and open. Here is how the two line up, and where Grok Bot's catalogue is bigger.

Updated 2026-11-19. Page: https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-templates

Casama is not affiliated with xAI or Grok Bot. Grok Bot is a trademark of its owner. We make Casama,
so weigh our view accordingly. Facts about Grok Bot were checked on November 19, 2026, and the
sources are at the end.

## What Grok Bot templates are

The [Grok Bot page](https://x.ai/bot) has a section called "Give each Bot a job" that lists eight
templates:

1. Sales Outbound
2. Talent Scout
3. Paid Media
4. Expense Manager
5. Product Performance
6. Bug Reproduction
7. Account Health
8. Chief of Staff

Only Sales Outbound has a description on the page. The page also links to "Explore more bots" in a
marketplace. The page gives no count, but x.ai's [sitemap](https://x.ai/sitemap.xml) listed 91
template pages when we checked on November 18, 2026.

You can also make your own. Per the [Grok Bot FAQ](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq), you open a Bot's
details, choose Share, then Create a copy, publish it and copy the link. Anyone with the link can
preview it on x.ai and add a copy. They don't get your computer, logins or history. The link shows
the Bot's configuration, so the FAQ says to remove secrets first, and a team can switch template
sharing off.

## Casama equivalents

Casama's [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai) is an open catalogue. Anyone can add to it by pull
request. These are the closest real items to each Grok Bot template. They are not copies of Grok
Bot's: we haven't seen what is inside those, so match them by job, not by detail.

| Grok Bot template | Closest Casama items |
|---|---|
| **Sales Outbound** | [Outbound prospector](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/outbound-prospector/) bot builds lead lists and drafts first touches. [Sales](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/sales-researcher/) bot researches leads. [Sales pipeline review](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/routine/pipeline-review/) routine, Monday mornings. |
| **Talent Scout** | [Recruiting screener](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/recruiting-screener/) bot screens applicants and schedules next steps. [People ops](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/people-ops/) bot writes job descriptions and onboarding plans. |
| **Paid Media** | [Marketer](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/marketer/) bot plans campaigns and writes ads and landing pages. It writes the work; it isn't built to manage ad accounts. |
| **Expense Manager** | [Expense matcher](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/expense-matcher/) bot matches receipts to card transactions. [Receipt collector](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/routine/receipt-collector/) and [Subscription audit](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/routine/subscription-audit/) routines. |
| **Product Performance** | [Analyst](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/data-analyst/) bot runs the numbers and makes charts. [Weekly metrics](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/routine/weekly-metrics/) routine. [Mixpanel](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/app/mixpanel/) and [Amplitude](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/app/amplitude/) apps to read your analytics. |
| **Bug Reproduction** | [Bug triage](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/bug-triager/) bot reproduces reports and finds duplicates. [QA](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/qa-tester/) bot tests in a real browser. [Bug report](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/skill/bug-report/) skill. |
| **Account Health** | [Customer success](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/customer-success/) bot spots accounts that need attention. [Customer health check](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/routine/customer-health/) routine, Tuesdays. [Attio](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/app/attio/) and [Close](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/app/close/) apps for your CRM. |
| **Chief of Staff** | [Assistant](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/executive-assistant/) bot triages inbox and calendar. [Personal assistant](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/bot/casama/) is Casama itself. [Morning plan](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/routine/morning-plan/) and [Week ahead](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/routine/week-ahead/) routines. |

Casama also has things Grok Bot's list doesn't show, such as a
[Competitor watch](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/routine/competitor-watch/) routine and a [Competitive brief](https://gallery.casama.ai/i/skill/competitive-brief/)
skill. Browse the rest by type: bots, routines, skills and apps.

An app in the gallery connects a bot to a service, so it still needs you to sign in to that service.

## How to start one in Casama

1. **A bot.** In the sidebar, select Add, then New bot, then pick a persona or Browse all. Starter
   bots from the gallery appear there. Change the instructions however you like.
2. **A routine.** Open the bot's profile, then Routines, then New routine, and tap one of the Ideas at
   the top. It fills in the name, instructions and schedule.
3. **A skill.** Go to Settings, then Skills, then Skill catalog, and select Install for one bot or
   the whole workspace.
4. **From a file or link.** Select Add, then Import a bot, and pick a template file or open a link.
   Casama shows what comes with it before you import. Importing a template never carries keys or
   sign-ins.

New bots start by asking before risky actions. Each bot gets its own computer. The full steps are in
the [bots guide](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/bots), and
[moving from Grok Bot to Casama](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/moving-from-grok-bot) maps Grok Bot's
ideas onto Casama's.

## Sharing your own

In Casama you open a bot's profile, then Advanced, then Share as Template. You can save it as a file
or copy a link, which works for 30 days. Memories are left out unless you tick them. You can also
add it to the public gallery by pull request to
[stackwares/casama-gallery](https://github.com/stackwares/casama-gallery).

## Where Grok Bot's catalogue is bigger

To be clear: Grok Bot has a bigger catalogue, about 91 templates against our 49 starter bots. It has a marketplace, and its templates are made by a large vendor and
set up for Slack and Teams team Bots. Casama's gallery is smaller in some areas, new, and made by
a small community. Casama's starter bots are starting points you will edit, not finished products. If one particular Grok Bot template is
what you want, check the marketplace for it first.

## Questions

### How many Grok Bot templates are there?

The Grok Bot page lists eight, and links to a marketplace with more. xAI doesn't state a total, but
its sitemap listed 91 template pages on November 18, 2026.

### What are the Grok Bot templates?

The eight on its page are Sales Outbound, Talent Scout, Paid Media, Expense Manager, Product
Performance, Bug Reproduction, Account Health and Chief of Staff.

### Are Grok Bot templates free?

The sources don't give a separate price for templates. They are used from a Grok Bot subscription,
which starts at $30 a month. See [Grok Bot pricing](https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-pricing). Casama's gallery is
free, and every bot, routine and skill in it is open.

### Can I use my own template in Casama?

Yes, by pasting. Casama gives you a prompt to send your Grok Bot, and the Bot answers with its
setup. Paste the reply into Casama and its instructions, schedules, skills and apps come over, after
you review them. Events and sign-ins don't. The
[moving guide](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/moving-from-grok-bot) shows how.

### Do Grok Bot templates share my logins?

No. Per the FAQ, someone who adds a copy doesn't receive your computer, logins or history. The link
does show the configuration, so remove secrets first.

## Sources

- Grok Bot (checked 2026-11-19): https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/security, https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq, https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/approvals-security-and-privacy, https://x.ai/bot

Also: [Grok Bot pricing](https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-pricing), [Is Grok Bot free?](https://casama.ai/compare/is-grok-bot-free),
[Casama vs Grok Bot](https://casama.ai/compare/casama-vs-grok-bot), [Grok Bot alternative](https://casama.ai/alternatives/grok-bot),
[Grok Bot alternatives](https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-alternatives), [Casama pricing](https://casama.ai/pricing) and
[self-hosting](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

# Grok Bot vs Instinct vs Hark Pro

Three hosted AI assistants with very different shapes. Grok Bot is a paid work tool with apps everywhere. Hark Pro is a free phone-first assistant for errands. Instinct is an invite-only assistant you text or call. None can be self-hosted or lets you choose the model; Casama, the open-source option, does both.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-vs-instinct-vs-hark

## Side by side

| | Casama | Grok Bot | Instinct | Hark Pro |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Closed | Closed | Closed |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | xAI's cloud only | Instinct's cloud; you text or call it | Hark's cloud only |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | One cloud computer per person, shared by all of that person's Bots | Reviews describe its own cloud computer; the vendor's pages don't say | Its own cloud browser per person; you can watch it |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | An automatic check decides; you can add up to 20 "ask first" rules | Not documented; its terms don't promise any | It checks in before actions that need approval; there is no published list |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | No choice, and you aren't shown which model ran | Not stated | Hark chooses; no choice |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, Android | None needed; there is a web workspace for settings | Web, iPhone, iPad, Android |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | X, Slack, Microsoft Teams | Text message and phone call | Its own app only |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes | Implied, with no controls described | Yes; not in the EEA, the UK or Switzerland |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Schedules and some events | Reviews say it texts or calls you first | Scheduled tasks |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Team Bots in Slack; admin controls on Enterprise | None published | None found |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Paid plans at $30, $100 or $200 a month; a weekly usage pool, then billed at token cost | Not published; reported free during the beta | Free; $20 or $100 a month for more usage |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | No free plan; some accounts get a 7-day trial credit | Reported free while invite-only | Yes, with every feature; the cap isn't published |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open; its computers run in the United States | Invite or waitlist only | Open sign-up |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | A training opt-out exists | On by default; you can opt out | Says it doesn't train on your data |

Checked on November 18, 2026. Instinct publishes very little, so parts of its column come from
reviews and press; the sources are at the end. We make Casama.

## The short answer

- **Grok Bot** is for work. It has native apps on Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone and Android, team
  Bots in Slack and Teams, and plans at $30, $100 and $200 a month. There is no free plan.
- **Hark Pro** is for everyday life. Its free plan includes every feature, it says it doesn't
  train on your data, and it works from web and phone. There are no desktop apps or team plans.
- **Instinct** is for people who don't want an app at all. You text or call it. It is invite-only,
  with no published price.

## Three things to check before choosing

**Where the assistant works.** Grok Bot gives each person one cloud computer shared by all their
Bots. Hark gives each person a cloud browser you can watch. Instinct's own pages don't say.

**What it asks first.** Grok Bot uses an automatic check plus up to 20 rules you write. Hark says
it checks in before actions that need approval, without a published list. Instinct's terms promise
no confirmation steps.

**What happens to your data.** Hark says it doesn't train on your content. Grok Bot has a training
opt-out. Instinct trains by default unless you opt out.

## Choose Grok Bot if

- You want native apps on every desktop and phone platform from a large vendor.
- You want shared team Bots in Slack and Teams with ready-made roles.
- You want to teach a workflow by recording it once.

## Choose Hark Pro if

- You want a free plan that includes every feature.
- You want everyday errands on websites done from a cloud browser you can watch.
- You want a clear default of no training on your content.

## Choose Instinct if

- You want nothing to install: you text or call it like a person.
- You want everyday errands done for one person, such as groceries and tickets.
- You want an assistant that follows up without being asked.

## Where Casama fits

Casama is open source, so it answers the things none of these three can:

- **Run it yourself.** Free, on your own server, with your data on your machine.
- **Choose the model.** Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted.
- **A computer per bot.** Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux machine you can watch and take over.
- **Written rules.** What a bot must ask before doing is documented, and payments always ask.
- **Known costs.** Credits are dollars, with a budget per bot.
- **Open to everyone.** A free Cloud plan, with no invite and no region limits.

Casama is newer than all three and has a much smaller community.

## Worth knowing

**Grok Bot**

- Subscribers reported weekly limits being cut in late October 2026 without warning.
- All of a person's Bots share one computer, files and sign-ins.
- You can't choose or see the model, and you can't host it yourself.

**Hark Pro**

- Usage caps aren't published, and reviewers call them hard to predict.
- There are no desktop apps, no team plan, and no calls or texts.
- Memory is unavailable in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland.

**Instinct**

- Its terms bind you to agreements it makes for you and cap its liability at $100 or six months of fees.
- Training on your data is on by default.
- Early testers reported an email sent without permission and a successful phishing test.

## Questions

### Which is cheapest?

Hark Pro has a free plan, and Instinct is reported to be free during its beta. Grok Bot starts at
$30 a month. Casama has a free Cloud plan and is free to self-host.

### Which can I use outside the United States?

Grok Bot and Hark Pro don't publish a country list. Hark's memory is off in the EEA, the UK and
Switzerland. Instinct is invite-only. Casama has no region limits.

### Which is open source?

None of the three. Casama is, under AGPL-3.0.

## Sources

- Grok Bot (checked 2026-11-19): https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/security, https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq, https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/approvals-security-and-privacy, https://x.ai/bot
- Instinct (checked 2026-11-18): https://www.instinct.com/terms, https://builtin.com/articles/instinct-ai, https://instinct.com, https://www.eesel.ai/blog/instinct-ai-review, https://instinct.com/privacy-policy
- Hark Pro (checked 2026-11-18): https://hark.com, https://hark.com/using-hark, https://hark.com/security, https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hark-pro/id6772362941, https://hark.com/privacy-policy, https://hark.com/pricing

More: [Grok Bot](https://casama.ai/alternatives/grok-bot), [Instinct](https://casama.ai/alternatives/instinct) and
[Hark Pro](https://casama.ai/alternatives/hark) alternatives.

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# The best Hermes Agent alternatives in 2026

Hermes Agent, from Nous Research, is a free MIT-licensed agent that learns and writes its own skills. People look elsewhere when they want more chat apps, a smaller codebase, an agent that works off their own computer, or a hosted plan with approvals on by default. OpenClaw is the closest swap. Agent Zero, Rakazo and Casama give the agent a computer of its own.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/compare/hermes-agent-alternatives

## The short list

| | Pick it if you want | Agent works on | Stars |
|---|---|---|---|
| **OpenClaw** | The most chat apps and the biggest community | Your machine | about 395,000 |
| **nanobot** | A small Python agent in many chat apps | Your machine | about 50,000 |
| **NanoClaw** | A small codebase with every session in a container | A container per session | about 31,000 |
| **MausBot** | To reuse AI subscriptions you already pay for | Your machine | about 24,700 |
| **Agent Zero** | A full Linux desktop for the agent, free | Its own container | about 19,900 |
| **Rakazo** | A computer per bot with no markup on models | Its own computer | about 9,000 |
| **Casama** | A computer per bot with approvals on by default, native apps and a free hosted plan | Its own computer | new |

Hermes Agent itself has about 264,000 stars. Star counts are from GitHub on November 18, 2026. We
make Casama, so weigh its place here accordingly; every other fact has a source at the end.

## Why people switch from Hermes Agent

Hermes Agent runs on your own machine by default, with Docker, SSH and cloud sandboxes as options,
and asks about shell commands that match risky patterns. Its strength is one agent that improves
with use. The alternatives change different parts of that:

- **More reach:** OpenClaw and nanobot connect to more chat apps.
- **Off your machine:** Agent Zero, NanoClaw, Rakazo and Casama keep the agent in a container or a
  computer of its own by default.
- **Asking first:** Casama and Rakazo ask before risky steps by default, not only for shell commands.
- **Several bots and people:** Casama and Rakazo have teams of bots and workspaces for several people.

## Side by side

| | Casama | OpenClaw | nanobot | NanoClaw | Agent Zero | Rakazo |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | MIT | MIT | MIT | MIT | Apache-2.0 |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your own computer or server only; there is no hosted version | Your own machine or server, as a Python app or in Docker | Your own machine with Docker (macOS, Linux, Windows via WSL2); a hosted version is invite-only | Your computer or your own server, in Docker; no hosted version | Your own server, a desktop app, or Rakazo's cloud |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Runs on your machine; a sandbox is optional and off by default | The machine it's installed on; an optional shell sandbox | Each session in its own Docker container that sees only the folders you mount | A Docker container with its own Linux desktop, terminal and browser; can also be given access to your computer | Each bot has its own container or cloud computer |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Optional, and off by default | No ask-before-acting step; workspace limits and the sandbox are off by default in the config | Asks an admin before installing packages, adding MCP servers or admitting new senders; shell commands in the container don't ask | None by default: every tool is allowed until you block it in an agent profile | Yes: an Ask mode, or an Auto mode where a model decides when to ask |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Your own keys, a ChatGPT or Claude plan, or local models | Your own keys, Codex, Copilot or Grok sign-in, or local models; fallbacks supported | Claude by default (key or subscription); Codex, Cursor and OpenCode as options | Your own keys, a ChatGPT sign-in, or local models through Ollama or LM Studio | Your own keys, a ChatGPT plan, local models, or Rakazo credits at the provider's price |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, Android; no hosted web app | A web app (works on phones), a terminal UI and a CLI | None: chat apps and a terminal | A0 Launcher for Windows, Mac and Linux, a web app and a CLI; no phone app | Web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, Android |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | About 29, including WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, iMessage and Teams | Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, WeChat, Feishu, Signal, Matrix, email and more | WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Teams, iMessage, Signal, Matrix and more, each added with a skill | Telegram, WhatsApp and email; more through plugins | Slack and Teams; iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram only when self-hosted |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes, as Markdown files on your disk | Layered files, tidied on a schedule and tracked in git | Markdown files per agent group | Long-term memory you can search and edit, per project | Yes, per bot, and bots can share what they learn |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Schedules, event triggers, webhooks | Time, interval or cron schedules, command triggers and long-running goals | One-time or cron tasks | Scheduled tasks: cron, one-time or by hand | Schedules, email, webhooks, GitHub events, watched changes |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | A group that trusts each other can share one; it isn't built to separate users | No team accounts; separate people need separate instances | Owner and admin roles and agent teams; built for one person | Not described: one login per instance | Organizations, spaces and group chats; roles for people aren't described |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Free; you pay your model provider | Free; you pay your model provider | Free; you pay your model provider | Free; you pay your model provider | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: $15, $49 or $99 a month, or credits from $20 |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Yes, entirely | Yes, all of it | Yes, all of it | Yes, all of it | Self-hosting is free; hosted plans have a 7-day trial |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone | Open to everyone | Open to everyone; needs a terminal, git and Docker | Open to everyone | Open to everyone |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | There is no OpenClaw cloud; your model provider's policy applies | Not stated | Not stated; self-hosted data stays on your machine | Not stated; it runs on your machine and sends prompts to the model you choose | Not stated either way |

## Each alternative

### OpenClaw

- You want the most chat apps: about 29 channels, plus apps on every desktop and phone platform.
- You want software with no paid tier at all, run by a nonprofit.
- You want the largest community: about 395,000 GitHub stars.

Worth knowing:

- Tools run on your own machine, and both the sandbox and approval prompts are off until you turn them on.
- The Register reported three high-impact security advisories in three days in February 2026, and malicious skills on its skill registry.
- It isn't designed for people who don't trust each other to share one agent.

### nanobot

- You want an agent in many chat apps, including WeChat, Feishu, QQ and DingTalk.
- You want any model, including local ones, with fallbacks.
- You want a small Python codebase you can read, extend or embed.

Worth knowing:

- There is no hosted version: you install it, bring a model and keep it running for chat apps and schedules.
- The workspace limit and shell sandbox are off by default, and plugins run with full permissions.
- One instance has one memory and one admin, so keeping people apart takes separate instances.

### NanoClaw

- You want each agent sandboxed in its own container, with API keys kept out of it.
- You want to message your agent from many chat apps, including WhatsApp, Signal and iMessage.
- You want a small codebase you can read in an afternoon and change with a coding agent.

Worth knowing:

- It needs Docker and comfort with a terminal; there is no desktop or phone app.
- There are no settings screens: you customize it by changing code, and adding chat apps needs Claude Code.
- Containers have open internet access by default, and asking before each credential use is opt-in.

### MausBot

- You already pay for Claude Code, Codex or Grok and want to reuse those sign-ins with no markup.
- You want a free desktop app that runs bots on your own computer.
- You want many cloud computer hours for the price.

Worth knowing:

- The vendor itself says approvals aren't guaranteed to pause every action.
- Slack is the only chat app, and only on paid plans.
- Free bots stop when your computer is off, and the phone apps aren't in the stores.

### Agent Zero

- You want an agent with a full Linux desktop you can watch, including apps like LibreOffice and Blender.
- You want free software you can read and change, with plugins, MCP and A2A.
- You want to choose any model, including local ones.

Worth knowing:

- There is no hosted version: you run Docker and bring your own model keys or model server.
- Tools are allowed by default and nothing asks before acting; limits are set in agent profiles.
- No phone apps and no team accounts.

### Rakazo

- You want hosted model usage at the provider's price with no markup.
- You want a wide choice of sandbox providers for bot computers when self-hosting.
- You want every way to run it (self-hosted, desktop, hosted) from one project.

Worth knowing:

- It is young: the repository was created in August 2026 and it is before version 1.0.
- iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram work only when self-hosted.
- The entry hosted plan has 25 computer hours a month.

### Casama

- You want a team of bots, each on its own sandboxed Linux computer you can watch and take over.
- You want risky steps of every kind to wait for you, not only shell commands.
- You want bots that save and improve their own skills, with each change shown to you first.
- You want native apps on iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows and Linux.
- You want a free hosted plan, or to self-host with any model.

Worth knowing:

- It is the newest here, first released in November 2026, with a small community.
- It reaches fewer chat apps than Hermes Agent or OpenClaw.
- Choosing your own model is for self-hosted servers. On Casama Cloud, Casama picks.

## Questions

### What is the closest alternative to Hermes Agent?

OpenClaw: also free, MIT-licensed and on your own machine, with more chat apps. See
[OpenClaw vs Hermes Agent](https://casama.ai/compare/openclaw-vs-hermes-agent).

### Is there a hosted Hermes Agent alternative?

Yes. Casama, Rakazo and MausBot have hosted plans, and Casama's has a free tier.

### Which alternatives keep the agent off my computer?

Agent Zero, NanoClaw, Rakazo and Casama, by default. OpenClaw, nanobot and MausBot run on your
machine unless you set up a sandbox.

### Can these alternatives use local models?

Most can, through Ollama or another OpenAI-style server. Check each product's sources below for the
details.

Tables that put the AI agents people weigh against each other on one page, with a source for every fact.

# Is Grok Bot free?

No. Grok Bot has no free plan, and its cheapest plan is Premium at $30 a month. Some accounts are offered a trial credit that lasts 7 days and never turns into a paid plan. If you want to pay nothing, the free options are open-source agents you run yourself, and Casama's free Cloud plan.

Updated 2026-11-19. Page: https://casama.ai/compare/is-grok-bot-free

Casama is not affiliated with xAI or Grok Bot. Grok Bot is a trademark of its owner. We make Casama,
so weigh our view accordingly. Facts about Grok Bot were checked on November 19, 2026, and the
sources are at the end.

## What the sources say

- **No free plan.** Grok Bot is included in the Premium, Super and Ultra X subscriptions. Plus and
  Free accounts don't include it ([Grok Bot FAQ](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq)).
- **A trial for some accounts.** Some accounts see a Start Trial button. The FAQ says the trial is a
  usage credit with a 7-day window, it never converts to a paid plan, the credit is used up by
  agent steps and tokens, and used credit isn't restored. If you cancel it you can't restart it.
- **"Get started for free".** The [Grok Bot page](https://x.ai/bot) has a button with that label, but
  gives no trial length or terms.
- **App Store trials.** Trials bought through Apple are run by Apple, and they turn into paid
  subscriptions unless you cancel first.

## What the cheapest plan gets you

Premium costs $30 a month. It includes weekly Grok Bot usage, but the amount isn't published. Super
at $100 has 3.5 times Premium's usage, and Ultra at $200 has 12 times. Beyond the weekly pool, usage
is billed by token cost. The details, and what is not published, are in
[Grok Bot pricing](https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-pricing).

## Free alternatives

| Option | Cost | Worth knowing |
|---|---|---|
| **Casama Cloud Free** | $0 | $1 of credits a month, 3 bots, 1 computer with 5 hours. It doesn't expire. |
| **Casama, self-hosted** | $0 for the software | Any model, no limit on users or bots. You pay your model provider, or use local models for nothing. |
| **OpenClaw** | Free; you pay your model provider | MIT licence, on your own computer or server only, with no hosted version. |
| **Agent Zero** | Free; you pay your model provider | MIT licence, a full Linux desktop for the agent, in Docker. |
| **NanoClaw and nanobot** | Free; you pay your model provider | MIT licence, on your own machine. |
| **Hermes Agent** | Free; optional Nous Portal plans | MIT licence, on your own computer or server. |
| **Rakazo** | Self-hosting is free | Hosted plans start at $15 a month with a 7-day trial. |
| **MausBot** | The desktop app is free | Cloud plans start at $15 a month. |

Every price in this table is from each product's own pages, checked November 18, 2026. They are in
our [best open-source AI agents](https://casama.ai/compare/best-open-source-ai-agents) comparison and our guide to
[free AI agents](https://casama.ai/learn/are-there-free-ai-agents).

### What "free" leaves out

An agent has three costs: the software, the model and the computer. Open-source software removes the
first. The model is paid per use unless you run a local one, which is slower and weaker on long
tasks. The computer is free if you already own a machine to run it on. A free hosted plan, like
Casama's, covers a small allowance and then stops rather than charging you.

## Free with Casama

Casama is open source under AGPL-3.0, and each bot gets its own computer that you can watch and take
over.

1. **Try it hosted.** [Sign up for the free Cloud plan](https://app.casama.ai). When the $1 of monthly credits runs out, bots stop starting paid work and tell you.
   Nothing is charged unless you buy a pack or change plan.
2. **Or run it yourself.** One command installs the stack with Docker on a VPS, a home server or a
   laptop. See [self-hosted Casama](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

The Free plan is small. It is for trying things out. Paid plans start at $15 a month; see
[Casama pricing](https://casama.ai/pricing). Casama is also new, first released in November 2026, with a small
community, and on Casama Cloud, Casama picks the model.

## When Grok Bot is still the better pick

If you want native apps everywhere from a large vendor, shared team Bots in Slack and Teams, or to
teach a workflow by recording it once, Grok Bot has those. Casama can also learn a task from a recording, but its Slack support works through its chat apps. It is paid, though, and its limits have been cut before; see
[Grok Bot pricing](https://casama.ai/compare/grok-bot-pricing).

## Questions

### Is Grok Bot free to use?

No. It needs a paid X subscription: Premium at $30 a month, Super at $100 or Ultra at $200. Some
accounts get a 7-day trial credit.

### Does Grok Bot have a free trial?

Some accounts do. The FAQ says it is a usage credit with a 7-day window that never becomes a paid
plan. Not every account sees it, and the Grok Bot page gives no terms for its "Get started for free"
button.

### Is there a free Grok Bot alternative?

Yes. Casama's Cloud Free plan costs $0, and self-hosted Casama, OpenClaw, Agent Zero, NanoClaw and
nanobot are free software. Model usage costs money unless you use a local model.

### Is the Grok Bot free trial really free?

The credit is free, but Apple-run trials from the App Store become paid subscriptions unless you
cancel first, per the FAQ. Check which kind you have.

### Can I use Grok Bot without paying if I self-host it?

No. Grok Bot runs only in xAI's cloud, and its security docs say self-hosting isn't supported.
Casama can be self-hosted.

# The best Manus alternatives in 2026

People look past Manus for three reasons. They want a price that doesn't depend on how a task turns out, they want to choose the model or run it themselves, or they want the agent to ask before risky steps. Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Dots suit people who already pay for those assistants. Meta Muse and Hark Pro have free plans. Agent Zero and Casama are open source.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/compare/manus-alternatives

## The short list

| | Pick it if you want | Runs on | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Claude Cowork and Duet** | Finished documents from your own files, inside a Claude plan | Anthropic's cloud | Included in paid Claude plans |
| **ChatGPT Dots** | An always-on agent inside ChatGPT | OpenAI's cloud | Included with ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium |
| **Grok Bot** | Native apps everywhere and team Bots in Slack and Teams | xAI's cloud | $30, $100 or $200 a month |
| **Meta Muse** | A generous free plan, and your agent inside WhatsApp | Meta's cloud, US only | Free for most use |
| **Hark Pro** | A free plan with every feature, for everyday errands | Hark's cloud | Free; $20 or $100 a month |
| **Lindy** | One assistant a whole team shares in Slack | Lindy's cloud | From $29.99 a month per seat |
| **Agent Zero** | Free, open-source software with a full Linux desktop for the agent | Your computer or server | Free |
| **Casama** | Open source, a computer per bot, approvals on by default, self-hosted or hosted | Your server or Casama Cloud | Free; $15, $49 or $99 a month |

We make Casama, so weigh its place here accordingly. Every fact about the others comes from the
sources at the end of the page, checked on November 18, 2026.

## Why people switch from Manus

Manus is a hosted agent with a cloud computer and a browser. It is good at finished work such as
slide decks, websites and wide research, with nothing to set up. Its sources also show where people
run into trouble:

- **Credits.** Credit use depends on how complex a task turns out to be. Trustpilot reviewers
  complain about credits lost to errors.
- **No choice of model.** Manus picks it on standard plans, and you can't host Manus yourself.
- **No approvals in the cloud.** None are described for its cloud agent. Its desktop app has three
  modes for commands on your own computer.
- **Access.** In August 2026 it deleted data and paused sales for users in regions it didn't name.

| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Manus picks; no choice on standard plans | Claude models only | OpenAI's model; no choice | No choice, and you aren't shown which model ran | Meta's Muse Spark model only |

## Each alternative

### Claude Cowork and Duet

- You want finished documents made from your own files: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF.
- You already pay for Claude and want agents inside it.
- You want firm approval rules: Duet has a short list of actions it won't do even if you approve.

Worth knowing:

- Duet is US-only and waitlisted, and you can't watch or take over its browser.
- Anthropic advises against scheduling tasks that send, buy or do things that are hard to undo.
- Both draw on your Claude plan's usage limits, and Cowork uses them faster than chat.

### ChatGPT Dots

- You already pay for ChatGPT Pro and want an always-on agent inside it.
- You want a very large set of app connections.
- You want cautious background behaviour: unprompted work is read-only.

Worth knowing:

- It is only on the most expensive plans, and not for Pro subscribers in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK.
- Users reported dots stopping for hours at a limit with no meter or reset time.
- Early users described repeated confirmation prompts.

### Grok Bot

- You want native apps on every desktop and phone platform from a large vendor.
- You want shared team Bots in Slack and Teams with ready-made roles.
- You want to teach a workflow by recording it once.

Worth knowing:

- Subscribers reported weekly limits being cut in late October 2026 without warning.
- All of a person's Bots share one computer, files and sign-ins.
- You can't choose or see the model, and you can't host it yourself.

### Meta Muse

- You want a generous free plan for a full cloud-computer agent.
- You want to message your agent inside WhatsApp.
- You want a documented safety design with a separate guard that approves outbound actions.

Worth knowing:

- It is available in the United States only.
- Training on your interactions is on by default until you switch it off.
- Meta can technically access the agent's computer today; the stronger private mode hasn't shipped.

### Hark Pro

- You want a free plan that includes every feature.
- You want everyday errands on websites done from a cloud browser you can watch.
- You want a clear default of no training on your content.

Worth knowing:

- Usage caps aren't published, and reviewers call them hard to predict.
- There are no desktop apps, no team plan, and no calls or texts.
- Memory is unavailable in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland.

### Lindy

- You want one assistant your whole team shares in Slack, called with an @mention.
- You want routines that start on emails, Slack messages, calendar events or meetings ending.
- You want to see and edit what the assistant remembers, with version history.

Worth knowing:

- The free plan is $50 of credits that expire after 7 days; after that you pay per seat.
- Microsoft Teams isn't supported yet.
- Hosted only, and the privacy notice doesn't say which region holds your data.

### Agent Zero

- You want an agent with a full Linux desktop you can watch, including apps like LibreOffice and Blender.
- You want free software you can read and change, with plugins, MCP and A2A.
- You want to choose any model, including local ones.

Worth knowing:

- There is no hosted version: you run Docker and bring your own model keys or model server.
- Tools are allowed by default and nothing asks before acting; limits are set in agent profiles.
- No phone apps and no team accounts.

### Casama

- You want each bot on its own sandboxed Linux computer that you can watch and take over.
- You want risky steps, such as sending email, to wait for you from the start, and payments to
  always ask.
- You want to pay in dollars: on Casama Cloud a credit is a dollar, and each bot has a budget per
  run and per day.
- You want to self-host for free with any model, or start on a free hosted plan.

Worth knowing:

- It is new, first released in November 2026, with a small community.
- For a one-off deck or research report with nothing to set up, Manus is built for exactly that.
- Choosing your own model is for self-hosted servers. On Casama Cloud, Casama picks.

## Moving over from Manus

Manus projects keep instructions and files. To move one, make a bot for it, paste the project's
instructions, and add the files it needs. Re-create scheduled tasks as routines. Most products on
this list can run on a schedule, though limits differ.

## Questions

### What is the best free alternative to Manus?

It depends on where you live and how much you'll run it. Meta Muse is free for most use but only in
the United States. Hark Pro's free plan includes every feature, with a cap it doesn't publish.
Agent Zero is free software that you run yourself. Casama is free to self-host and has a free
hosted plan with $1 of credits and 5 computer hours a month.

### Is there an open-source alternative to Manus?

Yes. Agent Zero and Casama are open source and both give the agent a computer of its own. Our list
of the [best open-source AI agents](https://casama.ai/compare/best-open-source-ai-agents) covers seven more.

### Which Manus alternative lets me choose the model?

Agent Zero, and Casama when you self-host. Claude Cowork uses Claude models only, ChatGPT Dots uses
OpenAI's model, and Grok Bot doesn't show which model ran. Lindy picks per task and lets you
choose per task. See [which AI agents let you choose the model](https://casama.ai/learn/which-ai-agents-let-you-choose-the-model).

### Which Manus alternative asks before it acts?

Claude Duet asks before sending, paying, signing or deleting. Meta Muse needs approval for email,
moving data out and every purchase. Lindy waits for your OK on actions with outside impact. Casama
asks before risky steps by default and payments always ask. Agent Zero allows every tool until you
block it.

### Is there a Manus alternative that isn't priced in credits?

Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Dots are part of a subscription, though both have usage limits. Grok Bot
has a weekly usage pool. Agent Zero and self-hosted Casama cost nothing beyond your model provider.
On Casama Cloud, credits are dollars, so a task's cost reads as a price.
