# The best OpenClaw alternatives in 2026

People look past OpenClaw for three reasons. They want the agent off their own computer, they want it to ask before risky steps without setting that up, or they want a smaller codebase they can read. Hermes Agent is the closest like-for-like swap. NanoClaw and nanobot are the small ones. Agent Zero, Rakazo and Casama give the agent a computer of its own.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/compare/openclaw-alternatives

## The short list

| | Pick it if you want | Agent works on | Stars |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hermes Agent** | The closest swap: one agent that writes its own skills | Your machine | about 264,000 |
| **nanobot** | A small Python agent in even more chat apps | Your machine | about 50,000 |
| **NanoClaw** | A small codebase with every session in a container | A container per session | about 31,000 |
| **MausBot** | To reuse AI subscriptions you already pay for | Your machine | about 24,700 |
| **Agent Zero** | A full Linux desktop for the agent, free | Its own container | about 19,900 |
| **OpenBot** | Rolling agents out across a company | A container per person | about 12,700 |
| **Rakazo** | A computer per bot with no markup on models | Its own computer | about 9,000 |
| **Casama** | A computer per bot with approvals on by default, native apps and a free hosted plan | Its own computer | new |

OpenClaw itself has about 395,000 stars. Star counts are from GitHub on November 18, 2026. We make
Casama, so weigh its place here accordingly; every other fact on this page has a source at the end.

## Why people switch from OpenClaw

OpenClaw is free, MIT-licensed and reaches about 29 chat apps. It runs on your own machine, with its
sandbox and approval prompts off until you turn them on. That suits a careful person on a spare
computer. It's the part most alternatives change:

- **Where the agent works.** Agent Zero, NanoClaw, Rakazo, OpenBot and Casama keep the agent in a
  container or a computer of its own, so a mistake stays there.
- **When it asks.** Casama and Rakazo ask before risky steps by default, OpenBot uses admin
  policies, NanoClaw asks before installs and new tools, and Hermes Agent asks about risky-looking
  shell commands. Agent Zero and nanobot don't ask.
- **How big it is.** NanoClaw and nanobot were written as much smaller takes on OpenClaw.

## Side by side

| | Casama | Hermes Agent | nanobot | NanoClaw | Agent Zero | Rakazo |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | MIT | MIT | MIT | MIT | Apache-2.0 |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your own computer or server; a hosted agent comes with paid Nous Portal plans | Your own machine or server, as a Python app or in Docker | Your own machine with Docker (macOS, Linux, Windows via WSL2); a hosted version is invite-only | Your computer or your own server, in Docker; no hosted version | Your own server, a desktop app, or Rakazo's cloud |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Your machine by default; Docker, SSH or cloud sandboxes are optional | The machine it's installed on; an optional shell sandbox | Each session in its own Docker container that sees only the folders you mount | A Docker container with its own Linux desktop, terminal and browser; can also be given access to your computer | Each bot has its own container or cloud computer |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | For shell commands that match risky patterns | No ask-before-acting step; workspace limits and the sandbox are off by default in the config | Asks an admin before installing packages, adding MCP servers or admitting new senders; shell commands in the container don't ask | None by default: every tool is allowed until you block it in an agent profile | Yes: an Ask mode, or an Auto mode where a model decides when to ask |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Your own keys, Nous Portal, some subscriptions, or local models | Your own keys, Codex, Copilot or Grok sign-in, or local models; fallbacks supported | Claude by default (key or subscription); Codex, Cursor and OpenCode as options | Your own keys, a ChatGPT sign-in, or local models through Ollama or LM Studio | Your own keys, a ChatGPT plan, local models, or Rakazo credits at the provider's price |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Mac and Windows desktop apps and a terminal app; no phone app yet | A web app (works on phones), a terminal UI and a CLI | None: chat apps and a terminal | A0 Launcher for Windows, Mac and Linux, a web app and a CLI; no phone app | Web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, Android |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | More than 20, including Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Teams and iMessage | Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, WeChat, Feishu, Signal, Matrix, email and more | WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Teams, iMessage, Signal, Matrix and more, each added with a skill | Telegram, WhatsApp and email; more through plugins | Slack and Teams; iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram only when self-hosted |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes, and it writes and improves its own skills | Layered files, tidied on a schedule and tracked in git | Markdown files per agent group | Long-term memory you can search and edit, per project | Yes, per bot, and bots can share what they learn |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Schedules set up in plain language | Time, interval or cron schedules, command triggers and long-running goals | One-time or cron tasks | Scheduled tasks: cron, one-time or by hand | Schedules, email, webhooks, GitHub events, watched changes |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Limited; separate user accounts aren't described | No team accounts; separate people need separate instances | Owner and admin roles and agent teams; built for one person | Not described: one login per instance | Organizations, spaces and group chats; roles for people aren't described |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Free; optional Nous Portal at $0, $20, $100 or $200 a month | Free; you pay your model provider | Free; you pay your model provider | Free; you pay your model provider | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: $15, $49 or $99 a month, or credits from $20 |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Yes | Yes, all of it | Yes, all of it | Yes, all of it | Self-hosting is free; hosted plans have a 7-day trial |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone | Open to everyone | Open to everyone; needs a terminal, git and Docker | Open to everyone | Open to everyone |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | With your own keys only your provider sees your data; Nous Portal may train on prompts unless Privacy Mode is on | Not stated | Not stated; self-hosted data stays on your machine | Not stated; it runs on your machine and sends prompts to the model you choose | Not stated either way |

## Each alternative

### Hermes Agent

- You want one agent that teaches itself: it writes and refines its own skills and keeps searchable memory.
- You want wide model choice, including local models and several subscription sign-ins.
- You want to choose where commands run: locally, in Docker, over SSH or in a cloud sandbox.

Worth knowing:

- Commands run on your own machine by default, and its docs say the deny rules are pattern matching that scripts can get around.
- There is no phone app yet.
- It is still before version 1.0, with a very large backlog of open issues.

### nanobot

- You want an agent in many chat apps, including WeChat, Feishu, QQ and DingTalk.
- You want any model, including local ones, with fallbacks.
- You want a small Python codebase you can read, extend or embed.

Worth knowing:

- There is no hosted version: you install it, bring a model and keep it running for chat apps and schedules.
- The workspace limit and shell sandbox are off by default, and plugins run with full permissions.
- One instance has one memory and one admin, so keeping people apart takes separate instances.

### NanoClaw

- You want each agent sandboxed in its own container, with API keys kept out of it.
- You want to message your agent from many chat apps, including WhatsApp, Signal and iMessage.
- You want a small codebase you can read in an afternoon and change with a coding agent.

Worth knowing:

- It needs Docker and comfort with a terminal; there is no desktop or phone app.
- There are no settings screens: you customize it by changing code, and adding chat apps needs Claude Code.
- Containers have open internet access by default, and asking before each credential use is opt-in.

### MausBot

- You already pay for Claude Code, Codex or Grok and want to reuse those sign-ins with no markup.
- You want a free desktop app that runs bots on your own computer.
- You want many cloud computer hours for the price.

Worth knowing:

- The vendor itself says approvals aren't guaranteed to pause every action.
- Slack is the only chat app, and only on paid plans.
- Free bots stop when your computer is off, and the phone apps aren't in the stores.

### Agent Zero

- You want an agent with a full Linux desktop you can watch, including apps like LibreOffice and Blender.
- You want free software you can read and change, with plugins, MCP and A2A.
- You want to choose any model, including local ones.

Worth knowing:

- There is no hosted version: you run Docker and bring your own model keys or model server.
- Tools are allowed by default and nothing asks before acting; limits are set in agent profiles.
- No phone apps and no team accounts.

### OpenBot

- You are rolling AI coworkers out across a company and need roles, single sign-on, audit export and spend limits.
- You want to deploy inside your own cloud with Kubernetes.
- You want to plug in agents you built yourself.

Worth knowing:

- The MIT app can't run without CopilotKit Intelligence, which needs a paid licence for production.
- Only the Mac and Windows desktop apps are generally available.
- An independent review of version 1.0.2 found the default policy allows every action.

### Rakazo

- You want hosted model usage at the provider's price with no markup.
- You want a wide choice of sandbox providers for bot computers when self-hosting.
- You want every way to run it (self-hosted, desktop, hosted) from one project.

Worth knowing:

- It is young: the repository was created in August 2026 and it is before version 1.0.
- iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram work only when self-hosted.
- The entry hosted plan has 25 computer hours a month.

### Casama

- You want each bot on its own sandboxed Linux computer that you can watch and take over.
- You want risky steps to wait for you from the start, with a checkpoint saved before destructive
  commands.
- You want native apps on iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows and Linux.
- You want a free hosted plan, or to self-host with any model.

Worth knowing:

- It is the newest here, first released in November 2026, with a small community.
- It reaches fewer chat apps than OpenClaw, Hermes Agent or nanobot.
- Choosing your own model is for self-hosted servers. On Casama Cloud, Casama picks.

## Questions

### What is the best free alternative to OpenClaw?

Hermes Agent, nanobot, NanoClaw and Agent Zero are free and open source like OpenClaw. Casama is
free to self-host and has a free hosted plan. You pay for the AI model unless you run a local one.

### Which OpenClaw alternative is the most secure?

The one whose defaults match how much setup you'll do. If you won't configure a sandbox and
approvals yourself, pick one that keeps the agent off your machine and asks first by default.

### Is there a hosted OpenClaw alternative?

Yes. Casama, Rakazo and MausBot have hosted plans, and Casama's has a free tier. Hermes Agent has an
optional hosted agent through Nous Portal.

### Which alternative is closest to OpenClaw?

Hermes Agent: also MIT-licensed, on your own machine, in more than 20 chat apps. See
[OpenClaw vs Hermes Agent](https://casama.ai/compare/openclaw-vs-hermes-agent).

# OpenClaw vs Hermes Agent: which should you run?

OpenClaw and Hermes Agent are the two most-starred open-source personal agents, and both are free and MIT-licensed. Pick OpenClaw for the most chat apps and phone apps. Pick Hermes Agent for an agent that writes its own skills. If you want each agent on its own sandboxed computer with approvals on by default, look at Casama as well.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/compare/openclaw-vs-hermes-agent

## Side by side

| | Casama | OpenClaw | Hermes Agent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | MIT | MIT |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your own computer or server only; there is no hosted version | Your own computer or server; a hosted agent comes with paid Nous Portal plans |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Runs on your machine; a sandbox is optional and off by default | Your machine by default; Docker, SSH or cloud sandboxes are optional |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Optional, and off by default | For shell commands that match risky patterns |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Your own keys, a ChatGPT or Claude plan, or local models | Your own keys, Nous Portal, some subscriptions, or local models |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, Android; no hosted web app | Mac and Windows desktop apps and a terminal app; no phone app yet |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | About 29, including WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, iMessage and Teams | More than 20, including Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Teams and iMessage |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes, as Markdown files on your disk | Yes, and it writes and improves its own skills |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Schedules, event triggers, webhooks | Schedules set up in plain language |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | A group that trusts each other can share one; it isn't built to separate users | Limited; separate user accounts aren't described |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Free; you pay your model provider | Free; optional Nous Portal at $0, $20, $100 or $200 a month |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Yes, entirely | Yes |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone | Open to everyone |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | There is no OpenClaw cloud; your model provider's policy applies | With your own keys only your provider sees your data; Nous Portal may train on prompts unless Privacy Mode is on |

Checked on November 18, 2026. Both projects ship new versions most weeks, so check the sources at
the end for anything that matters to you.

## The short answer

- **OpenClaw** is about reach. It connects to about 29 chat apps and has native apps for Mac,
  Windows, Linux, iPhone and Android. It has no paid tier at all.
- **Hermes Agent** is about one agent getting better. It writes and refines its own skills, keeps
  searchable memory, and lets you choose where its commands run. It has no phone app yet. The
  optional Nous Portal sells models and a hosted agent.
- **Both** run on your own machine by default and leave it to you to switch on isolation. Both use
  your own model keys, some subscriptions, or local models.

## Safety defaults

This is the difference people overlook. Per each project's own documentation:

- OpenClaw runs tools directly on the host by default. Sandboxing is optional, and command
  approvals don't prompt until you configure them.
- Hermes Agent runs commands on your machine by default and asks for approval when a command
  matches a list of dangerous patterns. Its docs say pattern matching can be got around by scripts.

Neither is unsafe if you set it up with care. Both expect you to do that setup.

## Choose OpenClaw if

- You want the most chat apps: about 29 channels, plus apps on every desktop and phone platform.
- You want software with no paid tier at all, run by a nonprofit.
- You want the largest community: about 395,000 GitHub stars.

## Choose Hermes Agent if

- You want one agent that teaches itself: it writes and refines its own skills and keeps searchable memory.
- You want wide model choice, including local models and several subscription sign-ins.
- You want to choose where commands run: locally, in Docker, over SSH or in a cloud sandbox.

## Where Casama fits

Casama is a third kind of open-source agent. Where these two are one agent on your computer, Casama
is a team of bots that each get their own sandboxed Linux machine, apart from your devices:

- Approvals are on from the start, for every kind of risky action, and payments always ask.
- A checkpoint is saved before destructive commands.
- There are native apps on phone and desktop, with push notifications.
- Workspaces, roles and group chats make it usable by more than one person.
- You can self-host it free, or use Casama Cloud, which has a free plan.

It has fewer chat apps than either (ten), and a far smaller community: it was first released in
November 2026.

## Worth knowing

**OpenClaw**

- Tools run on your own machine, and both the sandbox and approval prompts are off until you turn them on.
- The Register reported three high-impact security advisories in three days in February 2026, and malicious skills on its skill registry.
- It isn't designed for people who don't trust each other to share one agent.

**Hermes Agent**

- Commands run on your own machine by default, and its docs say the deny rules are pattern matching that scripts can get around.
- There is no phone app yet.
- It is still before version 1.0, with a very large backlog of open issues.

## Questions

### Which is easier to install?

Both install with one command and have desktop downloads. OpenClaw also has phone apps.

### Which has more users?

OpenClaw, by GitHub stars: about 395,000 against about 264,000 for Hermes Agent on the day we
checked.

### Can I run both?

Yes. They don't conflict, and some people run Hermes Agent for coding and OpenClaw for chat apps.

### Are they free?

Both are free and MIT-licensed. You pay your model provider. Hermes Agent's optional Nous Portal
has paid plans.

# Rakazo vs OpenBot vs MausBot vs Casama

Four open-source projects launched in 2026 with the same idea: AI teammates that keep working and have a computer to work on. Rakazo and Casama give every bot its own computer and can be fully self-hosted. OpenBot is built for company rollouts. MausBot is a free desktop app that reuses the AI subscriptions you already have.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/compare/rakazo-vs-openbot-vs-mausbot

## Side by side

| | Casama | Rakazo | OpenBot | MausBot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0); a separate `ee/` folder has its own licence | Apache-2.0 | MIT app; it needs CopilotKit Intelligence, which is licensed separately | Apache-2.0, with a source-available `enterprise/` folder |
| Where it runs | Your own server, Mac or Linux computer, or Casama Cloud | Your own server, a desktop app, or Rakazo's cloud | Your Mac or Windows desktop, or your own server or Kubernetes; hosted is early access | Your desktop, your own server, or MausBot Cloud |
| A computer for the agent | Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux computer; you can watch it live and take over | Each bot has its own container or cloud computer | A container per person; a bot can be given its own | Your machine by default; a cloud computer per bot on paid Cloud plans |
| Asks before risky steps | Yes. Rules per action, risky steps wait for your OK, and a checkpoint is saved before destructive commands | Yes: an Ask mode, or an Auto mode where a model decides when to ask | Yes: admin policies block, allow or require approval | Allow and Deny cards; the vendor says not every action is guaranteed to pause |
| Choice of AI model | Any provider, a ChatGPT plan or local models when self-hosted; Casama picks on Cloud | Your own keys, a ChatGPT plan, local models, or Rakazo credits at the provider's price | Your own keys or subscriptions, or any OpenAI-style endpoint | None included: it drives AI tools you're already signed in to, or API keys |
| Apps | iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, web | Web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, Android | Mac and Windows; phone, web, Slack and Teams are early access | Mac, Windows, Linux (beta); phone apps are handed out through Discord |
| Chat apps | Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Discord | Slack and Teams; iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram only when self-hosted | Slack and Teams, both early access | Slack, on paid plans |
| Memory | Yes, and you can read and edit it | Yes, per bot, and bots can share what they learn | Yes | Basic, per bot |
| Starts on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events, check-ins | Schedules, email, webhooks, GitHub events, watched changes | Schedules, at most every 15 minutes, up to 20 | Schedules, webhooks, app events |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, extra seats | Organizations, spaces and group chats; roles for people aren't described | Yes: roles, single sign-on, audit export and spend limits, on the paid edition | A paid Team plan, for up to 50 people |
| Price | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: Free, $15, $49 or $99 a month, credits included | Self-hosted: free. Cloud: $15, $49 or $99 a month, or credits from $20 | Free for personal use; Business up to $29 per active user a month | Desktop app: free. Cloud: $15, $49 or $99 a month; Team $40 for two people |
| Free to start | Yes: a free Cloud plan, and self-hosting is free | Self-hosting is free; hosted plans have a 7-day trial | Yes, for one person on their own laptop | Yes, the desktop app |
| Who can use it | Open to everyone | Open to everyone | The desktop app is open; the other apps are by request | Open to everyone |
| Training on your data | Not used to train models | Not stated either way | Not stated for OpenBot | Not stated |

Checked on November 18, 2026. We make Casama, so read our column with that in mind; every other
column has its sources at the end.

## Which one is for you

| If you want | Look at |
|---|---|
| Every bot on its own computer, self-hosted or hosted, under one open licence | Rakazo or Casama |
| A free hosted plan | Casama |
| Hosted model usage at the provider's price | Rakazo |
| Company controls: roles, single sign-on, audit export, Kubernetes | OpenBot |
| To reuse a Claude Code, Codex or Grok subscription on your desktop | MausBot |
| Phone apps in the stores today | Rakazo or Casama |
| Telegram, WhatsApp or iMessage | Casama; Rakazo when self-hosted |
| Nothing that needs a separate licence to run | Rakazo or Casama |

## Licences, in plain words

- **Rakazo**: Apache-2.0.
- **Casama**: AGPL-3.0 (SDKs and CLI Apache-2.0), with a separate `ee/` folder for a few enterprise features. It builds and
  runs without that folder.
- **MausBot**: Apache-2.0, with a source-available `enterprise/` folder.
- **OpenBot**: the app is MIT, but it needs CopilotKit Intelligence, which is licensed separately:
  free for personal use on a laptop, paid for production.

## Where each one runs a bot

- **Rakazo**: its own container per bot when self-hosted, or a cloud computer on hosted plans.
- **Casama**: its own sandboxed Linux machine per bot, self-hosted or on Casama Cloud.
- **OpenBot**: a container per person by default; a bot can be marked isolated to get its own.
- **MausBot**: your own machine by default; a cloud computer per bot on paid Cloud plans.

## Choose Rakazo if

- You want hosted model usage at the provider's price with no markup.
- You want a wide choice of sandbox providers for bot computers when self-hosting.
- You want every way to run it (self-hosted, desktop, hosted) from one project.

## Choose OpenBot if

- You are rolling AI coworkers out across a company and need roles, single sign-on, audit export and spend limits.
- You want to deploy inside your own cloud with Kubernetes.
- You want to plug in agents you built yourself.

## Choose MausBot if

- You already pay for Claude Code, Codex or Grok and want to reuse those sign-ins with no markup.
- You want a free desktop app that runs bots on your own computer.
- You want many cloud computer hours for the price.

## Choose Casama if

- You want a free hosted plan, with credits included in every paid plan.
- You want ten chat apps, including Telegram, WhatsApp and iMessage.
- You want workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, and extra seats.
- You want a checkpoint saved before destructive commands and budgets per bot.
- You want a self-hosted server your phone can reach with no domain.

## Worth knowing

**Rakazo**

- It is young: the repository was created in August 2026 and it is before version 1.0.
- iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram work only when self-hosted.
- The entry hosted plan has 25 computer hours a month.

**OpenBot**

- The MIT app can't run without CopilotKit Intelligence, which needs a paid licence for production.
- Only the Mac and Windows desktop apps are generally available.
- An independent review of version 1.0.2 found the default policy allows every action.

**MausBot**

- The vendor itself says approvals aren't guaranteed to pause every action.
- Slack is the only chat app, and only on paid plans.
- Free bots stop when your computer is off, and the phone apps aren't in the stores.

**Casama**

- It is the newest of the four: first released in November 2026, with a small community.
- On Casama Cloud, model usage is paid from credits at Casama's rates, not at the provider's price.
- Choosing your own model is for self-hosted servers. On Casama Cloud, Casama picks.

## Questions

### Are all four free to self-host?

Rakazo, MausBot's desktop app and Casama are. OpenBot is free for one person on their own laptop.

### Which has the most GitHub stars?

On the day we checked: MausBot about 24,700, OpenBot about 12,700, Rakazo about 9,000. Casama had
just been published.

### Do the hosted plans cost the same?

Rakazo, MausBot Cloud and Casama Cloud all use $15, $49 and $99 a month. What each includes
differs: computer hours, model usage, seats.

- Rakazo (checked 2026-11-18): https://api.github.com/repos/elie222/rakazo, https://rakazo.com, https://rakazo.com/docs/self-host/, https://rakazo.com/docs/approvals/, https://rakazo.com/docs/groups/, https://rakazo.com/pricing/, https://rakazo.com/privacy/
- OpenBot (checked 2026-11-18): https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot, https://open.bot/pricing, https://open.bot, https://www.copilotkit.ai/privacy-policy
- MausBot (checked 2026-11-18): https://github.com/milind-soni/OpenMausBot, https://www.mausbot.com/, https://www.mausbot.com/pricing, https://www.mausbot.com/privacy

More: [Rakazo](https://casama.ai/alternatives/rakazo), [OpenBot](https://casama.ai/alternatives/openbot) and
[MausBot](https://casama.ai/alternatives/mausbot) alternatives.

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# Contact us

The fastest answer is usually Casama Help, which knows our docs. For anything else, write to the address below that fits and a person will reply by email.

Updated 2026-11-19. Page: https://casama.ai/contact

## Get an answer now

- **Casama Help** answers questions about Casama straight away, from our docs. Ask it on the
  [help page](https://casama.ai/help) or with the **Questions** button at the bottom of any page.
- **Signed in?** Open **Settings → Help & support** in the app. There, Casama Help can also check
  your plan, purchases, usage and connected apps, and hand your problem to our support team with one
  tap.
- **Is something down?** [status.casama.ai](https://status.casama.ai) shows whether the API, web
  app, sign-in and docs are working right now.

  [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@casama.ai) and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/user/casamaai/).

These are for news and conversation. For anything about your account, use support below: we won't

# Delete your account

You can delete your Casama account and its data at any time, from any Casama app or by email. Here is how, what is deleted and when, and the little we have to keep.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/delete-account

## Before you delete

- **Cancel any paid plan first.** Deleting your account doesn't cancel a subscription bought in the
  App Store or Google Play, because Apple and Google bill it. Cancel it in **Settings → Apple ID →
  Subscriptions** on your iPhone, or in **Play Store → Payments & subscriptions** on Android. For a
  plan bought on the web or in the desktop app, open **Settings → Billing → Manage Subscription**.
- **Keep a copy if you want one.** Open **Settings → Privacy → Export My Data** for a ZIP of
  everything you can see. Download files and pages you want to keep from the Library.
- **Shared workspaces.** A workspace where you are the only owner is deleted with your account,
  even if other people use it. If it should stay, [write to us](mailto:support@casama.ai) first.

## Delete it in the app

This works the same in the iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows and Linux apps, and in the web app
at [app.casama.ai](https://app.casama.ai):

1. Sign in and open **Settings → Privacy**.
2. Under **Danger Zone**, tap **Delete My Account**.
3. Type your email address to confirm.

You are signed out everywhere at once, and the app shows the date your data will be erased. From
the command line, `casama account delete --confirm you@example.com` does the same.

## Delete it without the app

If you no longer have the app or can't sign in, email
[privacy@casama.ai](mailto:privacy@casama.ai) from the address on your Casama account, with the
subject "Delete my account". We may ask you to confirm it's you, then delete the account the same
way and tell you when it's done. We aim to reply within 30 days.

## What is deleted, and when

| What | When |
|---|---|
| Your sign-ins on every device, push notifications to your devices, and device data you shared (calendar, health summaries, places and the like) | Right away |
| Your account and profile | After a 7-day grace period |
| Every workspace where you are the only owner, with its bots, chats, memories, files, pages, routines and computers (including computer snapshots) | After the grace period |
| Your membership in workspaces that have another owner | After the grace period; those workspaces and their data stay |
| Your usage analytics | With your account |
| Encrypted backup copies | 14 days after the account is erased |

## What we keep

- **Billing records**, such as invoices and payment records, for as long as tax and accounting laws
  require.
- Questions you asked Casama Help on our websites are never tied to you, so there is nothing to
  delete there.

Deleting your account doesn't delete what other people copied or downloaded from links you shared,
and doesn't stop a store subscription you didn't cancel.

## Self-hosted servers

If you use a Casama server that you or someone else runs, your data is on that server, not with
us. Delete your account in the app the same way, or ask whoever runs the server. See
[Privacy and security](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/privacy#delete-your-account) in the docs and
our [privacy policy](https://casama.ai/privacy) for the details.

# How can we help?

Search the questions people ask most, or ask Casama Help. It answers from our docs.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/help

## Getting started

### What is Casama?

Casama gives you AI teammates, called bots, that keep working after you close the chat. Each bot
has its own instructions, memory, skills and a sandboxed Linux computer. It can research, write,
code, browse and run tasks on a schedule, and it asks before doing anything risky.

You can use it on Casama Cloud, the hosted service, or run the whole thing on your own server for
free. See [What is Casama](https://docs.casama.ai/introduction).

### How is Casama different from a chat assistant?

A chat assistant answers in a text box while you watch. A Casama bot has its own computer, your
tools, a memory and a schedule, so it does the work itself: fills in the form, drafts the email,
builds the page, and comes back when it's done or needs you.

It works on schedules and triggers when you're not there, reaches out first with a morning brief
and suggestions, uses your tools through connections, and asks you before risky steps. What it
makes is kept in the [Library](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/library). You can run it yourself, on any model.

### What can my first bot do on day one?

The first time you sign in, Casama asks what bots should call you, then makes a workspace named
after you and a personal bot called Casama, and opens its chat. On Casama Cloud the bot already has
a model, so you can give it work straight away. The chat starts with tiles to **Connect your apps**
and a few starter requests you can tap.

It can use its computer to research, write, code and keep files, make pages and documents, and set
up reminders and routines from a plain request such as "Remind me in 20 minutes to call Ana". Its
check-ins are on: each morning it sends a brief, and during the day it offers suggestions you
accept or dismiss. See [Your first bot](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/bots#your-first-bot).

### Which devices can I use it on?

There are apps for iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows and Linux, and a web app at
[app.casama.ai](https://app.casama.ai). The `casama` CLI works in the terminal and in scripts:
install it with `brew install stackwares/tap/casama` or download it from the
[releases page](https://github.com/stackwares/casama/releases).

You can also reach your bots from chat apps such as Slack, Telegram and WhatsApp, and from AI
coding tools over MCP. A few things need the desktop app: signing in with a ChatGPT plan, lending
your own computer to bots, and iMessage, which needs a Mac. See [Quick start](https://docs.casama.ai/quick-start).

### Should I get the Mac app from the website or the Mac App Store?

Get it from the website ([casama.ai/download](https://casama.ai/download)) unless you prefer the
App Store. The website version can do everything. Apple's App Store requires a sandbox, which
keeps an app inside its own box, so the App Store version leaves out the features that reach
outside the app:

| | From the website | Mac App Store |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat, bots, voice, widgets, notifications | Yes | Yes |
| Let bots use your Mac (terminal, files, browser, desktop apps) | Yes | No |
| Coding agents and local MCP servers on your Mac | Yes | No |
| Run your own Casama server on this Mac (**Run on This Mac**) | Yes | No |
| Quick ask reads the front window and your selection | Yes | No |
| Watch folders for new files | Yes | No |
| Updates | The app updates itself | Through the App Store |
| How you pay | Web checkout | In-app purchase (in the US, a web checkout link too) |

Your account, bots and chats live on the server, so you can switch later: install the other
version and sign in. A plan you bought in one version stays with the store you bought it in. To
manage or cancel it, go back to that store (see [Where do I pay?](https://docs.casama.ai/faq#where-do-i-pay)).

### Which languages does Casama support?

The apps are in English only for now.

### Do I need technical skills?

Not for Casama Cloud. Sign in with Google, Apple or your email and ask a bot for what you need in
plain words. It sets up its own routines when you ask, and most apps connect with one sign-in.
Connecting some chat apps means pasting keys from that app's developer settings.

Self-hosting takes one command in a terminal. On a Mac or Linux computer, the desktop app can also
run a server for you with no terminal: start Docker Desktop, then choose **Run Casama on This
Computer** on the sign-in screen. See [Quick start](https://docs.casama.ai/quick-start).

### Is Casama open source?

Yes. The product (server, worker, agent and apps) is licensed under AGPL-3.0,
and the SDKs, CLI, MCP server, plugin kit, examples and these docs under Apache-2.0, so what you
build on Casama can use any license. The `ee/` folder (enterprise features such as SAML
single sign-on and audit-log export) is source-available under the Casama Enterprise
License. Running Casama, even for a business, has no license cost; if you change the product and
let others use it, you share your changes under AGPL-3.0 too. A commercial license is
available. The code is on
[GitHub](https://github.com/stackwares/casama). See [Open source](https://casama.ai/open-source)
and [LICENSING.md](https://github.com/stackwares/casama/blob/main/LICENSING.md).

### Why is Casama Cloud invite-only?

We're letting people in as we add capacity, so Casama stays fast for everyone who is in. Running
Casama on your own server is open to everyone, with no invite and no waitlist. See
[Getting an invite](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/getting-an-invite).

### How do I get an invite?

Join the waitlist at casama.ai/waitlist and we'll email you once, when it's your turn. Or ask
someone who uses Casama: every member has a few invites to share.

### I have an invite code. What now?

Go to casama.ai/waitlist and enter it with your email. Then sign in with that address. Google,
Apple and the email link all work, as long as it's the same address.

## Plans & billing

### Is it free?

Self-hosting is free, with no paywall or limits; you pay only your model provider and your server.
A local model costs nothing at all. [Casama Link](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/remote-access), which puts a server
on your own computer on your phone, is free too.

Casama Cloud, the hosted service, has a Free plan that doesn't end: $1 of credits every month, 3
bots and one cloud computer with 5 hours of computer time. Three paid plans add more. See
[Usage, budgets and plans](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage).

### What plans are there and what do they cost?

Casama Cloud has four plans:

- **Free**: $0. $1 of credits a month, 3 bots, 1 computer, 5 computer hours a month, 1 person,
  1 GB of Library storage.
- **Plus**: $15 a month or $150 a year. $5 of credits a month, 10 bots, 2 computers, 30 computer
  hours, 1 person, 10 GB.
- **Pro**: $49 a month or $490 a year. $15 of credits a month, unlimited bots, 5 computers, 100
  computer hours, 3 people, 50 GB.
- **Max**: $99 a month or $899 a year. $30 of credits a month, unlimited bots, 10 computers, 300
  computer hours, 10 people, 200 GB.

Plus, Pro and Max can also be paid by the week: $7.99, $19.99 and $39.99, with a quarter of the
monthly credits each week.

Bigger plans also get bigger computers. Plans can change, so **Settings → Billing** always shows
the current ones. See [Pricing](https://casama.ai/pricing) and [Plans](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#plans).

### What do credits pay for?

On Casama Cloud, a credit is a dollar. Credits pay for the things that cost money each time a bot
works: AI models, cloud computer time beyond your plan's hours, live calls, images and video,
read-aloud and dictation, apps connected through Casama's own connector account, and paid data
lookups, which always ask first and show the price.

A run that is waiting for your approval, or a computer that is asleep, costs nothing. A run that
fails because of Casama or a model provider doesn't cost model credits. A self-hosted server uses
no credits: you pay your providers directly.

Credits belong to the workspace. A month's included credits last until the end of the following
month, and credit packs bought on the web and rewards last 12 months. Credit packs bought in the
App Store or Google Play never expire. Credits that run out soonest are spent first.
See [Credits](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#credits).

### What happens when I run out of credits?

Bots stop starting new paid work and tell you why. Nothing is charged without you buying a credit
pack or changing plan. On a paid plan you can buy packs of $10 or $25 of credits. On the Free plan,
the paywall shows the paid plans.

Each plan also has a daily limit on what Casama Cloud spends for you in a day ($0.25 on Free, $5 on
Plus, $10 on Pro and $25 on Max), which resets at midnight UTC, and a number of computer hours a
month. Using up the hours stops only the bots' computers; chat keeps working on credits. When a workspace's balance drops under $1, its owners get a notification, at most once a
week. See [When a run hits a limit](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#when-a-run-hits-a-limit).

### Can I limit what a bot spends?

Yes. Every bot has a budget per run ($1 by default) and per day ($10 by default). When a run
reaches its budget it stops and tells you. The **Usage** screen shows spend by bot, by model, by day
and by where the work came from, and **Settings > Show usage on replies** puts each reply's cost
under it. See [Bot budgets](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#bot-budgets).

### Is there a free trial?

Pro is free for 7 days, once per person, if you've never had a subscription. During the trial the
workspace gets $2 of credits and 10 computer hours; the first payment tops the month up to $15.

Once per person means once per email inbox, so accounts on the same inbox share the trial, and
deleting an account and signing up again doesn't start it over. See [Plans](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#plans).

### Can I add people to my workspace?

Pro includes 3 people and Max includes 10. On the web, Pro and Max can add more people at $12 a
month each ($120 a year). Free and Plus are for one person, the owner, so inviting someone needs
Pro or Max. See [Workspaces and teams](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/workspaces).

### Where do I pay?

It depends on where you use the app. On iPhone, iPad and the Mac App Store app you pay by in-app
purchase, and in the US there's a web checkout link too. On Android you pay through Google Play. On
the web, Windows, Linux and the Mac app from the web you use the web checkout.

Credit packs cost their face value on the web, and a little more in the App Store and Google Play,
because the stores keep a share. Card details are handled by Apple, Google or Dodo Payments; Casama
never sees your card number. See [Where you can buy](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#where-you-can-buy).

### How do I cancel?

Open **Settings → Billing** and tap **Manage Subscription**. A subscription bought in a store is
managed and cancelled in that store: on iPhone in **Settings > Apple ID > Subscriptions**, and on
Android in **Play Store > Payments & subscriptions**.

Cancelling a store subscription keeps access until the end of the paid period. See
[Usage, budgets and plans](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#where-you-can-buy).

### Can I get a refund?

App Store purchases are refunded by Apple, at [reportaproblem.apple.com](https://reportaproblem.apple.com).
Google Play purchases are refunded by Google, under **Play Store > Payments & subscriptions** or
on Google's refund request page. For purchases on the web or the desktop app, email
[billing@casama.ai](mailto:billing@casama.ai).

A refund ends the plan for the period it paid for and takes back the credits that plan added that
month. A refunded credit pack takes its credits back.

### What happens if I downgrade?

Your workspace keeps everything: bots, chats, files and memories. Every bot you already have keeps
working on the new plan's credits, even when you have more bots than the plan includes. You can't
add another bot or bring back an archived one until you're under the plan's number or upgrade. Only
the new plan's number of cloud computers start, oldest first, and check-ins are limited to the
plan's number of bots in the same way. See
[Usage, budgets and plans](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage).

## Account & data

### Who can see my data?

On Casama Cloud, your chats, memories and files are used to run Casama for you. In a shared
workspace, members see content according to their roles. Your About you details, the facts bots
learn about you and your device data stay private to you. Every table uses row-level security, so
one workspace can't read another's data, and workspace owners can encrypt content at rest.

On a self-hosted server, only people with access to your server can see your data, and Casama
doesn't receive it. The server sends no telemetry unless its owner turns it on. The official apps
connected to your server send only crash reports and one anonymous daily ping. See
[Privacy and security](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/privacy).

### Is my data used to train AI models?

No. Your chats, memories and files are used to run Casama for you and for nothing else. We don't
sell data or show ads, and your keys never reach the model.

To answer you, a bot sends the conversation and the context it needs to the model that runs it.
Model providers have their own policies about the data they receive. A local model keeps it on
your machine. See [Privacy Policy](https://casama.ai/privacy).

### Where is my data stored?

On Casama Cloud, the database and sign-in run on Casama's own servers, with Cloudflare for
delivery, file storage and protection from attacks. Model requests go through OpenRouter, and
live calls and read-aloud through Google. Casama is based in the Philippines, and some providers
process data in other countries, including the United States. Encrypted backups are kept for 14
days.

On a self-hosted server, your data stays on your server. See
[Privacy Policy](https://casama.ai/privacy).

### How do I export my data?

Open **Settings → Privacy** and tap **Export My Data**, or run `casama account export`. You get a
ZIP of JSON files with everything you can see: bots, chats, memories, skills, routines, usage and
more. Secrets and keys appear by name only.

The export doesn't include what bots made in the Library; open or download those from the
Library. A single chat can be exported as Markdown or JSON. See
[Export your data](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/privacy#export-your-data).

### How do I delete my account?

Open **Settings → Privacy**, and under **Danger Zone** tap **Delete My Account**, then type your
email to confirm. You're signed out everywhere at once, and the app shows the date your data will
be erased. On Casama Cloud that's after a 7-day grace period.

A workspace where you're the only owner is deleted with your account, even if other people use it.
The app has no screen for making someone else an owner yet, so ask for help first if the workspace
should stay. See [Delete your account](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/privacy#delete-your-account), and
[casama.ai/delete-account](https://casama.ai/delete-account) for deleting without the app.

### Does the model see my passwords and API keys?

No. Secrets live in a vault and are filled in at the moment a tool uses them, inside the computer or
the request. They're redacted from logs and never put into the model's input.

### How do I keep my account secure?

Turn on two-step sign-in with an authenticator app, add a passkey to sign in with Face ID, a
fingerprint or your screen lock, and turn on the app lock so Casama asks you to unlock it when it
opens. With **Confirm risky actions** on (the default), Casama also asks you to unlock again before
things like deleting your account or allowing a high-risk request. See
[Two-step sign-in](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/privacy#two-step-sign-in).

## Bots, apps & chat apps

### Which models can I use?

On Casama Cloud, Casama picks and runs the models for you, so you don't need a key. Models are
paid from your credits.

On your own server, use any model you have a key for: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, OpenRouter, or
any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio and others). Each bot picks its own model,
with fallbacks. See [Bots and models](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/bots).

### Can I use my ChatGPT plan?

Yes, on a self-hosted server. In the desktop app, open **Settings** → **Model keys** and choose
**Continue with ChatGPT**, or run `casama credential chatgpt` in the CLI. Bots' model calls then
count toward your plan's limits, and only you can use it. Casama Cloud doesn't offer it. See
[Connect a ChatGPT plan](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/bots#connect-a-chatgpt-plan).

### Can I run it fully offline or with local models?

You can run the server on your own network and use a local model through an OpenAI-compatible
endpoint, and calls to it are free. A local model can read pictures, and a local embedding model
keeps memory search on your machine too. Bots that browse the web or use cloud apps still need
internet access for those tasks. See [Local models](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/bots#local-models).

### How do bots use my other apps?

Through connections. Open **Settings** → **Integrations**, pick an app from the catalog, and connect
it with one sign-in or an API key. You can also add any MCP server, logins from a password manager
such as 1Password or Bitwarden, and plugins.

Every connection is stored encrypted, and each bot gets only the connections you give it. See
[Apps and connections](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/connections).

### Can a bot answer me in WhatsApp, Telegram or iMessage?

Yes. A bot can answer in Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage,
Microsoft Teams and Discord, and every conversation also shows up in the Casama app. Assign it a
Linear or Jira issue and it replies with a comment.

Each chat app is connected to one bot, and the bot answers only people on its **Allowed senders**
list. iMessage needs your Mac to be on with the desktop app running. Group chats on WhatsApp and
iMessage aren't supported, and approval buttons are in Telegram and Slack only. See
[Chat apps](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/chat-apps).

### Does a bot join my meetings?

No. Casama doesn't send a bot into your calls. A bot can work from the notes your meeting app
already takes, or from your calendar, and file a summary with decisions and action items. See
[Meeting notes](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/meetings).

### Can a bot work on a schedule?

Yes. A routine is work a bot does later on its own: once at a time you pick, on a repeating
schedule, or when something happens, such as a webhook, a meeting, a message or an event on your
phone. The quickest way is to ask in chat, for example "Every weekday at 9:00, summarize my
inbox". A routine can stop on a date or after a number of runs. See [Routines](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/routines).

### Does each bot get its own computer?

Every bot works on a sandboxed Linux computer with a shell, a home folder that persists between
chats and a browser that stays signed in. By default bots share the workspace's team computer, and
you can give a bot a private computer of its own, optionally with a desktop you can watch live.

A computer goes to sleep after 5 minutes with nothing to do and wakes with everything intact, and
an asleep computer costs nothing. On Casama Cloud, your plan sets how many computers you have and
how many hours they can run each month. See [Computers](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/computers).

### Can a bot use my own computer?

Yes, if you allow it. The desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux can lend your machine to the
bots you choose, to run commands and edit files in folders you share and use your desktop apps.
Everything a bot does on your machine shows on screen and can be stopped, and nothing is allowed
until you turn it on. See [Your own computer](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/companion).

### Can I talk to a bot?

Yes. You can dictate messages, have replies read aloud, call a bot live, and let a bot ring your
phone when something needs you. On Casama Cloud, voice is paid from your credits, with no keys to
add. On your own server, voice uses your workspace's provider keys. See
[Voice and calls](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/voice).

## Safety

### Can a bot do something I didn't want?

Every action has a risk level, and the bot's autonomy level decides which actions need your approval
first. Risky steps such as sending, booking, paying or deleting wait for your OK by default. Action
rules can allow an action (optionally within limits, such as recipients at one domain or a maximum
amount), always ask, or hand it to you to finish.

You can also set budgets and stop a run at any time. Destructive commands take a checkpoint first
(a recent one counts), so you can roll the computer back. Every run keeps a timeline of each step,
what it cost and why.
See [Autonomy and approvals](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/autonomy).

### Can a bot spend my money without asking?

No. Payments always ask, whatever the bot's autonomy setting. Model and computer costs are capped
by the bot's budgets. See [How Casama keeps bots safe](https://casama.ai/security).

### Does a bot follow instructions hidden in a web page?

Web pages, emails and files can contain text written to trick a bot. Casama marks that content as
untrusted and tells the bot never to follow instructions inside it. After a bot has read untrusted
content, actions that send data out ask for approval, even ones that normally wouldn't. See
[Untrusted content](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/autonomy#untrusted-content).

### What stops a bot's computer from reaching my network?

Computers reach the internet only through an egress proxy that blocks private and cloud-metadata
addresses, so a bot's computer can't reach your home or office network. Computers can't reach each
other or Casama's internal services. See [Computer providers](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/computers).

### What stops people from misusing Casama?

If a bot's reply is harmful, long-press it and choose **Report reply**. You can also report a bot,
a gallery item or a person, and block people so they can't invite you. Reports go to the people who
run the server, who can take content down or suspend a workspace.

Every public page and Library item has a link for viewers to report it, and after reports from
three different people it's hidden until someone looks at it. A workspace can make at most 20 new
public links a day. Casama Link addresses used for phishing or malware are taken down. See
[Report or block](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/privacy#report-or-block).

## Self-hosting

### Can I run it on my own server?

Yes. One command installs the whole stack with Docker on a Linux server, a home server or a Mac,
or you can start it from the Mac and Linux app. Self-hosting is free, with no limit on users, bots
or computers. See [Self-hosting](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/).

### What do I need to self-host?

A Linux server (or a Mac, for a trial) with Docker, and a domain if other people will connect. Plan
on 4 vCPU, 8 GB of RAM and 40 GB of disk for a few computers at once. See
[Self-hosting](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/) for sizing. To try it on your own Mac or Linux computer without a
terminal, use **Run on This Mac** (or **Run on This Computer**) on the desktop app's sign-in screen.
It walks you through Docker, the server, your account, a model and your phone.

### How do I upgrade?

Re-run `./install.sh`, or `casama selfhost upgrade`. Your settings and data are kept. See
[Operations](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/operations).

### Can I use a server on my own computer from my phone?

Yes. [Casama Link](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/remote-access) gives a server installed with `--local` an address
like `https://k7qm2xfd9abc.casama.link`, with no domain and no open ports. Your phone signs in by
scanning a QR code, and notifications reach it like any other app's. Phone traffic goes through
Cloudflare to your computer, never through Casama's servers. It's free on every plan, including
Free. Watching a bot's computer live while you're away from home comes with Plus and up.

### Can I use Casama Cloud computers from my own server?

Yes, with [Casama Link](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/casama-link). Computer time and model calls are paid from the cloud
workspace's credits, and your bots, chats and data stay on your server. See
[Cloud computers and credits](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/casama-link-cloud).

### Can I move between Casama Cloud and my own server?

Yes. Your workspace exports in full, and bots, skills and routines can be shared as files and
packs. See [Templates, sharing and import](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/sharing).

## Casama Link & Pages

### What is Casama Link?

Casama Link connects a Casama server you run yourself to a Casama Cloud workspace. It has two
parts, and you can use either or both. Remote access gives your server an address your phone can
reach, sign-in by scanning a code, and notifications in the store apps. Cloud computers and credits
let your bots use Casama Cloud's computers and models.

Your bots, chats, memory and files stay on your server either way. See
[Casama Link](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/casama-link).

### Is Casama Link free?

Remote access is free on every plan: the address, sign-in by QR code and notifications. Live video
of a bot's computer away from the computer that runs the server comes with Plus and up; on Free you
see a screenshot about once a second. Free and Plus link one server, Pro three and Max ten.

Cloud computers and model calls are billed to the cloud workspace's credits. See
[Servers per plan](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/remote-access#servers-per-plan).

### What is a page?

A page is a small web page a bot publishes for you: a report, a dashboard, a tracker, a site or a
game. Ask for one when an answer is better as something to look at, keep, play or share than as a
chat message. Pages open in your browser, stay private until you share them, can refresh
themselves on a schedule, and are kept in the Library. See [Pages](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/pages).

### How do I share something a bot made?

Open it in the Library and, under **Who Can See It**, choose **Only me**, **Workspace** or
**Anyone with the link**. A public link opens for anyone without signing in, and is hidden from
search engines. On Casama Cloud, shared pages open at `share.casama.page`.

To take a link back, set it to **Only me** or **Workspace**; the old link stops working, and making
it public again gives a new one. See [Share what bots make](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/sharing#share-what-bots-make).

## Building on Casama

### Is there an API?

Yes. Everything the apps do goes through a documented HTTP API, with a CLI and SDKs for TypeScript
and Dart. See [HTTP API](https://docs.casama.ai/develop/api) and the [API reference](https://docs.casama.ai/api/).

### Can I extend what bots can do?

Yes: connect MCP servers, write [plugins](https://docs.casama.ai/develop/plugins) (skills plus tool servers), share whole
bots and their routines as [packs](https://docs.casama.ai/develop/packs), share [bot templates](https://docs.casama.ai/develop/bot-templates),
or call other agents over [A2A](https://docs.casama.ai/develop/a2a).

### Can my coding agent learn Casama?

Yes. Give it the agent kit (skills for plugins, the API and more) and the docs MCP server, or point
it at [llms.txt](https://docs.casama.ai/llms.txt). No account is needed. See
[Build with AI agents](https://docs.casama.ai/develop/agents).

### Can a bot hand work to a coding agent?

Yes. A bot can hand a coding task to a coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, and
report back with a summary and the files that changed. The agent can run on your own computer with
your own sign-ins, on the bot's computer, or as one of Cursor's cloud agents. See
[Coding agents](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/coding-agents).

### How do I contribute?

Read [Contribute to Casama](https://docs.casama.ai/develop/contributing), and
[How Casama is built](https://docs.casama.ai/develop/architecture) for a map of the code. Bug reports, docs fixes and
code are all welcome.

## Getting help

### How do I get help in the app?

Open **Settings > Help & support**. On Casama Cloud, **Casama Help** answers straight away: it
knows these guides and can check your account and the workspace you have open: your plan and its
limits, purchases, this month's usage, credit history, connected apps and chat channels, invites,
and a bot's settings, routines and recent errors. It sees what the app would show you and never
reads your chats. Answers can link straight to the screen or store page you need.
When a person should take over, it writes up the problem and you send it to our support team with
one tap; we reply by email. You can also choose **Contact support** there at any time.

The same page shows your **support IDs**. Your workspace ID is also your purchase ID in the App
Store and Google Play, so share it if we ask about a purchase.

### Is Casama Cloud down?

[status.casama.ai](https://status.casama.ai) shows whether the API, web app, sign-in and docs are
working right now, with 90 days of uptime and a note when we know about a problem. It runs outside
our servers, so it stays up when they don't. If the app can't reach Casama Cloud, the bar at the
top has a **Status** button that opens it. For a self-hosted server, see
[Troubleshooting](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/troubleshooting).

### How do I reach the Casama team?

| For                              | Email                                         |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Anything else, or not sure       | [hello@casama.ai](mailto:hello@casama.ai)       |
| Help with the apps or your account | [support@casama.ai](mailto:support@casama.ai) |
| Plans, invoices and refunds      | [billing@casama.ai](mailto:billing@casama.ai)   |
| Your data and privacy requests   | [privacy@casama.ai](mailto:privacy@casama.ai)   |
| Security issues                  | [security@casama.ai](mailto:security@casama.ai) (see `SECURITY.md`) |

All of them are on the [contact page](https://casama.ai/contact).

Still stuck? Email support@casama.ai. Signed up? Open Help & support in the app for account help.

# AI agent vs chatbot: what's the difference?

A chatbot answers in a text box, and then you do the work. An AI agent has tools, a place to work, a memory and a schedule, so it does the work itself and comes back when it is done or needs you.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/learn/ai-agent-vs-chatbot

## Side by side

| | Chatbot | AI agent |
|---|---|---|
| What you get | An answer or a draft | A finished task |
| Who does the clicking | You | The agent |
| Tools | Usually none, or a web search | Browser, files, shell, your connected apps |
| Where it works | Inside the chat | On a computer: yours, or one of its own |
| Length of a task | One reply | Many steps, minutes to hours |
| When it works | When you type | Also on schedules and triggers |
| Memory | The current chat | Facts and preferences kept across chats |
| Risk | It can be wrong | It can be wrong and act on it |
| Cost | Per message | Per step, so longer tasks cost more |

## The same request, twice

**"Find three hotels in Lisbon under €150 for the first weekend of May, near the tram."**

A chatbot gives you a list from what it knows, which may be out of date, and you check each one.

An agent opens the booking sites, sets the dates, filters by price, checks the map, and returns
three options with live prices and links. If you say "book the second one", it fills in the form
and stops for your approval before paying.

## When a chatbot is enough

- You want an explanation, an idea or a first draft.
- The task is one step.
- Nothing needs to be looked up live or done in another app.

## When you want an agent

- The task has several steps across sites or apps.
- It repeats: every morning, every Monday, every time an email arrives.
- It should carry on while you do something else.
- It needs to remember how you like things done.

## What changes when software can act

Because an agent acts, the questions to ask are different from the ones you'd ask of a chatbot:

- **What can it touch?** An agent on its own sandboxed computer can't reach your files. One that
  runs on your laptop can.
- **What does it ask first?** Look for approvals before sending, paying and deleting.
- **Can you see what it did?** A step-by-step record lets you check its work.
- **Can you undo it?** Checkpoints or backups turn a mistake into an inconvenience.
- **What stops a runaway task?** Budgets and limits on repeated failures.

## How Casama handles it

A Casama bot has its own computer, your tools, a memory and a schedule. You decide what each bot
may do, action by action: allow, allow within limits, or ask first. Risky steps such as sending,
booking, paying or deleting wait for your OK, and the computer is saved first so you can roll back.
[How Casama keeps bots safe](https://casama.ai/security) has the details.

## Related questions

- [What is an AI agent?](https://casama.ai/learn/what-is-an-ai-agent)
- [Which AI agents ask before they act?](https://casama.ai/learn/which-ai-agents-ask-before-they-act)

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# Are there free AI agents?

Yes, in two ways. Open-source agents are free to run on your own computer, and some hosted agents have a free plan. What is rarely free is the AI model behind the agent, unless you run a local one. Here is what each kind of "free" includes.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/learn/are-there-free-ai-agents

## Three things an agent costs

| Cost | What it is | When it's free |
|---|---|---|
| The software | The agent itself | Open-source agents; free plans of hosted ones |
| The model | Each step is a call to an AI model | Local models; free credits; small free allowances |
| The computer | Somewhere for the agent to work | Your own machine; included hours on a free plan |

An agent is only free for you if all three are.

## Free option 1: open source on your own machine

Install an open-source agent on a computer you already own. The software costs nothing and so does
the computer.

- **With a local model**, the whole thing is free. Expect it to be slower and weaker on long tasks
  than the best hosted models.
- **With your own API key**, you pay the model provider for what you use. Light use is often a few
  dollars a month.
- **With a subscription you already have**, such as a ChatGPT plan, some agents can sign in with it
  so there is no new bill.

Our [comparison of open-source AI agents](https://casama.ai/compare/best-open-source-ai-agents) lists which do what.

## Free option 2: a hosted free plan

Some hosted agents have a free tier. Read what it includes:

- **How much usage.** Often a small monthly amount of credits or tasks.
- **Whether a card is needed** to sign up.
- **What happens at the limit.** It should stop, not start charging.
- **Whether your data is used for training** on the free plan.

## What "free" usually leaves out

- Heavy use. An agent that works for hours a day will pass any free allowance.
- The strongest models.
- Team features.
- Live video of the agent's screen, long-running computers, large storage.

## Free in Casama

- **Self-hosted Casama is free**, with no limit on users or bots. Use local models through Ollama
  and nothing is billed by anyone. Local model calls are recorded at $0.
- **Casama Cloud's Free plan** has $1 of credits every month, 3 bots and one cloud computer with 5
  hours of computer time. It doesn't expire. When credits run out, bots stop starting paid work
  until the next month; nothing is charged.
- **Your data isn't used for training** on any plan.

Paid plans start at $15 a month. See [pricing](https://casama.ai/pricing).

## Questions

### What is the cheapest way to run an AI agent all day?

Your own always-on machine, an open-source agent, and a local model for routine work, with a
hosted model on your own key for the hard tasks.

### Do free plans include an agent with its own computer?

Some do, with limited hours. Casama's Free plan includes one cloud computer for 5 hours a month.

### Is a free AI agent safe?

Price doesn't tell you. Check what it asks before doing, and what happens to your data.

## Related questions

- [Self-hosted or hosted AI agent: which should I choose?](https://casama.ai/learn/self-hosted-or-hosted-ai-agent)
- [Can AI agents run on my own models?](https://casama.ai/learn/can-ai-agents-run-on-local-models)
- [How much does an AI agent cost a month?](https://casama.ai/learn/how-much-does-an-ai-agent-cost)

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# Can AI agents run on my own models?

Yes. An agent can use a model on your own computer through Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM, as long as the agent software accepts an OpenAI-style endpoint. It costs nothing per message and nothing leaves your network. The trade-off is skill on long, tool-heavy tasks.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/learn/can-ai-agents-run-on-local-models

## What "your own model" can mean

| Option | What it is | You pay |
|---|---|---|
| A local model | A model running on your machine or network through Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM | Hardware and electricity |
| Your own API key | You buy model usage straight from a provider | The provider's price, with no middleman |
| A plan you already have | Sign in with a subscription such as ChatGPT instead of a key | Your existing subscription |

All three need an agent that lets you choose the model. Many hosted agents don't: they run a fixed
model and bill you for it.

## What local models are good at

- **Privacy.** Prompts, files and results stay on your machine.
- **Cost.** No per-message charge, so routine work is free.
- **Simple, frequent jobs**: sorting, summarising, tagging, drafting short replies.
- **Embeddings** for memory and search.

## Where they fall short

- **Long tasks with many tools.** Agents call tools dozens of times in a row. Smaller models lose
  track sooner, pick the wrong tool more often and recover from errors less well.
- **Browsing and screenshots.** Reading a web page from an image needs a model with vision.
- **Speed.** Without a strong GPU, each step is slow, and a task has many steps.

## A setup that works

Most people who run local models don't use them for everything:

1. A local model for private or simple bots.
2. A hosted model, on your own key, for hard tasks.
3. A fallback: if the first model is unavailable, the bot uses the second.

## How to connect one

Start the model server, then give your agent its address. For Ollama on the same machine that is
usually `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`. Pull a model with tool support first, and a separate small
model for embeddings if the agent uses memory search.

## Local models in Casama

Self-hosted Casama accepts any OpenAI-style server: Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM or your own. Each bot
has a main model and fallbacks, so one bot can run locally while another uses a provider key.
Calls to a local model are recorded in Usage at $0. You can also use keys for Anthropic, OpenAI,
Google Gemini, xAI or OpenRouter, or sign in with a ChatGPT plan.

On Casama Cloud, Casama picks and runs the models for you. Choosing your own model is part of
[self-hosting](https://casama.ai/self-hosted), which is free.

## Questions

### Which local model should I use?

Pick the largest model with tool calling that your hardware runs at a usable speed, and test it on
a real task. The [bots and models guide](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/bots) has current advice.

### Does the bot's computer need a GPU?

No. The model runs wherever your model server is. The bot's computer only runs the tools.

### Can I mix local and hosted models?

Yes, per bot, with fallbacks.

## Related questions

- [How do I self-host an AI agent?](https://casama.ai/learn/how-to-self-host-an-ai-agent)
- [Self-hosted or hosted AI agent: which should I choose?](https://casama.ai/learn/self-hosted-or-hosted-ai-agent)
- [Which AI agents let you choose the model or use your own API keys?](https://casama.ai/learn/which-ai-agents-let-you-choose-the-model)

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# How do AI agents work?

An AI agent runs a loop. The model picks the next step, a tool carries it out, the model reads the result and picks again, until the task is done or it needs you.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/learn/how-do-ai-agents-work

## The loop

Every agent, whatever it is called, does roughly this:

1. **Read the task** and everything it knows: your request, its instructions, what it remembers.
2. **Pick one step**, such as "open this page" or "run this command".
3. **Use a tool** to carry out the step.
4. **Read what happened**: the page's content, the command's output, an error.
5. **Decide**: another step, a question for you, or a final answer.

One pass through the loop is a step. A simple task takes a handful. A research task can take
dozens. Each step is a call to an AI model, which is why long tasks cost more than a chat message.

*Diagram: A diagram of how an AI agent works. A goal enters a loop of three stages: plan, which picks one step; act, which uses tools on the agent's computer; and check, which reads the result. If the task is not done, the loop goes round again from plan. The agent leaves the loop in one of two ways: done, when the task is finished, or ask you, when it needs a decision or approval.*

An agent plans a step, acts with its tools, checks the result and repeats until it is done or needs you.

## The parts

| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| Model | Chooses each step. It doesn't act by itself; it asks for a tool to be used. |
| Tools | The things an agent can do: browse, run commands, read and write files, call your apps. |
| Workspace | Where tools run: your computer, a browser tab, or a computer of the agent's own. |
| Instructions | Who the agent is and how it should work. |
| Memory | Facts and preferences saved from earlier work and recalled when relevant. |
| Skills | Written how-tos for tasks it does often, loaded when needed. |
| Triggers | What starts a task without you: a schedule, an email, a webhook. |
| Guard rails | Approvals, budgets, step limits and sandboxing. |

## Why a place to work matters

A model can only produce text. To click a button it needs something that can click. Some agents
borrow your browser or your laptop, which is quick to set up but means the agent shares your files
and your sign-ins. Others give the agent a computer of its own in a sandbox, so its work is apart
from your devices, keeps going when you close your laptop, and can be rolled back.

## What keeps the loop in check

Left alone, a loop can go wrong in a few known ways. Each has a standard answer:

- **It does something you didn't want.** Approvals pause the loop before risky steps.
- **It repeats a failing step.** A loop guard stops repeated identical actions.
- **It runs up a bill.** Budgets per task and per day end the run at a limit.
- **A web page tells it what to do.** Content from outside is marked untrusted, and steps that
  send data out ask first.
- **The server restarts mid-task.** Durable runs pick up from the last finished step.

## How this looks in Casama

In Casama each task is a run with a timeline. You can open any run and see every step, the tool it
used, what it cost and why. A run stops at 40 steps or 30 minutes, at the bot's budget, or after
five failed steps in a row. Risky steps wait for approval, and a waiting run costs nothing.

## Related questions

- [What is an AI agent?](https://casama.ai/learn/what-is-an-ai-agent)
- [Why give an AI agent its own computer?](https://casama.ai/learn/why-give-an-ai-agent-its-own-computer)

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/
