# Open-source AI agents you can read, run and change

Casama is open source under AGPL-3.0. The server, the apps for every platform, the CLI and the SDKs are all in one public repository.

Updated 2026-11-19. Page: https://casama.ai/open-source

## What is open

Everything you need to run Casama for yourself or your team is in
[the repository](https://github.com/stackwares/casama):

- **The server**: the API, the worker that runs bots, and the sandbox that gives each bot a
  computer.
- **The apps**: iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux and web, from one codebase.
- **The CLI, the SDKs** for TypeScript and Dart, and an MCP server so other AI tools can talk to
  your bots.
- **The gallery**: skills, starter bots, routines, apps and looks, with a public catalog anyone can
  add to.

The licence is AGPL-3.0: use it, change it and run it, at work or at home. If you change Casama and
let other people use your version, you share your changes under the same licence. The SDKs, CLI,
MCP server and plugin kit are Apache-2.0, so whatever you build on Casama can use any licence.
One folder, `ee/`, holds
a few enterprise features under a separate licence. Casama builds and runs without it, and the
[licensing page](https://github.com/stackwares/casama/blob/main/LICENSING.md) says exactly what is
where.

## Why it matters for an AI agent

An agent acts for you. It reads your mail, signs in to your accounts and spends your money. That is
a lot to hand to software you can't inspect.

- **You can see what it does.** The rules that decide which actions ask first are code you can
  read, not a promise.
- **You choose the model.** Self-hosted bots use any provider, your own keys or a local model.
- **It can't be taken away.** If a vendor closes, changes its prices or leaves your country, a
  hosted agent goes with it. Your own copy keeps running, and your workspace exports in full.
- **Your data stays where you put it.** On your own server, chats, memory and files never leave
  your machine.

## What makes Casama different from other open-source agents

Most open-source agent projects are one of two things: a framework for developers to build agents
with, or a single assistant that runs in a terminal or a chat app on your own computer. Casama is a
finished product for people who don't write code, with a team of bots:

| | Casama |
|---|---|
| A computer per bot | Each bot gets its own sandboxed Linux machine, apart from your devices |
| Asking first | Rules per action; risky steps wait, and a checkpoint is saved before anything destructive |
| Real apps | Native apps on phone, tablet and desktop, with push notifications and live calls |
| Teams | Workspaces with roles, group chats with people and bots, shared spaces |
| Starting on its own | Schedules, webhooks, email, calendar events and check-ins |
| Hosted option | Casama Cloud, if you'd rather not run a server |

## Build on it

Everything the apps do goes through an open HTTP API. Plugins give bots new skills and tools from a
GitHub repository, and packs share whole bots with their routines. If you build with Claude Code,
Codex or Cursor, the [agent kit](https://docs.casama.ai/develop/agents) gives your coding agent
Casama's docs and API reference.

## Sponsor Casama

Self-hosting stays free, so the project is paid for by Casama Cloud and by sponsors. If you run
Casama yourself, [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/stackwares) is the simplest way to
give back, monthly or one time:

| Tier | What it gets you |
|---|---|
| $5 a month | A sponsor badge on your GitHub profile and our thanks |
| $25 a month | Your name in the README's sponsors list |
| $100 a month | Your team's name and link in the README and on this page |
| $500 a month | Your logo in the README and on this page, and a monthly call with the maintainers |

One-time sponsorships of $10, $50 or any amount you choose are welcome too. Sponsorships pay for
signed releases on every platform, security fixes, plugin and gallery reviews, and docs.

## Questions

### Is Casama free?

Self-hosting is free with no limit on users or bots. Casama Cloud has a free plan and paid plans
from $15 a month. See [pricing](https://casama.ai/pricing).

### Can I use it at work?

Yes. AGPL-3.0 allows commercial use, including running it for your business and your customers.
If you change Casama and offer your version to others, share those changes under AGPL-3.0. If
that doesn't suit your company, a commercial licence is available from hello@casama.ai.

### How can I support the project without writing code?

[Sponsor it on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/stackwares), use
[Casama Cloud](https://casama.ai/pricing), share a bot in the gallery, or tell people about it.

### How do I contribute?

Read the [contributing guide](https://github.com/stackwares/casama/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
Gallery items (skills, bots, routines) are the easiest place to start.

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# Casama pricing

Start free on Casama Cloud, or run the whole thing on your own server for nothing. Every paid plan includes credits each month, and credits are dollars.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/pricing

## Casama Cloud plans

- **Free**: $0. $1 of credits a month, 3 bots, 1, with 5 hours, Included Library, 1.
- **Plus**: $15 a month, or $150 a year. $5 of credits a month, 10 bots, 2, with 30 hours, 10 GB Library, 1.
- **Pro**: $49 a month, or $490 a year. $15 of credits a month, Unlimited bots, 5, with 100 hours, 50 GB Library, 3, then $12 each.
- **Max**: $99 a month, or $899 a year. $30 of credits a month, Unlimited bots, 10, with 300 hours, 200 GB Library, 10, then $12 each.

Pro starts with a 7-day free trial. Paying yearly costs less: $150 for Plus, $490 for Pro and $899
for Max. For a short project you can also pay by the week: $7.99 for Plus, $19.99 for Pro and
$39.99 for Max, with a week's share of the credits.

## What credits pay for

On Casama Cloud a credit is a dollar. Credits pay for the things that cost money each time a bot
works:

- **AI models.** Every question a bot puts to a model.
- **Cloud computer time** beyond the hours in your plan.
- **Live calls, images, video and read-aloud voices.**
- **Paid data lookups**, which always ask first and show the price.

Every plan includes credits each month. When a busy month needs more, paid plans can buy credit
packs. A bot that is waiting for your approval, or sleeping, costs nothing.

## You stay in charge of spending

Each bot has a budget per run ($1 by default) and per day ($10 by default). When a run reaches its
budget it stops and tells you. The Usage screen shows spend by bot, by model, by day and by where
the work came from, and each reply shows what it cost.

## Self-hosted: $0, forever

Casama is open source under AGPL-3.0. One command installs the whole stack with Docker on a VPS,
a home server or your laptop, and the Mac and Linux app can run a server for you with no terminal.

- No limit on users, bots or computers.
- Use any model: your own keys for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, xAI or OpenRouter, your
  ChatGPT plan, or local models through Ollama. You pay your providers directly, and local models
  cost nothing.
- Casama Link gives your server an address your phone can reach, free on every plan.

See [Run Casama on your own server](https://casama.ai/self-hosted).

[Read the self-hosting guide](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/)

## Questions

### Is there a free plan?

Yes. The Free plan has $1 of credits every month, 3 bots and one cloud computer with 5 hours of
computer time. It doesn't end.

### What happens when I run out of credits?

Bots stop starting new paid work and tell you why. Nothing is charged without you buying a credit
pack or changing plan.

### Can I add people?

Pro includes 3 seats and Max includes 10. More people cost $12 a month each. Plus and Free are for
one person.

### Do I pay for a run that waits for me?

No. A run that is waiting for your approval costs nothing while it waits.

### Can I move between Cloud and my own server?

Yes. Your workspace exports in full, and bots, skills and routines can be shared as files and
packs.

## Plans and billing questions

### Is it free?

Self-hosting is free, with no paywall or limits; you pay only your model provider and your server.
A local model costs nothing at all. [Casama Link](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/remote-access), which puts a server
on your own computer on your phone, is free too.

Casama Cloud, the hosted service, has a Free plan that doesn't end: $1 of credits every month, 3
bots and one cloud computer with 5 hours of computer time. Three paid plans add more. See
[Usage, budgets and plans](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage).

### What plans are there and what do they cost?

Casama Cloud has four plans:

- **Free**: $0. $1 of credits a month, 3 bots, 1 computer, 5 computer hours a month, 1 person,
  1 GB of Library storage.
- **Plus**: $15 a month or $150 a year. $5 of credits a month, 10 bots, 2 computers, 30 computer
  hours, 1 person, 10 GB.
- **Pro**: $49 a month or $490 a year. $15 of credits a month, unlimited bots, 5 computers, 100
  computer hours, 3 people, 50 GB.
- **Max**: $99 a month or $899 a year. $30 of credits a month, unlimited bots, 10 computers, 300
  computer hours, 10 people, 200 GB.

Plus, Pro and Max can also be paid by the week: $7.99, $19.99 and $39.99, with a quarter of the
monthly credits each week.

Bigger plans also get bigger computers. Plans can change, so **Settings → Billing** always shows
the current ones. See [Pricing](https://casama.ai/pricing) and [Plans](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#plans).

### What do credits pay for?

On Casama Cloud, a credit is a dollar. Credits pay for the things that cost money each time a bot
works: AI models, cloud computer time beyond your plan's hours, live calls, images and video,
read-aloud and dictation, apps connected through Casama's own connector account, and paid data
lookups, which always ask first and show the price.

A run that is waiting for your approval, or a computer that is asleep, costs nothing. A run that
fails because of Casama or a model provider doesn't cost model credits. A self-hosted server uses
no credits: you pay your providers directly.

Credits belong to the workspace. A month's included credits last until the end of the following
month, and credit packs bought on the web and rewards last 12 months. Credit packs bought in the
App Store or Google Play never expire. Credits that run out soonest are spent first.
See [Credits](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#credits).

### What happens when I run out of credits?

Bots stop starting new paid work and tell you why. Nothing is charged without you buying a credit
pack or changing plan. On a paid plan you can buy packs of $10 or $25 of credits. On the Free plan,
the paywall shows the paid plans.

Each plan also has a daily limit on what Casama Cloud spends for you in a day ($0.25 on Free, $5 on
Plus, $10 on Pro and $25 on Max), which resets at midnight UTC, and a number of computer hours a
month. Using up the hours stops only the bots' computers; chat keeps working on credits. When a workspace's balance drops under $1, its owners get a notification, at most once a
week. See [When a run hits a limit](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#when-a-run-hits-a-limit).

### Can I limit what a bot spends?

Yes. Every bot has a budget per run ($1 by default) and per day ($10 by default). When a run
reaches its budget it stops and tells you. The **Usage** screen shows spend by bot, by model, by day
and by where the work came from, and **Settings > Show usage on replies** puts each reply's cost
under it. See [Bot budgets](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#bot-budgets).

### Is there a free trial?

Pro is free for 7 days, once per person, if you've never had a subscription. During the trial the
workspace gets $2 of credits and 10 computer hours; the first payment tops the month up to $15.

Once per person means once per email inbox, so accounts on the same inbox share the trial, and
deleting an account and signing up again doesn't start it over. See [Plans](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#plans).

### Can I add people to my workspace?

Pro includes 3 people and Max includes 10. On the web, Pro and Max can add more people at $12 a
month each ($120 a year). Free and Plus are for one person, the owner, so inviting someone needs
Pro or Max. See [Workspaces and teams](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/workspaces).

### Where do I pay?

It depends on where you use the app. On iPhone, iPad and the Mac App Store app you pay by in-app
purchase, and in the US there's a web checkout link too. On Android you pay through Google Play. On
the web, Windows, Linux and the Mac app from the web you use the web checkout.

Credit packs cost their face value on the web, and a little more in the App Store and Google Play,
because the stores keep a share. Card details are handled by Apple, Google or Dodo Payments; Casama
never sees your card number. See [Where you can buy](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#where-you-can-buy).

### How do I cancel?

Open **Settings → Billing** and tap **Manage Subscription**. A subscription bought in a store is
managed and cancelled in that store: on iPhone in **Settings > Apple ID > Subscriptions**, and on
Android in **Play Store > Payments & subscriptions**.

Cancelling a store subscription keeps access until the end of the paid period. See
[Usage, budgets and plans](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage#where-you-can-buy).

### Can I get a refund?

App Store purchases are refunded by Apple, at [reportaproblem.apple.com](https://reportaproblem.apple.com).
Google Play purchases are refunded by Google, under **Play Store > Payments & subscriptions** or
on Google's refund request page. For purchases on the web or the desktop app, email
[billing@casama.ai](mailto:billing@casama.ai).

A refund ends the plan for the period it paid for and takes back the credits that plan added that
month. A refunded credit pack takes its credits back.

### What happens if I downgrade?

Your workspace keeps everything: bots, chats, files and memories. Every bot you already have keeps
working on the new plan's credits, even when you have more bots than the plan includes. You can't
add another bot or bring back an archived one until you're under the plan's number or upgrade. Only
the new plan's number of cloud computers start, oldest first, and check-ins are limited to the
plan's number of bots in the same way. See
[Usage, budgets and plans](https://docs.casama.ai/guide/usage).

More questions: https://casama.ai/help

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# How Casama keeps a bot from doing what you didn't want

A bot that can act can also act wrongly. Casama is built so the worst a bot can do is small, visible and reversible.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/security

## It asks before risky steps

Every tool a bot can use has a risk level: low, medium or high. Each bot has an autonomy setting
that decides what waits for you:

| Setting | The bot asks before |
|---|---|
| Ask before acting | Every action that changes something |
| Ask for risky actions (the default) | Sending email or chat messages, calling people, making a page public, deleting outside its workspace folder, paid data lookups, and anything you marked "always asks" |
| Act on its own | Nothing, except high-risk actions on your own computer |

Payments always ask, whatever the setting. A request shows the bot, the tool, its risk and exactly
what it wants to do. You can approve, deny, or allow that action from now on. A run that waits for
you costs nothing and survives a server restart.

## It works on a computer that isn't yours

Each bot has its own sandboxed Linux machine. It can't reach your devices or any file you didn't
share with it. You can watch the computer live and take control at any time.

Before a command that deletes data, Casama saves a checkpoint of the bot's computer, so you can put
the files back as they were.

## It never sees your passwords

Secrets don't reach the AI model. A bot uses a placeholder, and Casama fills in the real value only
when the request goes to a site that secret is allowed for. Logins can come from 1Password or
Bitwarden.

## It doesn't follow instructions hidden in a web page

Web pages, emails and files can contain text written to trick a bot. Casama marks that content as
untrusted and tells the bot never to follow instructions inside it. After a bot has read untrusted
content, actions that send data out ask for approval, even ones that normally wouldn't.

## It stops when it's stuck or over budget

- Each bot has a budget per run and per day. At the limit, the run stops and tells you.
- The same action with the same details isn't run a third time in one run.
- Five failed steps in a row end the run, so a confused bot doesn't spend your money retrying.

## Your data

- Your chats, memories and files are used to run Casama for you and for nothing else. They are not
  used to train AI models, sold, or used for ads.
- Each workspace is walled off from every other in the database, with a test that proves it.
- You can export everything and delete your account at any time. You can also turn on encryption
  for a workspace's content and set how long run history is kept.
- Sign-in supports two-step codes and passkeys, and the app can lock itself and ask for your face
  or fingerprint before risky actions.

If you want nothing to leave your own machine, [self-host Casama](https://casama.ai/self-hosted), which is free.

## Report a problem

Security reports go to security@casama.ai. The
[security policy](https://github.com/stackwares/casama/blob/main/SECURITY.md) explains what to
send and what to expect.

## Questions

### Can a bot spend my money without asking?

No. Payments always ask. Model and computer costs are capped by the bot's budgets.

### Can I see what a bot did?

Yes. Every run keeps a timeline of each step, what it cost and why.

### What if a bot deletes something?

Restore the checkpoint Casama saved before the command ran.

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# Self-hosted AI agents, on a server you own

Casama runs on your own hardware with one command. Your chats, memory and files stay on your machine, you choose the models, and it costs nothing.

Updated 2026-11-19. Page: https://casama.ai/self-hosted

## What you get

A self-hosted Casama is the full product, not a cut-down edition:

- **Bots with their own computers.** Each bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine with a shell,
  files and a browser. You can watch it live and take over.
- **Any model.** Bring keys for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, xAI or OpenRouter, sign in with
  your ChatGPT plan, or point a bot at a local model in Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM. Local models
  are recorded at $0.
- **Approvals.** Risky steps wait for your OK. You set the rules per bot and per action.
- **Routines.** Bots start on a schedule, on a webhook, on an email or a calendar event.
- **Apps everywhere.** The same apps for iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux and the web
  sign in to your server.
- **No limits.** As many users, bots and computers as your hardware can carry.

## Install it

You need a machine with Docker. To try it on your own computer:

```
git clone https://github.com/stackwares/casama && cd casama
./install.sh --local
```

For a server other people reach over the internet, point a domain at the machine first:

```
./install.sh --domain casama.example.com
```

The installer checks Docker, creates every secret, starts the stack and waits until it is healthy.
With Docker already installed it takes about 15 minutes, most of it building images. The
[quick start](https://docs.casama.ai/quick-start) walks through signing in and your first bot.

Prefer no terminal? The desktop app for Mac and Linux can run a server on the computer it is
installed on: choose **Run Casama on This Computer** on the sign-in screen.

## Use it from your phone

A server on a laptop or a home network normally can't be reached from outside. Casama Link fixes
that for free: your server gets its own `casama.link` address, with no domain, port forwarding or
VPN to set up. Scan a code with the Casama app to sign in, and notifications reach your phone like
any other app's. Your chats, memory and files stay on your server.

## Self-hosted or Casama Cloud?

| | Self-hosted | Casama Cloud |
|---|---|---|
| Price | Free | Free, then $15, $49 or $99 a month |
| Where your data lives | Your machine | Casama's servers |
| Models | Any provider, your ChatGPT plan, or local models | Casama picks and runs them |
| Model costs | You pay providers directly; local models are free | Paid from credits |
| Setup | One command and Docker | Sign in |
| Upkeep | You update and back up | Casama does |

You can also mix them: keep your server and let Casama Cloud run the bot computers and model calls
for it.

Self-hosting is free and stays free. If Casama earns a place on your server, you can
[sponsor the project on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/stackwares).

## Questions

### What hardware does it need?

One machine with Docker runs everything: the database, the API, the worker and the bots' computers.
The docs list the [requirements](https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/) and production advice.

### Is anything held back from the open-source edition?

The app is open source under AGPL-3.0. A separate `ee/` folder holds a few enterprise features under their own
licence; Casama builds and works without it.

### Can I run it with only local models?

Yes. Point a bot at an OpenAI-style endpoint such as Ollama. Nothing has to leave your network.

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# AI agents for small business

A small business needs more hands, not another dashboard. Give each Casama bot one job, a budget and a computer of its own, and keep the final say on anything that costs money or reaches a customer.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-agents-for-small-business

## What the bot does

- **Answers customers** from your help documents, around the clock.
- **Does the admin**: invoices, forms, data entry, chasing late payments.
- **Researches**: suppliers, competitors, prices, with sources.
- **Keeps the books tidy**: collects receipts, matches them, flags what's missing.
- **Reports**: a Monday summary of sales, support and what needs a decision.

## Where it stops to ask

- Refunds, payments and anything else that costs money.
- Messages to customers, until you allow routine ones.
- Anything outside the limits you set for that bot.

You set these rules per bot and per action. See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

1. Kelly, the support bot, answers 23 emails overnight. One $48 refund waits for the owner's OK.
2. Theo, the research bot, sends Monday's supplier price check with every source cited.
3. A new hire is added to the workspace and can use both bots, but can't change their rules.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. Create a workspace and invite your team. Pro includes 3 seats and Max includes 10.
2. Add one bot per job, from the built-in personas (Support, Sales, Ops, Researcher and others) or your own instructions.
3. Give each bot only the apps it needs.
4. Set a budget per run and per day for each bot. The Usage screen shows spend by bot and by person.

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## Questions

### How much does it cost for a team?

Pro is $49 a month with 3 seats, unlimited bots and $15 of credits. Extra people are $12 each. Self-hosting is free for any number of people.

### Can a bot spend money without approval?

No. Payments always ask.

### Do we need an IT person?

Not for Casama Cloud. Self-hosting needs someone comfortable with Docker.

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# An AI bookkeeping assistant that prepares the books and asks before paying

Bookkeeping is mostly matching one list against another. A Casama bot does the matching, sorts the expenses and shows you what is missing. It prepares the work for you or your accountant to check, and it never moves money without asking.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-bookkeeping-assistant

## What the bot does

- **Matches receipts to transactions.** By amount, date and merchant, with a note on how confident
  each match is.
- **Flags the gaps.** Transactions with no receipt, receipts with no transaction, and its best
  guess for each.
- **Sorts expenses.** Into categories, with recurring costs and simple totals.
- **Collects invoices.** From mail and files you point it to.
- **Builds a budget.** From your real numbers, in plain words.
- **Hands over a file.** A spreadsheet-ready list for each month that you or your accountant can
  check.

## Where it stops to ask

- **Every payment.** Payments always ask, whatever the bot's settings, and "always allow" has no
  effect on them.
- Sending email, such as a reminder about a late invoice, under the default setting.
- Changes in a connected accounting or payments app that you marked "always asks".

The Expense matcher persona is also told never to submit expense reports or move money. You set
the rest of the rules per bot and per action. See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

An example month:

1. You export the card transactions as a CSV file and send it to the bot with a folder of receipts.
2. The bot matches 61 of 68 transactions and marks four matches as uncertain.
3. It lists the seven with no receipt, with a guess for each: "probably the software subscription
   that renews on the 3rd".
4. You send two missing receipts. It updates the file and hands back the final list.
5. One supplier invoice is overdue. The bot drafts a polite reminder and asks before sending.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. Create a bot with the **Expense matcher** persona for receipts, or the **Budget** persona for
   sorting spending and planning.
2. Give it the data. A CSV export of transactions is enough. You can also connect mail, Google
   Drive or Sheets, Stripe or Zoho Books under Apps.
3. Mark each connected tool read-only, makes changes, or always asks. Read-only is a good start
   for anything that touches money.
4. Add a routine, such as "on the 1st of each month, match last month's receipts and list what is
   missing".

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## What it won't do for you

- It is not an accountant or a licensed adviser. The Budget persona is told to suggest a
  professional for tax and legal questions.
- A match can be wrong. The bot notes its confidence so you know which ones to check.
- It doesn't file returns or sign off the books. A person does that.

## Questions

### Can it pay an invoice?

Only with your approval each time, and only if your workspace owner has set up payments. The bot
never sees the card number. Money transfers and wires are never allowed.

### Does it need access to my bank?

No. An exported file of transactions is enough to start.

### Is my financial data used to train AI?

No. If you want it to stay on your own machine, self-host Casama.

### Does it work with my accounting software?

Stripe and Zoho Books are in the app catalog. Other tools connect through connector services or an
MCP server, where one exists. The bot can also work from exported files.

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# AI coding agents your bot can hand work to

A coding agent is good at code and bad at knowing when to run. A Casama bot can hand a task to Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, on a sandboxed computer, and come back with a summary and the changed files.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-coding-agent

## What the bot does

- **Runs a coding agent for you.** Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi or T3 Code.
- **Chooses where.** On the bot's sandboxed computer, on your own machine through the desktop app, or in Cursor's cloud.
- **Reports.** A summary, the files that changed and, for cloud agents, a pull request link.
- **Starts on triggers.** A new issue, a failing build, a schedule.
- **Keeps your machine safe.** On the bot's computer, the agent can't touch your files.

## Where it stops to ask

- Opening a pull request.
- High-risk actions on your own computer, always.
- Deleting anything outside its workspace folder.

You set these rules per bot and per action. See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

1. You, from your phone: "Use Claude Code to fix the failing tests in the billing package."
2. The bot starts the agent on its computer with the repository checked out.
3. Ten minutes later: "Fixed 3 tests. Changed 2 files. Here's the diff."
4. You ask it to open a pull request. It asks first, then does.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. For the bot's computer: add the coding agent's API key as a named secret.
2. For your own computer: install the agent's command-line tool, sign in, and share the project folder in the desktop app.
3. Ask the bot in plain words which agent to use and where. The **Coder** persona brings a code-change skill.

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## Questions

### Which coding agents work?

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi and T3 Code on your own computer; Claude Code, Codex and Cursor on the bot's computer; Cursor in the cloud.

### Does Casama replace my coding agent?

No. It runs the one you choose, on a schedule or from your phone, with approvals around it.

### Can I use it with MCP?

Yes. Casama has an MCP server, so a coding assistant can also hand work to your bots.

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# An AI customer support agent that asks before refunds

A support bot is only safe if it knows what it may not promise. A Casama bot answers from your help documents, looks up orders, and stops for you before any refund.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-customer-support

## What the bot does

- **Answers from your docs.** It uses the knowledge you give it, not guesses.
- **Works where customers write.** Email, WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger, SMS, Slack, Teams, Discord.
- **Looks things up.** Orders, bookings and accounts, through the apps you connect.
- **Hands over.** When it isn't sure, it asks a person in your team and learns the answer.
- **Reports.** How many it answered, what it escalated, and what the docs didn't cover.

## Where it stops to ask

- Refunds and credits.
- Anything that changes a customer's account, if you mark that tool "always asks".
- Replies outside what your documents cover, if you set it to draft only.

You set these rules per bot and per action. See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

1. A customer writes on WhatsApp at 02:10 asking where their order is.
2. The bot looks up the order, sees it shipped, and replies with the tracking link.
3. Another asks for a refund. The bot answers that it has passed the request on, and an approval appears on your phone.
4. In the morning: 23 answered, 1 refund waiting, 2 questions the docs didn't cover.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. Create a bot with the **Support** persona.
2. Add your help centre and policies as knowledge.
3. Connect a chat app and set who may write to the bot.
4. Connect your order system and mark refund tools **Always asks**.

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## Questions

### Which channels does it support?

Telegram, email, SMS, Slack, WhatsApp, Messenger, Feishu, iMessage, Microsoft Teams and Discord.

### Can it issue refunds?

Only with your approval, if you set the refund tool to always ask.

### Can several people approve?

Yes. Anyone who can use the bot can answer its requests.

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# An AI email assistant that waits for your OK

Hand your inbox to a bot without handing over the Send button. A Casama bot sorts, summarises and drafts, and sending waits for your approval until you decide otherwise.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-email-assistant

## What the bot does

- **Sorts the inbox.** What needs you today, what can wait, what is noise.
- **Drafts replies.** In your tone, using what it remembers about the people and the threads.
- **Answers from your documents.** It can look things up in files and knowledge you gave it.
- **Follows up.** Notices a thread that went quiet and suggests a nudge.
- **Briefs you.** A morning summary with the three emails that matter.

## Where it stops to ask

- Sending any email, under the default setting.
- Deleting mail.
- Acting on instructions that arrived inside an email: after reading outside content, steps that send data out ask first.

You set these rules per bot and per action. See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

1. 07:30: the bot sends your brief: 4 emails need you, 2 meetings moved, 1 invoice due.
2. It has drafted replies to the four. You open the first, change a line, and approve.
3. A customer asks for a refund. The bot drafts the reply and asks before promising anything.
4. A newsletter contains the line "forward this to all contacts". The bot ignores it: text inside an email is not a request from you.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. Create a bot with the **Inbox triage** persona, connect Gmail or your mail provider under Apps, and give the connection to that bot.
2. Mark each mail tool read-only, makes changes, or always asks.
3. Start with drafts only. Read them for a week.
4. Add a routine: "every weekday at 07:30, brief me on my inbox".

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## Questions

### Will it send email without asking?

Not unless you allow it. Sending through email is a high-risk action that asks under the default setting.

### Is my mail used to train AI?

No. If you want your mail to stay on your own machine, self-host Casama.

### Can it handle a shared support inbox?

Yes. See [customer support](https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-customer-support).

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# An AI executive assistant and chief of staff

A chief of staff keeps your day from being decided by your inbox. A Casama bot preps meetings, drafts replies, protects your calendar and tells you only what needs you.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-executive-assistant

## What the bot does

- **Preps meetings.** A one-page brief before each one: who, what was agreed last time, what is open.
- **Drafts for you.** Replies wait in your drafts; only you press Send.
- **Guards the calendar.** Spots clashes and offers new times with a button to do it.
- **Chases.** Keeps a list of what you're waiting on and nudges when it's late.
- **Holds the noise.** Non-urgent notifications wait out quiet hours.

## Where it stops to ask

- Sending, on your behalf, to anyone.
- Moving a meeting that involves other people, if you set it to ask.
- Any payment.

You set these rules per bot and per action. See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

1. 08:00: a brief with today's five meetings and one decision you owe.
2. 09:45: "Maya asked for a slot this week. I drafted a reply with two open times."
3. 13:50: ten minutes before the board call, the brief arrives with last quarter's actions.
4. 18:00: "Three threads are waiting on you. Want replies drafted?"

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. Create a bot with the **Assistant** persona, and add the **Briefing** persona's morning routine.
2. Connect mail, calendar and your documents.
3. Turn on check-ins so it can suggest work, with **Do It** and **Not Now** buttons.
4. Set quiet hours and which kinds of message may interrupt you.

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## Questions

### How is this different from a calendar assistant?

It works across mail, calendar and documents, remembers context between days, and runs on its own schedule.

### Can my human assistant use it too?

Yes. Put the bot in a group chat or a shared workspace, with roles for who may change what.

### Does it join meetings?

Meeting notes can come from the note-taking tools you already use; see the docs on meeting notes.

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# An AI meeting assistant for the work before and after the call

The meeting itself is the short part. The prep before it and the follow-up after it are where things get dropped. A Casama bot does both from your calendar and the notes your meeting app already takes. It doesn't join your calls.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-meeting-assistant

## What the bot does

- **Preps you.** A short note before a meeting, using the event's title, guests and description,
  and what it remembers about the people.
- **Files the notes.** For each meeting, a three-line summary, the decisions, and the action items
  with owners and dates.
- **Keeps them findable.** One file per meeting in a shared team folder.
- **Drafts the follow-up.** An email with the decisions and who does what.
- **Chases.** A routine can list the action items that are still open.

## What it doesn't do

Casama has no meeting bot that joins calls and records them. For the notes themselves, the bot
reads from a notes app you connect, such as Fireflies, Granola, Otter or Fathom. With no notes
app, it works from your calendar events and from notes you send it.

## Where it stops to ask

- Sending anything to anyone. The meeting notes routine asks before it sends, and sending email
  or chat messages asks under the default setting.
- Changes in a connected app that you marked "always asks".

Creating or changing calendar events doesn't ask by default. You can set it to. See
[how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

An example day:

1. 09:45: a brief arrives 15 minutes before a customer call. It has the guest list, the last
   thread with them and two open questions.
2. The call happens. Your notes app records it. The bot is not in the room.
3. 18:00: the meeting notes routine runs. The bot gathers the day's notes and writes a summary,
   decisions and action items for each meeting.
4. It saves one file per meeting and links them in its reply.
5. It drafts a follow-up to the customer and asks before sending. You change one date and approve.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. Connect Google Calendar or Outlook to one bot.
2. Add a **Meetings** routine for prep. Choose 30, 15 or 5 minutes before, and narrow it if you
   like: only meetings with people outside your company, only meetings with a video link, or only
   certain titles.
3. Connect your notes app under Integrations, if you use one, and give it to the same bot.
4. Add the **Meeting notes** routine idea. It runs each weekday at 18:00 unless you change the
   time.

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## Limits worth knowing

- In the app, a meeting routine counts from the meeting's start, up to 15 minutes after. Running
  a set time after a meeting ends is possible through the API only.
- Casama checks the calendar every 5 minutes, so a meeting added minutes before it starts may not
  be picked up in time.
- The notes-app connections follow each vendor's public documentation and haven't all been tried
  with real accounts.
- A summary is only as good as the notes it reads. Check action items and dates before you send
  them on.

## Questions

### Does the bot join my calls?

No. It works from your calendar and from the notes your meeting app takes.

### Does it record audio?

No. Recording and transcription are your notes app's job. Tell the people in the call what that
app records, as you would without Casama.

### What if I don't use a notes app?

The bot can still prepare you from the calendar, and write up notes you send it after the call.

### Will it email everyone the notes?

Only after you approve. The routine asks before it sends anything to anyone.

### Can the whole team see the notes?

The routine saves one file per meeting in the team folder, `shared/meetings/`, and links them in
its reply.

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# An AI personal assistant that does the task

Most AI assistants tell you how to do something. A Casama bot does it on a computer of its own, remembers how you like things, and asks before paying for anything.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-personal-assistant

## What the bot does

- **Books and reserves.** Tables, trips, tickets and appointments, in its own browser, on the real sites.
- **Compares.** Prices, options and reviews across several sites, returned as a short table with links.
- **Fills in forms.** Renewals, sign-ups and returns, with your details filled in from what it remembers.
- **Keeps track.** Reminders, renewals and a morning brief of what today needs.
- **Watches.** A price, a page or a delivery, and tells you when it changes.

## Where it stops to ask

- Paying for anything, always.
- Sending a message or an email in your name.
- Anything you marked "always ask".

You set these rules per bot and per action. See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

1. You: "Find a table for four near the office on Friday at 7, Italian, not too loud."
2. The bot searches the booking sites, checks reviews for noise, and returns three options.
3. You: "The second one."
4. It fills in the booking and stops: "Reserve Trattoria Nove, Friday 19:00, 4 people. Approve?"
5. You approve from your phone's lock screen. It confirms and adds it to your calendar.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. Create a bot with the **Assistant** persona (or **Travel**, for trips), or describe the bot you want in the welcome chat.
2. Connect your calendar and mail so it knows your day.
3. Tell it your preferences once: airline, seat, diet, budget. It saves them to memory, which you can read and edit.
4. Leave autonomy on **Ask for risky actions** until you trust it.

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## Questions

### Can it use my accounts?

It works in its own browser. Logins from 1Password or Bitwarden are filled in for the sites you allow, and the AI model never sees them.

### What does it cost?

The Free plan includes $1 of credits a month. A typical booking task costs a few cents of model usage.

### Can I reach it without the app?

Yes: Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage, SMS, email and other chat apps can be connected to a bot.

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/), or compare the [best AI personal assistants](https://casama.ai/compare/best-ai-personal-assistants).

# An AI recruiting assistant that screens to a scorecard and leaves the decision to you

Reading every application properly takes hours, and tired readers are inconsistent. A Casama bot scores each applicant against the same written scorecard and shows the evidence. It recommends. A person decides.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-recruiting-assistant

## What the bot does

- **Writes a scorecard with you.** Must-haves, nice-to-haves and deal-breakers for the role. It
  asks for one if it is missing.
- **Scores each applicant.** One line of evidence per criterion, quoted from what they sent.
- **Recommends.** Advance, hold or decline, with the reason.
- **Builds a shortlist.** The same format for everyone, so you can compare.
- **Drafts the messages.** A kind, specific note for each person, and interview invites for the
  shortlist.
- **Helps with next steps.** With your calendar connected, it can propose interview times.

## Where it stops to ask

- **Every decision.** The Recruiting screener persona is told that a person makes every final
  decision and that it never rejects anyone directly.
- Sending any email, under the default setting.
- Changes in a connected app that you marked "always asks".

You set these rules per bot and per action. See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it ignores on purpose

The Recruiting screener persona is told to ignore, and never infer, age, gender, ethnicity,
religion, disability, family status and other protected traits, and not to use photos or names as
signals. Instructions are not a guarantee. Read the evidence lines, sample the "decline" pile
yourself, and check the rules on automated screening where you hire.

## What it looks like

An example, for a made-up role:

1. You: "Screen today's applicants for the support lead role." You attach the scorecard and
   twelve applications.
2. The bot scores each one. For "has led a team", it quotes the line from the CV, or writes "no
   evidence found".
3. It recommends four to advance, three to hold and five to decline, and marks two it is unsure
   about.
4. You move one from "decline" to "hold" and tell it why. It remembers the correction.
5. It drafts interview invites for the shortlist. You read them and approve each send.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. Create a bot with the **Recruiting screener** persona.
2. Write the scorecard for one role, or ask the bot to draft one and edit it.
3. Give it the applications: send the files in chat, or connect the mailbox or folder where they
   arrive. Mark connected tools read-only to begin with.
4. Make the bot private to the people who hire, so applicants' details aren't open to the whole
   workspace.
5. Compare its first batch with your own reading before you rely on it.

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## What it won't do for you

- It doesn't interview anyone, and it doesn't judge character.
- It can miss something a careful reader would catch, or misread an unusual CV.
- Casama's app catalog has no applicant tracking system of its own today. Applications come in as
  files, by mail, or through a connector service.

## Questions

### Does the bot reject candidates?

No. It recommends and drafts. A person decides, and sending asks for approval by default.

### Is it fair?

It applies one scorecard to everyone and shows its evidence, which makes its reasoning checkable.
That is not the same as being free of bias. Keep a person reviewing the outcomes.

### Where is applicant data kept?

In your workspace and on the bot's computer. It is not used to train models. If you want it on
your own machine, self-host Casama.

### Can it schedule the interviews?

It can propose times and draft the invite. See [AI scheduling assistant](https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-scheduling-assistant).

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# An AI research assistant that cites every source

Research is many small steps: search, open, read, compare, write. A Casama bot does them on its own computer and hands you a brief with every claim tied to a source.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-research-assistant

## What the bot does

- **Reads widely.** Web pages, PDFs and your own Drive or Notion files.
- **Compares.** Builds a table across sources: prices, features, dates, positions.
- **Cites.** Each finding carries the page or file and the place in it.
- **Repeats.** A daily or weekly brief on the topics you follow.
- **Watches a page.** And tells you when it changes.

## Where it stops to ask

- Paid data lookups, which show their price first.
- Sending the result to anyone but you.

You set these rules per bot and per action. See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

1. You: "Compare the five biggest e-bike subscriptions in Germany: price, minimum term, theft cover."
2. The bot opens each provider's site, reads the terms, and builds the table.
3. It notes two it couldn't verify and says why.
4. You: "Check this every Monday and tell me what changed." It becomes a routine.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. Create a bot with the **Researcher** persona, which brings a research-report skill.
2. Connect the document stores it should read.
3. Tell it how you like results: length, format, how to cite.
4. Add a routine for anything you want regularly.

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## Questions

### Does it make things up?

Any AI model can. Sources on every claim let you check, and the run timeline shows which pages it opened.

### Can it read files I upload?

Yes, and knowledge you add stays available to that bot.

### What does a long research task cost?

It depends on how many steps it takes. Each bot has a per-run budget, $1 by default, and stops there.

# An AI sales assistant that researches first and never sends for you

Good outreach starts with reading, and reading takes time. A Casama bot looks up each lead, cites what it found and drafts a short, specific message. You decide what gets sent.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-sales-assistant

## What the bot does

- **Researches a lead.** What the company does, recent news, likely priorities and the person's
  role, with links.
- **Builds a prospect list.** Companies that look like your best customers, each with the signal
  that makes them a fit and where it was found.
- **Drafts outreach.** A short first message that refers to something specific, plus follow-ups.
- **Keeps a pipeline.** A simple file on its computer: company, person, stage, next step, date.
- **Remembers.** Your ideal customer, your tone and what you corrected last time.

## Where it stops to ask

- Sending anything. The Sales and Outbound prospector personas are told never to send messages
  themselves, and sending email or chat messages asks for approval under the default setting
  anyway.
- Paid data lookups, such as finding an email address. The approval shows the price first.
- Changes in a connected app that you marked "always asks".

You set these rules per bot and per action. See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

An example, with made-up companies:

1. You: "Find 20 companies like our best customer, a 40-person logistics firm in the Netherlands."
2. The bot asks two questions about size and the role to contact, then searches public sources on
   its own computer.
3. It returns a list of 20 with a source link and a fit score for each, and says which three it
   is least sure about.
4. You pick five. It drafts a first message under 100 words for each, and one follow-up.
5. You edit two lines and send them yourself, or approve the bot's request to send.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. Create a bot with the **Sales** persona for researching named leads, or **Outbound prospector**
   for building lists. Edit the instructions to describe your ideal customer.
2. Connect your CRM and mail under Apps, if you want the bot to read them. HubSpot and Zoho CRM
   are in the catalog. Mark each tool read-only, makes changes, or always asks.
3. Start with research and drafts only. Read them for a week and correct what is off.
4. Add a routine, such as "every Monday at 9:00, list the leads that went quiet and draft a
   follow-up for each".

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## What it won't do for you

- It can be wrong about a company. Check the links before you repeat a claim to a prospect.
- It doesn't replace the conversation. It prepares it.
- The Outbound prospector persona is told to respect opt-outs and local rules on cold outreach,
  and not to collect personal emails from behind logins. The rules where you sell are still yours
  to know.

## Questions

### Will it email prospects on its own?

Not unless you change that on purpose. The personas hand drafts to you, and sending asks for
approval by default.

### Does it work with my CRM?

HubSpot and Zoho CRM are in the app catalog. Other tools connect through connector services or an
MCP server, where one exists.

### Where does the lead data come from?

Public web pages the bot reads on its own computer, apps you connected, and paid data lookups you
approved. It lists its sources.

### Can a team share it?

Yes, in a shared workspace. See [AI agents for small business](https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-agents-for-small-business).

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/).

# An AI social media assistant that drafts the week and waits for your OK

The hard part of social media is turning up every week with something worth reading. A Casama bot plans the calendar and drafts each post in your voice. Posting stays with you until you decide otherwise.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-social-media-assistant

## What the bot does

- **Plans the week.** What to post, where, when, and which of your themes it fits.
- **Drafts per channel.** Length and format to suit each one, with an image idea.
- **Writes variants.** Two or three versions of a post or headline to test.
- **Keeps your voice.** It holds your brand voice, audience and themes in memory, where you can
  read and edit them.
- **Suggests replies.** Ideas for answering comments, for you to use or ignore.
- **Plans campaigns.** A launch plan with a way to measure each idea.

## Where it stops to ask

The Social persona is told never to post or reply publicly itself. It queues drafts for approval.
To make that a hard rule that doesn't depend on instructions:

- Add an action rule for **Publishing** set to **Ask me first**, or to **Hand it to me to finish**
  if you want to press the button yourself.
- If you connect a posting tool, mark it **Always asks**.
- Sending email or chat messages already asks under the default setting.

See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

An example week:

1. Monday 09:00: the weekly content plan routine runs. The bot drafts five posts with a day,
   a channel, the copy and an image idea for each.
2. You open the plan on your phone, rewrite one opening line and drop one post.
3. You tell it: "Less formal. No exclamation marks." It saves that and uses it next week.
4. On Wednesday you ask for three versions of the launch post. You pick the second.
5. You post them yourself, or approve each one when the bot asks.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

## Set it up

1. Create a bot with the **Social** persona. It comes with a weekly content plan routine on Monday
   mornings. For campaigns, ads and landing pages, use the **Marketer** persona.
2. Tell it your voice, your audience and three or four themes. Paste in a few posts you liked.
3. Add the Publishing rule above before you connect any account that can post.
4. Read the first two weeks of drafts closely and correct them. The corrections stay in memory.

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## What it won't do for you

- It doesn't know what happened in your business this week unless you tell it or connect a source.
- A draft can state something untrue. The Marketer persona is told never to make claims the
  product can't back up, and you should still read every post.
- Casama's app catalog has no social networks of its own today. Posting goes through a connector
  service, the bot's browser with you signed in, or your own hands.

## Questions

### Will it post without asking?

Not with the setup above. The persona queues drafts, and a Publishing rule set to "Ask me first"
wins even if the bot is otherwise allowed to act on its own.

### Can it make the images?

A bot can generate images. That uses credits, and by default it doesn't ask first, so set a budget.

### Can it reply to comments for me?

It can draft replies. The Social persona doesn't reply publicly itself.

### Can more than one person review the drafts?

Yes. In a shared workspace, anyone who can use the bot can answer its approval requests.

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/

# An AI travel planner that builds the trip and asks before paying

Planning a trip means twenty browser tabs and a spreadsheet. A Casama bot opens the tabs on its own computer and hands you a day-by-day plan with links. Booking and paying stay under your control.

Updated 2026-11-18. Page: https://casama.ai/use-cases/ai-travel-planner

## What the bot does

- **Asks first.** Dates, budget, pace, interests and who is travelling.
- **Builds the itinerary.** Day by day, with realistic travel times, a few options per day and
  rough costs.
- **Links to official sites.** For opening hours, tickets and entry requirements, and says what to
  double-check.
- **Lists what to book and when.** In the order that matters, such as the train before the museum
  slot.
- **Makes the packing list.** For the place, the season and the people.
- **Remembers.** That you want an aisle seat, a late start and no more than one museum a day.

## Where it stops to ask

- **Booking.** The built-in Travel persona is told never to book or pay for anything. It lists
  what to book, and you book it.
- **Paying.** If you change the instructions so the bot may fill in a booking form in its own
  browser, every payment still asks first, whatever its settings.
- **Signing in.** At a password or a two-step code, the bot asks you to take over its screen. You
  sign in yourself, and nothing you type reaches the bot.
- Sending email, such as a question to a hotel, under the default setting.

You set these rules per bot and per action. See [how approvals work](https://casama.ai/security).

## What it looks like

An example trip:

1. You: "Plan five relaxed days in Lisbon in May for two. Mid-range budget. We like food and
   walking."
2. The bot asks about your arrival time and whether you want a day trip.
3. It reads official sites and returns five days, each with a morning, an afternoon and two dinner
   options, with walking times between them.
4. It lists four things to book now and two that can wait, with links.
5. You ask it to swap day two and day four because of a closing day it flagged. It updates the
   plan.

## Why its own computer matters

Each Casama bot works on a sandboxed Linux machine of its own, with a browser, files and a shell.
It keeps going when you close your laptop, it can't reach your own files, and you can watch its
screen or take over at any time. Before a command that deletes data, its computer is saved, so the
work can be undone.

For travel this matters in one more way. The bot's browser keeps its sign-ins, so once you have
signed in to a booking site on its computer, it stays signed in there and not on your laptop.

## Set it up

1. Create a bot with the **Travel** persona.
2. Tell it how you travel: budget, pace, seats, food, what you never want.
3. Ask for a trip. Read the plan and check the things it says to double-check.
4. If you want it to prepare bookings, edit its instructions to allow filling in forms, and add
   an action rule for **Payments** set to **Hand it to me to finish** if you would rather type
   the card yourself.

Ready-made skills, starter bots and routines are in the [gallery](https://gallery.casama.ai).

## What it won't do for you

- Prices and opening hours change. The bot links to the source so you can check on the day.
- It can get a travel time or an entry rule wrong. Confirm visas and entry requirements with the
  official site.
- Paying through Casama needs the workspace owner to set up payments first. Without that, the bot
  prepares the booking and you pay.

## Questions

### Can it book flights and hotels?

Not with the built-in persona, which only plans. With changed instructions a bot can fill in a
booking form in its own browser. Paying always asks, and you can take over the screen to finish
yourself.

### Does the bot see my card number?

No. When payments are set up, each approved purchase gets a single-use virtual card, and the bot
handles placeholders, not card details.

### Can it tell me when to leave for the airport?

A routine can run when it is time to leave for your next calendar event that has a location. It
needs your places set up, a connected calendar and a maps key on the server.

### Can it plan for a group?

Yes. Tell it who is travelling and what each person needs.

See [what else Casama bots do](https://casama.ai/use-cases/).

Join the waitlist at https://casama.ai/waitlist (Casama Cloud is invite-only for now), or run it on your own server: https://docs.casama.ai/self-hosting/
